items.title: Spin Migration in the Argon Dimer
items.summary: We introduce the concept of \emph{spin migration}, i.e. time-dependent spin density, and the absolute smallest example of molecular spintronics. We illustrate the concept by \emph{ab initio} calculations of the coupled vibronic motion of the electrons and the nuclei in the argon dimer cation, in which the vibrational level spacing is similar to the spin--orbit splitting of the atomic argon cations. We find that the spin density varies on multiple time scales, given by the natural time scales of the electronic and nuclear wavepackets.

items.title: Accuracy of Vibrational Properties of Machine-Learning Force Fields for Molecular Crystal Transformations
items.summary: Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) enable the calculation of transformation pathways in molecular crystals at a fraction of the computational cost of density functional theory (DFT). However, a good agreement in energies and structures does not necessarily imply an accurate description of vibrational properties, which are essential for characterizing transition states and determining free energies at finite temperatures. Herein, we assess the accuracy of system-specific SO3krates MLFFs trained on PBE+MBD reference data for describing vibrational properties of molecular crystal transformations. As examples, we consider a polymorph transition of 1,4-diiodobenzene and a single-crystal-to-single-crystal Diels-Alder reaction. The transition state structures obtained from solid-state nudged-elastic-band (NEB) calculations with the MLFFs exhibit a single imaginary $Γ$-point frequency associated with the respective transformation. Compared with PBE+MBD, the mean absolute errors of $Γ$-point vibrational frequencies and relative harmonic free energies at 300 K are about 3 cm$^{-1}$ and 1 kJ/mol, respectively. Furthermore, we compare for the Diels-Alder reaction a collective transformation pathway with a sequential one, in which individual diene-dienophile pairs react successively, and demonstrate that PBE0+MBD single-point corrections can significantly affect the predicted reaction energetics. These results demonstrate that system-specific MLFFs can reproduce not only the energies and forces but also the local curvature of the potential-energy surface with high accuracy, enabling reliable calculations of harmonic vibrational free energies, providing a basis for extending the studies of molecular crystal transformations to larger supercells.

items.title: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
items.summary: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. Regarding the sphere as the homogeneous space $S^2 \cong \text{SO(3)}/\text{SO(2)}$, we lift a spin $s$ field to the rotation group, convolve on $\text{SO(3)}$, and project back to the sphere through the adjoint of the lift for a potentially different spin $s'$. We recover every rotation-equivariant convolution considered previously through constraints on the kernel, spin choices and inclusion or omission of the lift and projection. For maps between fields of fixed input and output spin, we prove that directional kernels, output on the sphere and equivariance cannot be achieved simultaneously. We make explicit that spin fields are sections of associated line bundles, linking the physics and bundle literatures, and express the spin rotation phase as the character of the twist of the section. We present harmonic-space algorithms for the exact and efficient computation of lifted spherical convolutions of band-limited fields by appealing to sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group. All operators are implemented in the open-source s2conv code, and numerical experiments confirm the reductions and the equivariance of the operators to machine precision. Finally, we illustrate the operators on fields measured on the Earth and on the celestial sky.

items.title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
items.summary: Foundation models have recently gained significant attention in fields such as high energy physics (HEP). The tokenizers that convert detector data into discrete inputs for such models, however, are comparatively unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by learning discrete and compressed tokenized representations of HEP datasets. We demonstrate the approach on four modalities covering two different simulated detectors that vary in complexity. Treating tokenization as a rate-distortion problem, a systematic hyperparameter scan yields four design rules for tokenizing HEP data that hold across all set-based modalities studied. The cost of tokenization is evaluated on tasks including jet $p_T$ regression, particle flow reconstruction, and flavor tagging. We find that tokenization preserves much of the information needed for these tasks at compression factors of approximately 4-11$\times$ while keeping the jet $p_T$ resolution below 1%. We also present heptokens, an open-source library for tokenizing HEP data.

items.title: Statistical Optical Replication and Mixing of Spatial Information across Wavelengths
items.summary: Accessing and combining the spatial information carried by light at different wavelengths is important for linking structured-light encoding with spectrally distinct detection channels. Here, we introduce a correlation-enabled linear-optical framework for cross-wavelength imaging, bidirectional replication, and spatial information mixing. Shared random holographic modulation establishes correlations between nondegenerate optical fields, allowing spatial information to be retrieved from joint intensity fluctuations. In the demonstrated replicator, a spatial pattern encoded at one wavelength is read out in the detection coordinates of another through intensity correlations. Selecting diffraction-order pairs produces correlation kernels containing either the product or the conjugate product of two input field envelopes. These operations reproduce the spatial algebra underlying sum- and difference-frequency generation, while the optical fields retain their original carrier frequencies. The theory accounts for wavelength-dependent propagation and coordinate scaling, linking the input structures to observable correlation patterns. Together, these results establish a common framework for cross-wavelength spatial information processing through engineered optical correlations and joint detection.

items.title: Modelling the complex dynamics of online disinformation cascades
items.summary: Disinformation on online social media has been on the rise in the past years. While there is extensive literature modelling social cascades, online disinformation cascades show distinctive characteristics: they provoke debunking reactions, they spread over networks with heterogeneous connectivity, and they compete for the limited attention of users --- which recommendation algorithms may partly offset. We propose a model including these ingredients and study it through Monte--Carlo simulations and mean--field approximations, on random graphs and an empirical Twitter network. We find that debunking reactions are double--edged: they reduce the reach of appealing items but allow unappealing ones to reach audiences they would not otherwise reach. Degree heterogeneity makes cascades trigger at a much lower content appeal but limits their final reach: heterogeneous networks are easy to ignite yet hard to saturate. Limited attention cancels the effects from degree heterogeneity, although the mediation of recommendation algorithms may restore them.

items.title: Systemic risk in interbank networks: disentangling balance sheets and network effects
items.summary: We study how the level of systemic risk empirically observed in an interbank network differs from the expected risk implied by the balance sheets composition of the participating banks, abstracting from the specific configuration of bilateral exposures. To this end, using different contagion models (i.e., interbank asset valuation functions), we measure observed systemic risk on e-MID network data from 2005 to 2012 and compare it with the expected risk generated by a null model: an ensemble of interbank networks whose links represent possible market clearing configurations. This counterfactual is obtained through a maximum-entropy approach that preserves banks' balance sheet variables and diversification patterns, while randomizing the configuration of exposures. We find that the aggregate levels of observed and expected systemic risks are generally consistent but diverge significantly during turbulent periods - specifically following the default of Lehman Brothers (2009) and the VLTRO implementation by the ECB (2012). At the individual level, however, banks often appear more or less risky than implied by their balance sheet alone, due to their position in the network. Our results show, on the one hand, that balance sheet information embedded in a suitable maximum-entropy framework provides reliable estimates of aggregate systemic risk; on the other hand, they highlight the importance of detailed network information for accurate stress testing of individual banks, particularly after systemic events.

items.title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
items.summary: Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.

items.title: Physical-state supervision for design-only Gaussian process surrogates of implosion simulations
items.summary: Physical diagnostics recorded during simulation can organize a sharply varying response, but using them as surrogate inputs normally requires another calculation at prediction. We construct a physical-state-supervised Gaussian process surrogate that learns these diagnostics from design variables. Cross-fitted state estimates augment a retained design representation; a global Gaussian process and an optional soft mixture of response-band experts use identical inputs. On a database of 1,987 paired one-dimensional implosions, learned burn-weighted states from calculations without alpha-particle heating reduce mean squared log-response error by 60.25% and 52.98% for the global predictor on random holdout and design-space extrapolation. Random-projection and shuffled-state supervision do not reproduce these gains. For CH, matched-input comparisons show that experts help at smaller training budgets but contribute little at 1,000 designs with this representation. A thermal-feedback benchmark validates the complete learned-state procedure, while 3,000 newly calculated Be/Cocktail designs expose weaker extrapolation gains and cases where experts degrade accuracy. A conditional state-error bound separates encoding sensitivity from routing effects. An open Python implementation reproduces the archived predictions and is released with the data, per-design results, and measured costs. Physical-state supervision is thus a useful representation for finite-data surrogates, whereas expert specialization should be selected by validation.

items.title: Warm-IP: A Path-Following ADMM Warm Start for Interior-Point Quadratic Programming
items.summary: Interior-point (IP) methods are powerful second-order optimization algorithms but can make slow progress during early iterations. We propose Warm-IP, a hybrid framework that combines a path-following variant of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a primal--dual IP method. The ADMM phase generates a warm start that remains close to the central path, enabling the subsequent IP phase to rapidly refine the solution to high accuracy. We evaluate Warm-IP on a diverse collection of real-world and synthetic quadratic programming (QP) instances and compare it with leading commercial solvers (MOSEK and Gurobi) and open-source solvers (Clarabel, PIQP, and OSQP). We also curate and release a new benchmark of large-scale QPs from cancer radiotherapy treatment planning, built from real patient data and provided in canonical QP form, with instances containing hundreds of thousands of constraints. Warm-IP substantially outperforms existing solvers on large-scale problems. On the large-scale radiotherapy benchmark comprising 60 lung cancer cases, for example, Warm-IP solves an instance in 47 seconds on average with no failures, while the strongest competitors, MOSEK and Gurobi, average 55 seconds with failures on 23\% of the cases and roughly 240 seconds with no failures, respectively. To support reproducibility and future benchmarking, we publicly release the implementation and benchmark data through a \href{https://github.com/Radiotherapy-Optimization/Warm-IP}{GitHub repository}. These results demonstrate that appropriately warm-started IP methods can combine the rapid initial progress of first-order methods with the high-accuracy convergence of second-order methods.

items.title: Particle dynamics in a microfluidic T-junction vortex flow: the role of history force
items.summary: The motion of inertial particles suspended in a carrier fluid, together with the dynamics of the underlying vortical structures, is investigated in a square microfluidic T-junction. The coherent structures forming near the branching strongly affect the particle distribution and may promote particle trapping around the T-region. Single-phase numerical simulations of the unperturbed base flow are combined with integration of the particle force balance equation, which, unlike most previous studies, includes the Basset-Boussinesq (BB) history force. The flow topology is analysed for $Re=500$ and $570$, while particle properties are varied through the Stokes number $St$ and the particle-to-fluid density ratio $ρ$. At $Re=500$ the base flow exhibits a steady vortex pair, whereas at $Re=570$ a Hopf bifurcation gives rise to a helical oscillation of the primary vortex pair characterized by periodic breathing. The BB history force has a non-negligible impact over the whole range of $(ρ, St)$ pairs investigated. It acts as an additional viscous force which, together with the drag of the relative motion, opposes the pressure-gradient force, widening particle spiral trajectories radially and elongating them axially. Its inclusion reduces the basin of attraction, indicating that memory effects promote particle displacement away from the vortex core and weaken trapping. At $Re=570$, spectral proper orthogonal decomposition characterizes the breathing of the primary vortex pair. Particles injected at a given location interact with the vortical structure at different phases of the cycle depending on the injection time, producing substantially different trajectories. This phase dependence is reflected in the shape and extent of the basin of attraction, quantified through the trapping probability over the inlet section and the probability density functions of the force components.

items.title: Geometric theory of elastic curves constrained on rigid curved surfaces
items.summary: Slender elastic objects constrained to curved surfaces are ubiquitous in soft systems, with examples ranging from DNA wrapping around histones to actin filaments forming contractile rings on the cell membrane during cytokinesis. In the continuum limit, the conformation of these effectively one-dimensional (1D) objects is governed by both the geometry and mechanics of the embedding surface, and the elasticity of the object. Existing phenomenological typically describe such behavior through elastic energy minimization that incorporates bending and twisting, but neglect stretching that may be important for filaments with finite cross-section or are highly incompatible with the underlying surface. Here we present a coarse-grained geometric theory of 1D elastic curves constrained on rigid surfaces, derived from the first principles. For an isotropic material, our model emerges naturally in terms of the Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and area moments of inertia. The resulting effective energy functional explicitly includes stretching in addition to bending and twisting. We minimize it to determine the equilibrium curve conformations on different zero, positive, or negative Gaussian rigid surfaces. Our theory provides a general framework for analyzing the equilibrium configurations of surface-bound elastic curves in biologically and physically relevant settings.

items.title: PhySeqNet: physics-informed fluorescent foci detection for BARseq spatial transcriptomics
items.summary: BARseq enables spatially resolved gene-expression profiling across intact tissue, but its sensitivity depends on accurate detection and decoding of dense fluorescent rolonies. Existing spot-calling approaches can be conservative where signals overlap, while supervised deep learning is limited by the lack of reliable manual ground truth in real tissue images. Here we present PhySeqNet, a physics-informed deep learning framework for annotation-free fluorescent foci detection in BARseq. PhySeqNet trains U-Net detectors entirely on semi-synthetic images generated from an instrument-matched optical model combined with real sample-free experimental noise, and is integrated into pyBARseq, a modular Python pipeline for BARseq analysis. PhySeqNet achieved high detection performance on held-out simulated data across wavelength bands. On real tissue images, where ground truth is unavailable, we evaluated detections by forward-model reconstruction: PhySeqNet with conservative barcode-aware non-maxima suppression (NMSB) achieved higher reconstruction fidelity (NCC and MS-SSIM) than the BarDensr single-shot estimator, tuned classical spot detectors, and a pretrained deep-learning detector. In the analyzed brain section, PhySeqNet with NMSB yielded a median of 51 counts per cell versus 47 for BarDensr, with a similar number of genes detected per cell. The recovered transcripts produced spatial expression patterns qualitatively consistent with Allen MERFISH reference data and preserved cell-type composition after scANVI label transfer. These results show that physics-informed simulation can train practical, annotation-free detectors that improve BARseq sensitivity without disrupting downstream biological interpretation.

items.title: Physics of stabilization and dynamic control of CW magnetrons for superconducting accelerators
items.summary: Powerful CW magnetrons were suggested for feeding RF cavities of superconducting accelerators because they provide higher efficiency and lower RF power cost than the traditionally used klystrons, IOTs, or solid-state amplifiers. RF amplifiers driven by a master oscillator serve as coherent RF sources. CW magnetrons are regenerative RF self-oscillators with a huge regenerative gain. This causes regenerative instability with notable noise when a magnetron operates as a self-oscillator, i.e., with the anode voltage above the threshold of self-excitation. An injection locking by a small signal was proposed for phase stabilization of magnetrons. In this case, CW magnetrons with injection-locked (coherent) oscillations generate a notable level of noise. This may preclude the use of CW magnetrons in this mode in superconducting RF (SRF) accelerators. This work discusses our analytical results, PIC simulations, and previously obtained analytical and experimental data regarding the operation and control of CW magnetrons. These results led to the development of methods which are most suitable for SRF accelerators.

items.title: Dynamics of fast magnetosonic wave turbulence
items.summary: Fast magnetosonic waves are among the fundamental oscillation modes of astrophysical plasmas. To study their dynamics, we carry out numerical simulations of the wave turbulence kinetic equation, which describes the evolution of the energy spectrum of a set of weakly nonlinear fast magnetosonic waves. This kinetic equation, which involves three-wave interactions, has recently been derived from compressible magnetohydrodynamics in the low-$β$ limit (Galtier 2023). It has an exact stationary solution, the Kolmogorov-Zakharov spectrum, corresponding to a direct energy cascade. Here we perform free decay simulations of the kinetic equation for which we propose a Kolmogorov-type phenomenology to explain the temporal decay laws of energy and integral length scale. In the forced simulations, we show that the cascade is in fact composed of a mixture of a forward cascade for counter-propagating waves, and a backward cascade for co-propagating waves, with the former being stronger than the latter. The Kolmogorov-Zakharov energy spectrum in $k^{-3/2}$ is found in the radial direction with an anisotropy due to the amplitude that depends on the angle relative to the strong mean magnetic field. We give the analytical expression of the Kolmogorov-Zakharov constant, which is numerically verified in the high Reynolds number limit. Our study provides a theoretical explanation for certain observations in the solar wind plasma (Zhao et al. 2022), where a regime of weak turbulence has been identified for fast magnetosonic waves, alongside a critical balance regime for strong Alfvén wave turbulence.

items.title: Dynamic mixed turbulence modeling using a super-resolution generative adversarial approach
items.summary: A dynamic mixed super-resolution model (DMSRM) for large-eddy simulations (LESs) is proposed, which combines the traditional dynamic mixed model (DMM) formulation with the generation of super-resolved velocity fields from which the subfilter-scale (SFS) stress tensor can be computed. A data-driven super-resolution generative adversarial network (SR-GAN) is employed to upsample the grid-filtered velocity fields by a factor of two, enabling the evaluation of both scale-similarity and the dynamic Smagorinsky contributions. A priori analyses of forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) show that the SR-GAN accurately reconstructs flow features and generalizes well across different filter sizes and higher Reynolds numbers within the same flow configuration, even for unseen input fields. The DMSRM reproduces SFS stresses and energy dissipation more accurately than the traditional DMM. A posteriori LES calculations further confirm that DMSRM predicts the energy spectrum and intermittency more accurately than DMM, even for different LES grid-scale resolutions and higher Reynolds numbers than those used for training within the same forced HIT flow configuration. Unlike DMM, DMSRM yields realistic backscatter and physically consistent SFS energy dissipation. These improvements arise from the physically accurate super-resolved fields generated by the SR-GAN, from which SFS stresses are directly computed. The result is a closure that accurately reproduces stress magnitudes and dissipation while reducing reliance on additional dissipation from the dynamic term. The DMSRM formulation achieves a balance of physical fidelity, robustness, and computational efficiency, offering a promising alternative to traditional DMMs for turbulence LES modeling.

items.title: Shear-driven arrest of dip-coating film entrainment
items.summary: A plate withdrawn from a bath of partially wetting liquid entrains a film above a critical velocity. Here, we show that this critical threshold can be substantially increased by the presence of a laminar gas flow opposed to the plate velocity that exerts a tangential shear stress on the liquid-gas interface. Using two-phase immiscible Navier-Stokes simulations and confining the gas to a narrow channel, we derive a closed-form expression for the interfacial stress, which combined with lubrication theory relates the thickness of the film and the contact line velocity to the applied shear stress. As the gas velocity is increased, the film thins and the contact line velocity slows down, until the imposed shear overcomes the drag of the moving plate and entrainment is arrested. As in the quiescent case, the velocity mismatch between plate and contact line is independent of the plate velocity and is set by the applied shear alone. We find that one set of varying gas flow simulations, with constant critical plate velocity, therefore determines the critical gas flow for every smaller plate velocity.

items.title: Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.summary: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials. These findings open a new avenue for designing nonlinear chiroptical crystals which harness the duality of polarity and chirality and chemical versatility of COFs.

items.title: Bogoliubov-de Gennes spectrum, Cherenkov radiation and recoil of solitons with third-order dispersion underlying optical analogue horizons
items.summary: Third-order dispersion turns the soliton of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, which underlies optical analogues of event horizons in fibers, into a weakly radiating solitary wave. We compute three of its properties without assuming a thermal emission law. First, the linearized (Bogoliubov-de Gennes) problem must be posed about the stationary state of the dispersive equation: linearizing about the integrable profile produces a complex quartet that is converged in grid and box, grows as the square root of the dispersion strength and is spurious. About the stationary state, on a periodic grid, the zero-mode sector consists of two Jordan blocks of size two and the spectrum is real at the operating point, including negative-energy box modes of the resonant branch. Second, we measure the steady Cherenkov emission of adiabatically prepared solitons from the flux of the radiation behind them, over eight decades. The radiation is phase-matched in the frame of the drifting soliton, and the first-order rate falls short of the measured one by factors of 29 to 45. Expressed through a scaled dispersion coefficient of the local soliton, the measured rate describes launched solitons of three amplitudes; with norm and momentum balance, and no further fitted parameter, it reproduces their recoil and the slow decay of their loss rate; at weak dispersion the loss of a launched soliton is the shedding of its launch mismatch. Third, a census of the asymptotic channels shows that long-wavelength upstream emission requires the chemical potential of the soliton, lowered by the comoving-frame Doppler shift of a drifting soliton, to lie inside the analysis band, which bounds the soliton amplitude. In a kinematic model of the flow the surface gravity has a closed form; the thermal relation and the entanglement built on it are imposed inputs of that model. The construction applies to Raman-free Kerr media.

items.title: Efficient simulation of second-order phase transitions in quantum anharmonic materials
items.summary: When a crystal undergoes a second-order structural phase transition, such as in ferroelectrics, Peierls, and charge-density waves, the diverging fluctuations of the order parameter lead to the break- down of the standard phonon quasiparticle picture. Simulating these highly anharmonic regimes is notoriously challenging, as methods such as molecular dynamics suffer from a critical slowdown near the transition point, while the harmonic approximation fails dramatically at saddle points of the energy landscape stabilized by quantum or thermal ionic fluctuations. This work introduces a new approach, based on the variational free-energy principle, to predict critical long-range behavior and dynamical spectra in strongly anharmonic systems, even when quantum ionic fluctuations dominate. The proposed framework builds upon the stochastic self- consistent harmonic approximation but reduces its computational scaling with the number of atoms, N, from O(N^6) to O(N^2) and the memory requirement from O(N^4) to O(N). We benchmark the method on the prototypical lead-free metal-halide perovskite CsSnI3, a promising candidate for photovoltaic engineering, simulating its phase stability and Raman spectrum near the phase transition, where the breakdown of the quasiparticle picture becomes evident. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the method by computing the full free-energy Hessian and the critical temperature in a supercell with 1080 atoms. Such simulations would have required tens of thousands of years with the legacy approach; it is now feasible in a few hours on consumer hardware.

items.title: Fast localized urban microclimate emulator: wind and temperatures in unseen urban morphologies
items.summary: Urban microclimate, encompassing wind and temperature fields shaped by building geometry, strongly affects building energy use, pedestrian wind comfort, pollutant dispersion, the urban heat island, and public health. Conventional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is computationally prohibitive for rapid assessments, while many deep learning approaches require extensive training data and struggle with generalization to unseen configurations. In this work, we present the Fast Localized Urban Microclimate Emulator (FLUME), a rapid, data-efficient, and geometry-aware framework based on a Fourier neural operator for predicting three-dimensional wind and temperature fields. FLUME assumes that, under prescribed inflow and thermal forcing, much of the spatial variation of these mean fields is controlled by surrounding building geometry. The framework introduces a Multi-Directional Distance Feature (MDDF), which captures geometry over adaptive, visibility-defined spatial scales. By decomposing simulations of only 23 urban blocks into smaller 3D patches enriched with precomputed MDDF information, FLUME enables learning from limited CFD data. The model achieves mean absolute errors of 0.2 m/s for streamwise velocity and 0.19$^{\circ}$C for temperature on unseen urban configurations. A deep ensemble provides a practical proxy for epistemic uncertainty, and conformal prediction transforms these estimates into calibrated prediction intervals. Ensemble spread is positively related to local prediction error, with greater uncertainty in roof-level shear layers, building wakes, and vertical velocity near the ground. These results indicate FLUME's potential for rapid scenario assessment in urban design and urban climate studies.

items.title: Optical atomic clocks on all-optical atom chips
items.summary: The feasibility and potential performance of optical clocks based on all-optical atom chips using neutral strontium atoms have been investigated. The key benefits of all-optical atom chips are their ability to trap alkali-earth atoms, and how easily these atoms can be manipulated and examined. The planar configuration of the chip enables ring photonic resonators to be incorporated into its structure, making it a promising candidate for active optical atomic clocks. Using the 'magic wavelengths' of the trapping optical fields (813 nm and 390 nm for strontium atoms) minimises frequency shifts in the intercombination clock transition caused by variations in optical field intensity. However, this frequency shift can be compensated for using optical AC Stark shifts, which are generated by the trapping optical fields and have frequencies below the 'magic frequencies'. Furthermore, it has been demonstrated that atom chip clocks can operate using solely repulsive, blue-detuned evanescent light fields when the attraction of the trapped atoms towards the photonic waveguide is realised through van der Waals forces alone. According to estimates, this could result in the short-term fractional frequency stability of the strontium atom-chip optical clocks being limited to ~10^{-16} per second, with an accuracy of about 5 x 10^{-15} for fractional intensity stability in the trapping light fields of 0.001.

items.title: Differences among preparatory processes preceding major earthquakes in Kamchatka, 2014-2025, including the MW 8.8 event
items.summary: Earthquake preparation involves progressive damage accumulation, strain localization, and changes in the organization of seismicity. We investigate preparatory processes preceding seven episodes of major earthquakes in the Kuril - Kamchatka subduction zone during 2014 - 2025, including the 29 July 2025 MW 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake. We track damage evolution using the seismic regularity coefficient dc and seismic strain dynamics coefficient SSD, defined for seismic series. Before 2022, each episode of strong seismicity was preceded by a pronounced dc minimum, commonly accompanied by an SSD minimum, followed by an increase in dc toward a maximum near the strong event or event group. After 2022, dc minima became shallower and were superimposed on a sustained upward trend. We interpret this transition as evidence that the metrics recorded two superimposed processes. The cycles before 2022 reflect complete strain-localization histories on southern or more distant structures that did not contribute to the segment ruptured in 2025. In contrast, the upward dc trend from 2022, with only shallow minima preceding Episodes 6 and 7, marks coupled behavior within the eventual main rupture segment, also influenced by stress transfer from southern source regions.

items.title: Instabilities in self-consistent diagrammatic approaches and how to cure them
items.summary: While self-consistent diagrammatic approaches are widely used to compute the physical properties of correlated quantum materials, their applicability may get severely hindered precisely in the parameter regions where the most exciting physics is observed. One of the major issues, referred to as "misleading convergence", is the tendency of iterative schemes to converge to unphysical fixed points for intermediate-to-strong electronic interactions, regardless of the numerical accuracy of the computation. Here, we explicitly verify that the origin of this problem in several established self-consistent many-electron approaches, defined in the general diagrammatic framework of the boson-exchange formalism, resides exclusively in the stability condition of the respective iteration schemes, and not in an intrinsic breakdown of their self-consistent diagrammatic description. This insight enables a simple and general remedy, as recently proposed in Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016502 (2026): The redefinition of the iterative procedure, by inverting the unstable eigendirections of the Jacobian associated with the fixed point of the self-consistent algorithm. We illustrate the successful outcome of this procedure by means of systematic calculations performed on exactly solvable testbed models. Our results demonstrate that the physical fixed point of the diagrammatic schemes we considered can be stabilized, de facto, across the entire parameter range, including the most challenging nonperturbative/strong-coupling regimes.

items.title: Stringent constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions using high-purity $ν_μ$ CC events in IceCube DeepCore
items.summary: The neutral-current (NC) nonstandard interactions (NSIs) of neutrinos with fermions can modify the flavor oscillations of atmospheric neutrinos as they propagate through the Earth. We present constraints on the NC-NSI parameters $\varepsilon_{μτ}$ and $\varepsilon_{ττ}-\varepsilon_{μμ}$ (one at a time) using a high-purity sample of $ν_μ$ charged-current atmospheric neutrino events collected by IceCube DeepCore over 7.5 years of livetime. These two parameters significantly affect the $ν_μ$ disappearance channel for which this golden event sample is optimized by IceCube Collaboration. The best fit to this dataset is consistent with no NSI hypothesis, and we place the stringent constraints $-\,0.0094 < \varepsilon_{μτ} < 0.0079$ and $-\,0.031 < \varepsilon_{ττ}-\varepsilon_{μμ} < 0.029$ at the 90% confidence level, assuming normal mass ordering.

items.title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
items.summary: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu$^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition at $\sim$580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C$_1$, C$_2$) yields higher branching ratios of the $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition, exceeding 1\% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of $T_{\text{2}}^{\text{opt}} = 2.3~μ\mathrm{s}$ at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.

items.title: Electron-Density-Informed Molecular Property Prediction Using Surrogate Functionals
items.summary: Machine learning methods are increasingly used to predict chemical properties directly from the molecular structure to bypass the often prohibitive cost of quantum mechanical calculations. Recent work has shown that including the ground-state electron density as input to the machine learning model can improve accuracy in this setting. This work employs the recent surrogate functional framework originally developed for orbital-free density functional theory and extends it to predicting molecular properties. We show that passing the ground-state density as input to the model, while simultaneously enforcing it to be the minimum of the surrogate functional, surpasses state-of-the-art performance for six out of seven extensive properties of the QM9 dataset. Additionally, the approach shows improved generalization to larger molecules taken from the QM40 dataset. On all extensive properties of both datasets, our approach outperforms models that are informed by the ground-state density but do not enforce the surrogate functional constraints.

items.title: Physics-guided surrogate learning enables zero-shot control of turbulent wings
items.summary: Turbulent boundary layers over aerodynamic surfaces are a major source of aircraft drag, yet their control remains challenging due to multiscale dynamics and spatial variability, particularly under adverse pressure gradients. Reinforcement learning has outperformed state-of-the-art strategies in canonical flows, but its application to realistic geometries is limited by computational cost and transferability. Here we show that these limitations can be overcome by exploiting local structures of wall-bounded turbulence. Policies are trained in turbulent channel flows matched to wing boundary-layer statistics and deployed directly onto a NACA4412 wing section at $Re_c=2\times10^5$ without additional training on the wing, constituting zero-shot deployment. The transferred policies reduce total drag by 11.1\%, while state-of-the-art opposition control reduces it by 8.9\%. With the actuation cost taken into account, the corresponding net-energy savings are 10.9\% and 8.8\%, respectively. Surrogate training provides an estimated improvement of four orders of magnitude in exploration efficiency over direct on-wing training, enabling scalable flow control.

items.title: Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
items.summary: Ultrafast all-optical magnetization switching (AOS) holds great promise for nextgeneration spintronic memory and hybrid spintronic-photonic systems. However, most implementations to date rely on bulky free-space optical setups, limiting scalability and practical integration. As a critical step toward integrated applications, we demonstrate single-pulse AOS within a silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuit. Using trains of femtosecond laser pulses guided through on-chip waveguides, we achieve deterministic toggle switching in a sub-micron out-of-plane Co/Gd Hall cross patterned directly atop the photonic waveguide. Electrical readout via the anomalous Hall effect reveals a switching contrast of up to 90% for 500 nm-wide devices. In larger Hall crosses, the contrast decreases and switching becomes stochastic, consistent with spatially non-uniform optical absorption as confirmed by finite-element simulations. This behavior is hypothetically attributed to domain wall relaxation and thermally assisted (de)pinning processes within partially switched regions. Our results highlight the critical role of device scaling in achieving robust on-chip AOS and establish a foundation for ultrafast, energy-efficient, and fully integrated spintronic-photonic platforms.

items.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
items.summary: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high $p_\mathrm{T}$. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

items.title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
items.summary: Qubits are powerful computational resources because each additional qubit doubles the size of the accessible state space. This expressive power comes at a cost: adding qubits also increases circuit size, constraint overhead, and exposure to hardware noise. These limitations are especially critical for near-term quantum computers, making the number of qubits required to formulate a problem a central practical concern. In this work, we present a method for efficiently mapping logistics and routing problems onto qubits through structure-aware encoding reduction. We demonstrate the method on a benchmark problem of latency-resilient routing under dual-link failures. For this benchmark, the reduced formulation substantially lowers both the qubit count and the compiled circuit complexity while preserving the original optimization task. By running the reduced model on the same trapped-ion quantum computer as the benchmark, we obtain a 100X improvement in the success probability. This finding shows how careful problem formulation can make current quantum hardware substantially more effective for practical optimization.

items.title: Magnetic connectivity from the Sun to the Earth with MHD models II. Impact of input magnetic maps
items.summary: Connectivity estimation needs to be fast and thus usually relies on semi-empirical models. We previously established that optimised magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) models can also be used to derive magnetic connectivity, yielding good results, especially for complex configurations. However, the modelling is not the only factor that can impact the connectivity estimation. Models' results, both semi-empirical and MHD, depend heavily on the input data used to drive the simulation. In order to quantify this impact on our connectivity estimation, we used 20 different maps by four providers. We selected the period of July 2019, which corresponds to Carrington rotation (CR) number 2219, because it had already been studied in a previous paper. It corresponds to a period of minimum activity, meaning minimal interference from transient structures, but with a high-speed stream and several polarity switches. We have compared our results with in situ data from ACE and developed several visualisation techniques to validate connectivity not only for a specific date but also for a full CR. The choice of the input magnetic map drastically affects the connectivity estimates, with global scores going from 28% global agreement to 63% in the most extreme case. The HMI and GONG maps consistently gave the best connectivity estimations, with more than 50% correct results of the full CR. For this specific period, the GONG-ADAPT maps yielded the least reliable results, with a score below 35%. This is not surprising, as we have shown before that COCONUT required parameter adjustments for these maps. However, WSO maps which showed poor coronal agreement actually provided good connectivity estimates, showing that the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) location is in the end the most crucial parameter for connectivity. Consistent data over a full Carrington rotation are to be favored compared to daily.

items.title: Predicting the Final Stationary State of Sheared 2D Euler Fluids
items.summary: The Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instability is a fundamental signature of the natural world, manifesting in phenomena ranging from atmospheric clouds to the iconic turbulence of Jupiter's Great Red Spot. While the linear dynamics of this instability is well-understood, the ultimate fate of the fluid --- the final stationary state to which it relaxes --- remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we present a general non-equilibrium statistical mechanics framework that allows us to predict the asymptotic vorticity distribution of a sheared 2D Euler fluid. By constructing a self-consistent ansatz for the solution of the Vlasov equation, we determine the stationary stream function without explicitly solving the time-dependent Euler equations. We demonstrate that the relaxation leads to a population-inverted core, where high-energy states are fully occupied, surrounded by a tenuous halo of vortices in the lower-energy regions of configuration space. This result establishes the core-halo structure as a robust statistical consequence of the system's evolution, offering a universal framework for understanding the saturation of shear-induced turbulence in inviscid 2D fluids.

items.title: A data-driven heuristic-ensemble method for behavioural inference in collective-risk dilemma experiments
items.summary: The collective-risk dilemma has become a paradigm for studying cooperation in a wide variety of social experiments, initiatives that generate increasingly rich datasets describing individual actions over successive decision-making processes. Beyond the purely descriptive analysis of such empirical datasets, a methodological framework is required to interpret and reproduce the observed dynamics, a scheme that may be skewed by exogenous biases. Here, we introduce a data-driven, non-parametric method for simulating individual decisions together with a validation protocol for assessing the fidelity level of the outcomes they generate. Our methodological contribution is based on an empirical heuristic ensemble: agents are represented by a finite set of behavioural heuristics, probabilities conditioned on different observable features of the game state, endowed with a hard-voting arbitration that determines their per-round final decisions. This reproducible generative framework allows for behavioural inference in different collective-risk dilemma setups: Behavioural heuristics are seeded directly from empirical data assessing conditional probabilities, without a priori assumptions; a plurality vote with uniform random tie-breaking resolves between competing heuristics each round, adding no free parameters; validation follows a pattern-oriented approach, comparing synthetic and empirical macro-indicators against single-heuristic and uniform-random baselines; synthetic data generated allow exploration of scenarios or experimental setups that have not been empirically realised; as a worked example, we instantiate our methodological approach on the xAire citizen science collective-risk dilemma experiment run in Barcelona.

items.title: Efficient Transport Networks through Edge Pruning by Relative Resistance
items.summary: Transport networks are key to living and engineered systems. How can transport networks adapt efficiently using only local rules, without a global objective or specific boundary conditions? Inspired by observations in biological transport networks, we adapt networks by subsequently pruning edges by relative resistance, thus removing edges whose resistance is higher than the resistance for routing flow through the rest of the network. We find that adaptation by such a local, boundary-condition-free measure of redundancy, set by topology alone, yields sparse, loop-rich, low-dissipation networks.

items.title: Measurement of the free ion yield and estimate of the electron mobility of Trimethyl-Bismuth (TMBi)
items.summary: This paper investigates the physical characteristics of the liquid Trimethyl-Bismuth (TMBi) relevant for charge readout in potential TMBi filled detectors for Positron-Emission-Tomography (PET) instruments. The high photo-efficiency and the possibility of fast timing by detection of Cherenkov light created in the liquid are both favorable for use of TMBi in a PET system. However, to obtain a high position and energy resolution also a readout of the charge signal created due to the absorption of a 511 keV photon is required. For this purpose the liquid has to be clean of electro-negative and ionic impurities. A distillation technique was developed within this study as one of the possible methods to remove such impurities and a measurement on the efficiency of this cleaning method is provided. The relevant quantities for an efficient charge readout are the free ion yield and the electron mobility of the liquid. We report on a new measurement of the zero-field free ion yield in TMBi and, using that result, produce an estimate of the electron mobility. The rather low zero-field free ion yield and its much lower expected electron mobility compared to tetramethyl-n compounds like TMSi question the use of the trimethyl molecule TMBi for a PET detector liquid. But we are also giving arguments that the tetramethyl molecule TMPb could be an interesting alternative.

items.title: On the Utility of Textbooks in Understanding the Renaissance of General Relativity
items.summary: This paper argues for the historical utility of general relativity textbooks written during, or shortly before, the Renaissance of general relativity. More so than research papers, textbooks offer a narrative account of the field--one that may differ substantially from the accounts of other authors addressing the same subject. Textbooks on general relativity therefore constitute a distinctive form of testimony to the intellectual forces that shaped general relativity, particularly during its reinvention period from 1955 to the mid-1970s. A second pillar of this argument is the observation that nearly all principal investigators at the research centers previously identified by Lalli et al.--centers that functioned as intellectual epicenters of the Renaissance of general relativity--eventually produced a textbook associated with their own school of thought. To situate this observation within the broader development of the field, the paper presents a concise history of general relativity textbooks from the theory's inception in 1915-16 to the 1980s. This history illustrates one way in which textbooks can serve as sources for reconstructing the intellectual dynamics of the Renaissance of general relativity.

items.title: Warning of infrastructure deformation anomaly through probabilistic analysis of InSAR observations
items.summary: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) offers a low-cost, wide-area solution for near continuous infrastructure monitoring. However, translating InSAR observations into automated anomaly warnings remains challenging because displacements are relative, affected by uncertainty, and acquired along line of sight (LOS). We introduced a probabilistic warning framework that accounts for these factors. LOS displacements were modelled through a Gaussian distribution. A limit state function was defined to describe the displacement exceedance, and the time-dependent probability of exceedance was evaluated. Instead of a fixed threshold, warnings were identified through abrupt increases in exceedance probability. The framework was validated using three case studies of quay walls in Amsterdam, providing timely anomaly warnings and issued no warnings for the non-collapse case. Results demonstrate the potential of a probabilistic interpretation of InSAR time series for deformation anomaly warning.

items.title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
items.summary: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

items.title: First Experimental Results of Space Object Detection Using the InteRFeX Array
items.summary: This paper presents the first experimental validation of InteRFeX, a non-uniform receive only (passive) array located at the Nova Systems Space Precinct in Peterborough, Australia, designed for space domain awareness applications. It operates over a frequency range of 70 to 300 MHz and is capable of functioning in a range of observational modes, including as a coherent passive bistatic radar for space surveillance, which is the focus of this work. InteRFeX exploits commercial broadcast transmissions as illuminators of opportunity, combining cross-ambiguity function processing for bistatic range and range-rate retrieval with MUSIC-based direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for angular localization. The International Space Station (ISS) serves as the experimental target, with measurements evaluated against Two-Line Element (TLE) orbit predictions. Taking advantage of the dual-polarized array, all four reference--surveillance polarization combinations are evaluated, revealing differences in detection rate and mean signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over the observation pass, with bistatic-range RMSEs of approximately 1 km relative to the TLE-derived reference. Independently, the MUSIC-based DoA estimates exhibit a mean angular separation of approximately $0.45^\circ$ from the TLE-derived reference directions. The angular deviations are further decomposed into along-track and cross-track components, enabling a more detailed characterization of the DoA offsets relative to the TLE-derived reference trajectory. The processing framework also includes a first-order bistatic link-budget analysis to estimate the expected SNR over the observation geometry. These results demonstrate the feasibility of passive-radar space domain awareness using radio-interferometric array technology and establish the proposed signal-processing pipeline as a basis for a dedicated coherent passive-radar mode within InteRFeX.

items.title: Re-emergence of fingering in solidifying liquid-metal drops
items.summary: Solidification is expected to suppress fingering by removing mobile liquid. Here we report an unexpected re-emergence of fingering in impacting molten-tin drops: cooling first weakens peripheral fingers, but stronger undercooling restores them. At weak undercooling, fingers originate from a decelerating liquid rim and solidification reduces the effective acceleration that drives Rayleigh--Taylor-like amplification. At strong undercooling, solidification structures develop while liquid is still spreading, creating lateral mobility contrasts that redirect the residual flow. Comparison between the kinematically estimated solidification time and the experimentally measured fingering-onset and growth-termination times reveals a reversal in temporal ordering across the temperature range. A physics-based reduced-order model combines solidification-modified rim deceleration with mobility-gradient growth, captures the characteristic onset dynamics and accounts for the final finger length within the same physical framework.These findings establish solidification as an active means of regulating interfacial flow and morphology, with broad implications spanning metal-based additive manufacturing and debris mitigation in semiconducting industry.

items.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
items.summary: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. The chip is opto-electronic and features co-packaged electronics using tiny electronic chiplets that are bonded to the sapphire. These consist of an LD driver and transimpedance amplifier for the UV photonics, together with ASICs, ADC, microcontroller, micro-battery and RF-wireless or Ethernet chiplets. The mission of this self-contained cost-effective chip is sensing targeted medical-chemical-biological (MCB) agents in a local or network setting. Eight significant MCB applications are detailed here.

items.title: Latin squares as a model of perfect mixing of high-entropy alloys
items.summary: The structure of high-entropy alloys, which include 5 or more components in equimolar proportions, is proposed to be described in the mathematical language of Latin squares. This model is fundamentally discrete and allows for a quantitative description of ideal mixing, in which any given alloy element is guaranteed not to have an identical element as its nearest neighbor. For the two-dimensional case, the model possesses four axes of translational symmetry, which makes it possible to tile the plane with a single Latin square and, based on the properties of this square, describe the properties of macroscopic material samples. The model makes it possible to make quantitative estimates of the suitability of a particular atomic structure (configuration) for implementation in a perfectly mixed high-entropy alloy with maximum mixing entropy. A condition has been obtained for acceptable fluctuations in the concentration of components at which the thermodynamic stability of the alloy is maintained. The possibility of identifying superstructures in high-entropy alloys based on group theory, as applied to the description and construction of Latin squares, is discussed. Based on the proposed model, the probability of forming a multicomponent alloy with ideal mixing is estimated. For a five-component alloy, this probability is no more than 2.6*10^{-10}.

items.title: The Hydrological Cycle and Circulation of Tidally-Locked Planets with a Finite Moisture Inventory
items.summary: Tidally-locked planets express a range of climate regimes distinct from those found in our solar system. Their atmospheres are often dominated by planetary-wide overturning circulations and super- rotating jets. In this paper we explore the hydrological cycle of such planets and how it might depend on the total inventory of condensate. To this end we use a set of idealised GCM simulations to probe the response of the hydrological cycle to the surface moisture budget in their atmospheres. We find that for low moisture inventories the climate quickly develops a barren day side and a moist night side where the moisture is trapped, as might be expected. For higher moisture inventories the drying of the day side is significantly delayed by the development of a substellar lake just east of the substellar point, which is sustained by the presence of a local thunderstorm-like convective system that persists even after the lake disappears. The timescales for the lake to disappear are millennia, suggesting that even a weak transfer of moisture through surface processes could maintain a moist day side. We also find that adjusting the threshold at which the evaporative rate becomes constrained by the remaining surface liquid depth modifies the longevity of the lake and surrounding day side conditions. These findings have implications for understanding a diverse range of planetary climates and habitability, given the distribution of moisture and presence of a substellar lake.

items.title: Energy-dependent trapping of backscattered helium during magnetron sputtering growth: A molecular dynamics study
items.summary: Helium incorporation during magnetron sputtering can strongly affect thin film growth and lead to the formation of gas/solid nanocomposites and nanoporous structures. Here, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are used to investigate the trapping mechanism of helium atoms (He) and the subsequent formation of He bubbles during the sputter deposition of aluminum (Al) and titanium (Ti) thin films. The simulations account for the kinetic energy distributions of sputtered metal atoms and backscattered gas species. Results indicate that He is efficiently incorporated into the growing films, leading to the formation of high-pressure, dense He bubbles, with a much higher He-to-metal atomic ratio in Ti ($\sim$ 60%) than in Al ($\sim$ 12%). More importantly, the simulations reveal a clear energy dependence of He trapping in Ti: background He atoms at thermal energies are essentially not incorporated, whereas efficient trapping starts at an incident energy of approximately 20 eV and increases up to a saturation regime near 100 eV. Simulated thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) further reveals distinct release mechanisms in the two investigated metals: He desorption from Al occurs at higher temperatures and is preceded by the removal of surface Al atoms, whereas He and Ti atom desorption starts continuously around 950 K, leading to a porous structure. Comparative simulations with argon (Ar) demonstrate negligible trapping even at comparable kinetic energy or momentum, showing that neither parameter alone accounts for the strong He incorporation observed in Ti. The above results are in very good agreement with what is reported in literature for low-kinetic energy He ion implantation in metal surfaces, suggesting similar insertion mechanisms. They clarify the atomistic conditions governing noble gas trapping during film growth and provide a basis for controlling He incorporation and porosity in films synthesized by magnetron sputtering.

items.title: A new device for live cell imaging of biological samples under in-plane shear
items.summary: The effect of mechanical stresses and deformations upon the behavior and properties of cells and tissues is a topic of paramount interest in the field of biophysics. Its understanding is essential for deepening our comprehension of cellular responses to environmental stimuli, with implications in fields ranging from embryogenesis to tumor development. For boosting the understanding in this field, it is important to develop devices for the application of simple deformations in order to probe the cellular response to the basic mechanical transformations. While a number of stretching devices have been developed, in-plane shearing deformation has been little investigated. Here, a new device is introduced that allows the application of homogeneous in-plane shear upon a cell monolayer while imaging the sample with a commercial optical microscope. A description of the faced experimental challenges is reported and a full characterization is presented. It is demonstrated the capability of the device to apply reproducible, controlled and homogeneous shear of both single cells and confluent cellular monolayers.

items.title: Unveiling the Influence of Graphitic Nanocarbon Structures, Defects, and Surface Functional Groups on Supercapacitive Performance in LiTFSI Electrolyte
items.summary: When investigating the performance of supercapacitors (SCs), it was found that they offer high-power density and long life but are limited in capacity and energy density. Water-in-salt electrolytes, i.e., 21___m lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI), offer a solution by expanding the electrochemical window compared to a diluted aqueous environment. While significant research has been dedicated to improving these electrolytes, the impact of carbon properties on energy storage remains relatively underexplored. This study investigated the influence of carbon structures, defects, and surface functional groups on supercapacitive performance in LiTFSI electrolytes. For this purpose, a series of carbon materials, including carbon nano-onions and porous conductive carbon black (ENSACO), were synthesized and systematically modified by oxidative and reductive thermal treatments. Our results indicated that higher specific surface area and active surface area improve the ion adsorption and capacitance, while specific oxygen functionalities, such as carboxylic and anhydride groups, were found to significantly enhance capacitance. Furthermore, crystallinity and graphitic characteristics play a role in capacitance, with smaller graphene domains and greater disorder promoting ion storage. The study demonstrates a direct correlation between carbon microstructure and electrochemical behavior, providing insights into the rational design of carbon electrodes in high-performance SCs.

items.title: Thin-film nanostructuring of NbTi superconducting resonators for enhanced temperature sensitivity in cryogenic thermometry
items.summary: The rising complexity of cutting-edge cryogenic systems is currently imposing challenging technical constraints to the monitoring of ultra-cold temperatures through standard commercially available sensors. Among different technologies, superconducting microwave resonators have been recently investigated as ideal candidates for performing on-chip cryogenic thermometry, in reason of their intrinsically low power dissipation, large temperature sensitivities and excellent sub-$μ$K resolution below 10 K. Through this study, we aim at demonstrating the possibility to enhance the temperature performance of superconducting microwave resonators by means of surface nanostructuring. Different arrays of nanotrenches are strategically patterned on the inductive line of a 1.3 GHz planar resonator, by partially etching a Nb$_{50}$Ti$_{50}$ thin-film, in order to tune the critical transition of the material and, therefore, increase the curvature of the $f_{res}(T)$ response. Although the presence of such thinned superconducting regions introduces larger microwave losses, a 1.5 K decrease of $T_\text{C}$ is recorded, which directly translates into an enhancement of the temperature sensitivity by a factor 10, with respect to a non-nanostructured sensor. A maximum value of $df_{res}/dT = 62 \ \text{MHz/K}$, at 4.2 K, is achieved for the device showing the largest nanotrench width of about 350 nm. These results demonstrate that such a surface nanostructuring approach can be exploited as an effective design strategy to tune the $f_{res}(T)$ response of superconducting microwave resonators. Although this technique is found to introduce additional RF losses into the superconducting device, thereby limiting the achievable temperature resolution to the few-$μ\text{K/Hz}^{1/2}$ range, we believe that similar approaches could be further investigated for the development of future cryogenic sensors.

items.title: The throttling refrigeration system for high cooling power recovery of the PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for radon removal
items.summary: The PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for removing radon (Rn) is designed to operate at a high liquid flow rate of 856 kg/h, equal to 5 liters per minute (LPM), to meet the required Rn concentration. However, it is challenging to maintain a continuous supply of cooling power (20 kW) for the Rn-removal system. This work proposes a throttling refrigeration system to address the power supply problem for the next-generation PandaX-xT dark matter detection experiment. The system utilizes carbon tetrafluoride (R14) refrigerant to recover power based on heat pump principles. The cooling power from the liquid xenon (LXe) in the reboiler at 178 K is transferred to liquefy the gaseous xenon (GXe) in the cryostat through the phase change circulation of R14, enabling xenon (Xe) to return to the detector in the same state as when it was extracted. Consequently, a stable circulation for liquid distillation is established. Given the high cost of Xe, a research and development (R&D) experiment has been conducted to validate the feasibility of this high-cooling-recovery system by using ethanol as a substitute for Xe. Experimental results indicate that the proposed system could achieve a cooling power recovery of 25 kW, with a recovery efficiency of 99%+-0.5%. Additionally, process simulation and optimization of the throttling refrigeration cycle are performed using Aspen Hysys. The deviation between the simulation and experimental results is found to be <3.64%. These findings demonstrate that implementing Rn-removal distillation at a high flow rate is feasible, eliminating the need for liquid nitrogen or cryocoolers. This system could save approximately 3650 m3 of liquid nitrogen per year or reduce power consumption by 230 kW.

items.title: The binormal flow: a toy model for turbulence
items.summary: These notes summarize the content of a one-week course given by Luis Vega on the binormal flow model applied to describe the dynamics of three-dimensional vortex filaments in incompressible fluids following the Euler equations. This topic touches connections between the binormal flow, the Schrödinger map and the 1d cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, providing a rich casuistry linked to the physical and numerical phenomenology. This course was part of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ Advanced Summer School held at the Institut d'Etudes Scientifiques de Cargèse (IESC), at Cargèse (Corsica), from $20^{\text{th}}$ to $30^{\text{th}}$ June 2023. These notes have been written and completed by two of its attendees, Elena Danesi and Pablo Merino.

items.title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
items.summary: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.

items.title: Field Angular Momentum Transformation as a Resolution Criterion for Microsphere-assisted microscopy
items.summary: This paper presents a sequential analysis of the resolving power of a microparticle as a function of its refractive index and size parameter. We demonstrate that the resolution of a microparticle for incoherent point sources is fundamentally determined by the number of excited Mie modes. Based on this mechanism, we propose a novel quantitative assessment framework that defines the spatial resolution limit via the ratio of the squared field angular momentum of the source to that of the total particle field (comprising the superposition of the source and scattered fields). The analytical results demonstrate good agreement with both numerical modeling and classical limits.

items.title: Implementation and verification of a new free boundary module for Resistive Wall Modes simulations with the nonlinear 3D full MHD code SpeCyl
items.summary: Self-consistent numerical simulations of free boundary instabilities, such as resistive wall modes (RWMs) and external kink modes, require special attention given their relevance on the path towards magnetic fusion based nuclear reactors. In this work, a new implementation and a verification benchmark are presented for the nonlinear three-dimensional (3D) full magneto-hydrodynamics (MHD) code SpeCyl, which self-consistently combines a free flow 3D treatment for the edge plasma velocity with double resistive wall thin shell magnetic boundary conditions, capable of capturing the essential features of common setups in experimental devices. Two coaxial resistive shells surround the plasma. Vacuum conditions are assumed between and outside the resistive shells, whose relative positions and time constants can be varied on purpose. The implementation is extensively verified against Shafranov's analytic theory, valid for a circular cross section large aspect ratio tokamak and assuming a flat current profile. The correctness of newly implemented Boundary Conditions (BCs) is confirmed by the good agreement obtained for the linear growth rates of (m=2,n=1) RWM and external kink, over a wide range of wall positions, resistive shell time constants, and for different initial reference equilibria. The (m=2,n=1) RWM growth rates are also benchmarked against previous different RWMs modelling and successful validation studies for RFX-mod tokamak plasmas. The new BCs make SpeCyl a flexible and robust tool to investigate free boundary MHD modes in large aspect ratio magnetic confinement configurations, such as those achieved with the RFX-mod machine and expected in RFX-mod2.

items.title: Spectral-control-assisted Kerr-lens mode-locking in a Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser
items.summary: We report a soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser stabilized by suppressing wavelength competition under high population-inversion conditions. The laser delivers an average output power of 0.5 W with a pulse duration of 112 fs at a repetition rate of 90 MHz and a central wavelength of 2.08 um. Further optimization for shorter pulses yields a pulse duration of 107 fs, through with a reduced output power of 0.22 W. These results demonstrate that spectral-control is an effective approach for achieving stable mode-locking in such laser with strong spectral competition.
