However, uniformly sampling scalarization weights usually induces non-uniform coverage of the PF. We explain this mismatch through the geometry of the scalarization path. As the weight varies, the corresponding solutions traverse the PF at a generally nonuniform speed. Integrating this speed gives cumulative arc length. After normalization by the total length, it defines a cumulative distribution function (CDF) on weights whose inverse selects points at equal arc-length intervals. Building on this insight, we propose SURF (Sampling Uniformly along the Pareto Front). For structured problems, including bi-objective bandits, we derive analytical expressions for this CDF map and the resulting PF-aware weight sampling rule. For general problems, SURF alternates between CDF reconstruction and weight sampling. Theoretically, we show that under provable conditions for bi-objective LS, SURF's CDF reconstruction error converges linearly to an $O(N^{-2})$ discretization floor. Empirically, experiments on bandits, multi-objective-gymnasium, and multi-objective LLM alignment demonstrate that SURF efficiently achieves more uniform PF coverage than baselines.

items.title: On Divisor Function Polynomials and Dirichlet Series
items.summary: We find the Dirichlet series and convergence bounds for the counting function of sum systems (collections of sets of non-negative integers whose Minkowski sum is an arithmetic progression). This motivates the definition and study of divisor function polynomials, which are generating functions for the non-trivial divisor function and for the balanced divisor function that counts, up to a sign, non-trivial ordered factorisations into squarefree factors. These divisor function polynomials turn out to be intimately connected between each other and with Bernoulli numbers and ordered Bell polynomials.

items.title: Large deviations of the spectral radius of iid subgaussian random matrices
items.summary: We study large deviations of the spectral radius of $X_n=n^{-1/2}(ξ_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$, where the entries are iid, centered, variance-one, and subgaussian, with zero pseudovariance in the complex case. We write $ρ(X_n)$ for its spectral radius, i.e. the largest modulus among its eigenvalues. For every fixed $r>1$, we prove $$ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\mathbb{P}\{ρ(X_n)>r\} \ge -\frac\beta2\bigl(r^2-1-2\log r\bigr), $$ where $β=1$ for real entries and $β=2$ for complex entries. We prove a matching upper bound for real symmetric laws with Gaussian-dominated even moments and for complex laws satisfying the sharp Gaussian Laplace-transform bound. These classes include discrete distributions. In the complex sharp class, we also identify the exponential rate for an eigenvalue to enter a fixed disk outside the unit disk. We then turn to lower deviations and establish a quadratic-speed bound. Under the additional assumption that the entry law $μ$ has a bounded density, we prove $$ \mathbb{P}\{ρ(X_n)\le r\}\le e^{-c_{μ,r}n^2} $$ for every fixed $0<r<1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, where $c_{μ,r}>0$. For the matching upper-tail classes with a bounded density, these bounds give a full speed-$n$ large deviation principle, with the displayed upper-tail rate for $r\ge1$ and infinite rate for $r<1$. The upper-tail proof uses a change of measure that preserves the entry support and creates an outlying eigenvalue. The lower-tail proof develops a weighted comparison for adaptive orthonormal observations and applies it to Arnoldi residuals.

items.title: Degree similar and net-degree similar signed graphs
items.summary: Two graphs are degree similar if their adjacency matrices and their degree matrices are simultaneously similar, a notion recently introduced by Godsil and Sun. We extend it to signed graphs in two ways, degree similarity and net-degree similarity, according to whether the degree or the net-degree matrix is used. We prove that signed trees are determined by their degree similarity class, but not by their net-degree similarity class. We then develop constructions of (net-)degree similar signed graphs, based on a signed version of Godsil--McKay switching, on partial transposition and on block extensions. As a byproduct, we obtain infinite families both of pairs of net-degree similar unicyclic signed graphs with non-isomorphic underlying graphs, and of unicyclic signed graphs, not necessarily regular, which are not determined by their degree similarity class. This settles the net-degree version of a problem of Godsil and Sun on unicyclic graphs.

items.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil IV: Analytic local-to-global
items.summary: This is the fourth in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we pin down precise normalizations for some $U(m,m)$ Siegel Eisenstein series, give local Siegel--Weil special value formulas with explicit constants, and record a geometric Siegel--Weil result for degrees of complex $0$-cycles. Using this, we complete the proof of our arithmetic Siegel--Weil results by patching together the local main theorems from our companion papers.

items.title: Second-Order Optimization with Asynchronous Curvature
items.summary: Second-order methods make fast progress per iteration, but forming and factorizing the Hessian often dominates their wall-clock time. We study \emph{Split-Client}, a task-parallel design in which a curvature client factorizes Hessians in the background while a gradient client takes cubic-regularized steps with the most recently published matrix, so that curvature cost appears as a delay rather than as blocking time. For delayed exact Hessians, we prove a first-order stationarity bound that depends on the average age of the curvature rather than its maximum, using an overlap count and a weighted Hardy inequality that allows any bounded-error initial matrix; the analysis extends to subsampled and uniformly inexact curvature. Under a fixed-cost model, the resulting wall-clock bound matches the scaling of optimally tuned Lazy Hessian without choosing a reuse period. In experiments on two LIBSVM datasets, an implementation decreases the objective earlier in wall-clock time than Lazy and Vanilla cubic Newton, with the largest gains at intermediate accuracy.

items.title: Clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers: spectral bounds and anticodes
items.summary: Using spectral and polynomial methods, we show several sharp spectral bounds for the clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers that only use spectral information from the original graph. In particular, we strengthen earlier spectral-radius estimates to obtain an asymptotically sharp colouring bound for general graph powers, and prove a sharp bound for powers of line graphs with a complete characterisation of equality. We also develop polynomial methods yielding upper and lower bounds for clique numbers of graph powers. Regarding the connection between the clique and coloring parameters of graph powers, we propose a spectral analogue of Wegner's conjecture, determine the extremal values for graph squares, and establish the conjecture for all powers when the spectral-radius bound is sufficiently small. Finally, we connect our spectral polynomial method with coding theory: we prove that for distance-regular graphs, optimisation over the adjacency algebra recovers Delsarte's linear programming bound for anticodes.

items.title: PLUTO: An Agentic AI Tool for Interactive Spacecraft Rendezvous Trajectory Design
items.summary: Modern space missions require trajectory design methods capable of efficiently adapting to diverse mission objectives and operational constraints. Despite the maturity of non-convex trajectory optimization techniques, their broader adoption remains limited by the substantial domain expertise required to tailor problem formulations across varying mission scenarios. Recent advances in large language model (LLM) reasoning and agentic AI coding capabilities offer a promising pathway to improving the accessibility of advanced trajectory optimization techniques. This paper introduces PLUTO (Plain Language Understanding for Trajectory Optimization), an interactive trajectory design framework that integrates agentic AI coding tools within a sequential convex programming (SCP) architecture. The proposed system maps high-level semantic inputs to well-defined mathematical constraints while preserving a structured representation suitable for SCP. These constraints are processed through an auto-convexification pipeline and incorporated directly into executable optimal control formulations, thereby systematically connecting user intent and trajectory generation. Visual constraint verification and scenario parameterization further support an intuitive environment for trajectory design across a wide range of application scenarios. Within an evaluation of 50 natural-language rendezvous mission prompts spanning 10 constraint types, PLUTO generated a trajectory for every prompt, and 94% of the resulting trajectories satisfied both the quantitative and qualitative requirements of the mission intent. Ultimately, this work explores the potential of agentic AI to bridge the gap between advanced optimization algorithms and engineer-focused trajectory design workflows.

items.title: Determinant representations for Garvan formulas
items.summary: In this note, we demonstrate how determinant representations for correlation functions in conformal field theory can be used to derive explicit determinant formulas for powers of the classical $η$-function, expressed via deformed elliptic functions with parameters. At genus one, comparing the fermionic and bosonic evaluations of a twisted torus partition function, together with an elliptic Frobenius/Fay determinant identity, gives for every $n\ge1$ a determinant formula for $η(τ)^{3n}$ built from a twisted Szegő kernel; at $n\equiv0,1\pmod 8$ this gives determinant identities for powers of the modular discriminant $Δ=η^{24}$ of the same shape as the classical formulas of Garvan and Milne, although those classical determinants are not recovered. At genus two, an analogous comparison for a torus formed by self-sewing, combined with a finite/infinite determinant factorization of the genus two Szegő kernel, gives a determinant formula for $η(τ)^{3κ^2}$, $-1/2<κ<1/2$, in terms of genus two data; identifying the genus two modular form to which this specializes is left open.

items.title: Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons: Unbiased Gap Estimation and the Price of Preference Feedback
items.summary: We study the minimization of $L$-Lipschitz, possibly nonsmooth and nonconvex $f:R^d\to R$ from noisy pairwise comparisons: comparing $x$ and $y$ returns a bit equal to $1$ with probability $σ((f(y)-f(x))/τ)$, for a known link $σ$ and temperature $τ$, and the goal is a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point. We give an exactly unbiased estimator of the gap $f(y)-f(x)$ whenever $σ^{-1}$ is analytic on a lens in the complex plane, as for the logistic, probit and cauchit links: compare the pair until the outcome changes and return $\pmτ$ times a partial sum of the expansion coefficients of the inverse link, the harmonic number of the run length for the logistic link. It uses at most $1+1/(1-α)$ comparisons in expectation, $α$ the largest queried success probability, and has second moment of order the gap squared plus $τ^2$. With randomized smoothing and the online-to-nonconvex conversion this gives $O\big(d\,(1+d\,C_{link}/κ^2)\,L^2Δ_f/(δε^3)\big)$ comparisons when $Δ_f\ge Lδ$, where $κ$ is the ratio of the largest queried gap to $τ$, which the smoothing radius caps at a constant; relative to the optimal rate $O(dL^2Δ_f/(δε^3))$ for noisy value oracles, comparisons cost a factor $d/κ^2$. We prove that any comparison-based method needs $Ω(d^2τ^2/(ε^2δ^2))$ comparisons on a smooth convex subclass once $d\gtrsim(εδ/τ)^2$: in the comparison-noise-dominated regime the bounds agree in $d$ and $τ$, and a factor $Δ_f/(δε)$ remains open. Experiments illustrate the estimator's cost and variance and the $d^2$ growth of the gradient-estimator second moment.

items.title: Weighted, GIT and Néron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
items.summary: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the Néron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted Néron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the Néron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.

items.title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
items.summary: We construct a smooth embedded annulus in $R^3$ with negative Gauss curvature in its interior whose boundary consists of two strictly convex curves in planes tangent to the annulus, and which contains two closed asymptotic curves. This gives a counterexample to a 1962 conjecture of Nirenberg. The construction is based on Lelieuvre's formula, which yields a closed curve that is then realized as an asymptotic curve on a ruled annulus. The second asymptotic curve is obtained from the periodic solution of a Riccati equation.

items.title: A Network Simplex Framework For Discrete Unbalanced Optimal Transport
items.summary: The network simplex method is a classical algorithm for minimum cost flow problems formulated as linear programs, that has attracted recent interest from the optimal transport community. Indeed, discrete optimal transport is a subclass of minimum cost flow for which network simplex techniques compute exact solutions while leveraging the inherent problem sparsity. However, extending these approaches to other, nonlinear optimal transport formulations has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this paper, we adapt the network simplex algorithm to unbalanced optimal transport. Our proposed framework is applicable to various unbalanced formulations, and can be implemented explicitly in the most common cases, including semi-unbalanced optimal transport. The resulting algorithms are memory-efficient, and perform competitively with existing approaches, as shown by our experiments on a range of transport and barycenter calculations.

items.title: On diagonal sections of Markov products of copulas
items.summary: Given a bivariate copula $C$, the bivariate copula $Ψ(C)$ is defined as the Markov product of $C^T$ and $C$. In this paper we consider the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$ under the additional assumption that its value at a single point is known. We determine the exact upper and lower bounds for the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$, given that $Ψ(C)(a,a)=d \in [a^2,a]$, where $a \in [0,1]$ is a fixed point. Furthermore, we describe some additional properties of the transformation $Ψ$, such as its behavior under ordinal sums and the survival operation. We also study checkerboard copulas in the range of $Ψ$ and matrices associated to them.

items.title: Dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for $\mathbb R^2$-valued polynomials
items.summary: We prove a dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for polynomial mappings $(f_1,f_2)\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^2$ of degree at most $d$. For product probability measures whose one-dimensional marginals have densities bounded by $1$, we obtain a lower bound for the integral of the Gram determinant of $\nabla f_1$ and $\nabla f_2$ in terms of the Gram determinant of the $d$-th derivative tensors $D^df_1$ and $D^df_2$, with a constant depending only on $d$. For pairs in a fixed Wiener chaos, the resulting Gaussian inequality answers a question of Nourdin, Nualart, and Poly concerning a lower bound for the expectation of the Malliavin determinant in terms of the determinant of the covariance matrix.

items.title: Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman spaces in rearrangement-invariant and Hardy spaces
items.summary: In 1981, Bourgain, Rosenthal, and Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of $L_p$ for $1 < p < \infty$, $p \neq 2$. We extend their construction to rearrangement-invariant spaces and Hardy spaces. For any separable rearrangement-invariant space $X$ with non-trivial Boyd indices, we show that these subspaces are complemented, previously obtained by Ghawadrah via a different argument, and establish the following dichotomy: Either one can extract an uncountable family of pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces, or they are all isomorphic to $X$. To this end, we introduce an ordinal index that detects whether $X$ embeds complementably into an arbitrary separable Banach space. On the other hand, we give sufficient conditions which imply that in certain spaces close to $L_1$ and $H^1$, these subspaces fail to be complemented.

items.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
items.summary: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

items.title: The Integrality Gap of the Traveling Salesman Problem is $4/3$ if the LP Solution Has at Most $n+6$ Non-zero Components
items.summary: We address the classical Dantzig - Fulkerson - Johnson formulation of the symmetric metric Traveling Salesman Problem and study the integrality gap of its linear relaxation, namely the Subtour Elimination Problem (SEP). This integrality gap is conjectured to be 4/3. We prove that, when solving a problem on n nodes, if the optimal SEP solution has at most n + 6 non-zero components, then the conjecture is true. To establish this result, we devise a new methodology that combines theoretical analysis and computational verification.

items.title: Monodromy of Tate-Linear varieties
items.summary: We answer a question of Chai about the rigidity of Tate-linear subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_g$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$: we show that that a smooth subvariety of a central leaf of $\mathcal{A}_g$ which is Tate-linear at one point is Tate-linear at every point. This is achieved by a careful analysis of the $p$-adic monodromy groups of Tate-linear varieties, building on recent work of D'Addezio and van Hoften.

items.title: An introduction to local differential privacy protocols using block designs
items.summary: The design of protocols for local differential privacy (or LDP) has been a topic of considerable research interest in recent years. LDP protocols utilise the randomised encoding of outcomes of an experiment using a transition probability matrix (TPM). Several authors have observed that balanced incomplete block designs (BIBDs) provide nice examples of TPMs for LDP protocols. Indeed, it has been shown that such BIBD-based LDP protocols provide optimal estimators. In this primarily expository paper, we give a detailed introduction to LDP protocols and their connections with block designs. We prove that a subclass of LDP protocols known as pure LDP protocols are equivalent to $(r,λ)$-designs (which contain balanced incomplete block designs as a special case). An unbiased estimator for an LDP scheme is a left inverse of the transition probability matrix. We show that the optimal estimators for BIBD-based TPMs are precisely those obtained from the Moore-Penrose inverse of the corresponding TPM. We also review some existing work on optimal LDP protocols in the context of pure protocols.

items.title: Large deviation principle at speed $n^d$ for the random metric in first-passage percolation
items.summary: We consider the standard first passage percolation model on $\mathbb Z^d$ with bounded weights. We show a large deviation estimate for the probability that the rescaled passage time restricted to a box is greater than a target pseudometric. Moreover, the associated rate function can be written as the integral over the box of an elementary cost. Under the additional assumption that weights are bounded away from zero, the random pseudometric follows a large deviation principle (LDP) at speed $n^d$. Consequences include LDPs at speed $n^d$ for the point-to-point passage time, the crossing passage time and the random ball of radius $n$. Our strategy consists in proving first the existence of the rate function for any seminorm $g$ with a multidimensional subadditivity argument, then using this result as an elementary building block to estimate the rate function in full generality.

items.title: Counting cographs in locally dense graphs
items.summary: An $n$-vertex graph $G$ is $(ρ, d)$-dense if for all $U \subseteq V(G)$ of size at least $ρn$, the induced subgraph $G[U]$ contains at least $\frac{d}{2}|U|^2$ edges. In 2010, partly motivated by the theory of quasirandomness, Kohayakawa, Nagle, Rödl, and Schacht conjectured that, for any fixed graph $F$, the number of homomorphic copies of $F$ in a given $n$-vertex $(o(1),d)$-dense graph is at least $(1-o(1))d^{e(F)}n^{v(F)}$. Despite considerable effort, only a few graphs are known to satisfy the conjecture. We find a new broad class of graphs that satisfy the conjecture, including cographs.

items.title: Just Previsions
items.summary: Previsions are positively homogeneous functionals, and are generalized forms of integration functionals. We investigate previsions -- just previsions, not sublinear or superlinear previsions as in previous work. We show that every prevision can be expressed as an infimum of sublinear previsions, and as a supremum of superlinear previsions under mild conditions. This extends to homeomorphisms between spaces of previsions and certain hyperspaces over spaces of sublinear or superlinear previsions, which can also be characterized in terms of orthogonality relations, making the construction a variant of a double powerspace construction.

items.title: Unramified Gromov-Witten and Gopakumar-Vafa invariants
items.summary: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov-Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar-Vafa (BPS) invariants for Fano and primitive Calabi-Yau curve classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar-Vafa invariants in these cases.

items.title: Two-orbit right-angled Polytopes and Hypertopes
items.summary: Abstract polytopes and hypertopes are thin and residually-connected incidence geometries or, equivalently, chamber systems. Their degree of regularity is understood by looking at the action of their automorphism group on the set of their chambers. When this action has only one orbit, they are called regular. In this article, we are interested in polytopes and hypertopes with exactly two orbits on their chambers. Let $I = \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For any $J\subsetneq I$ with $|I| \geq 3$, we show that there exists a class $2_J$ two-orbit hypertope whose diagram is any graph on $|I|$ vertices, with edges all labeled by $\infty$. In order to do so, we first establish a general framework for constructing hypertopes as quotient of chamber systems, and then exploit the machinery of acylindrically hyperbolic groups for showing that this framework can be used to create two-orbit polytopes and hypertopes of class $2_J$. Note that all polytopes and hypertopes constructed in this paper are infinite.

items.title: Decomposition results for multiplicative actions and applications
items.summary: Motivated by partition regularity problems of homogeneous quadratic equations, we prove multiple recurrence and convergence results for multiplicative measure preserving actions with iterates given by rational sequences involving polynomials that factor into products of linear forms in two variables. We focus mainly on actions that are finitely generated, and the key tool in our analysis is a decomposition result for any bounded measurable function into a sum of two components, one that mimics concentration properties of pretentious multiplicative functions and another that mimics vanishing properties of aperiodic multiplicative functions. Crucial to part of our arguments are some new seminorms that are defined by a mixture of addition and multiplication of the iterates of the action, and we prove an inverse theorem that explicitly characterizes the factor that these seminorms naturally determine.

items.title: A Variable Smoothing for Weakly Convex Composite Minimization with Manifold Constraint via Parametrization
items.summary: In this paper, we address a manifold constrained nonsmooth optimization problem involving the composition of a weakly convex function and a smooth mapping under the availability of a parametrization of the manifold. To find a stationary point of the target problem, we propose a variable smoothing-type algorithm by combining the ideas of (i) translating the constrained problem into a Euclidean optimization problem with a parametrization of the constraint set; (ii) exploiting a sequence of smooth approximations of the objective constructed using the Moreau envelope. The proposed algorithm produces a vector sequence by the gradient descent update of a smooth approximation of the objective. In a case where the proximity operator of the weakly convex function is available, the proposed algorithm does not require any iterative solver for subproblems therein. By leveraging tools in the variational analysis, we show the so-called gradient consistency property, which is a key ingredient for smoothing-type algorithms, of the smooth approximations used in this paper. Based on the gradient consistency property, we establish a subsequential convergence guarantee of the proposed algorithm to a stationary point of the parameterized problem and clarify conditions, such as a submersion condition on the parametrization, under which the corresponding point is stationary for the original manifold constrained problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
items.summary: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves a nonlinear elliptic ODE of the form $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation, on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and nonlinearities $f$. Under mild assumptions, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

items.title: Upper bound for the number of limit cycles for symmetric piecewise linear differential equations with three zones
items.summary: The study of the periodic dynamics of the family of continuous observable and non-controllable three-dimensional symmetric piecewise linear systems with three zones considered here can be reduced to the study of periodic solutions of the piecewise differential equation $x'=ax+(b-a)\mathop{\rm sat}(x)+μ\sin t$, where $\operatorname{sat}$ stands for the normalized saturation function. This paper proves that the number of limit cycles (that is, isolated periodic solutions) of the equation is uniformly bounded independently of $a,b,μ$. Moreover, when $ab>0$, the equation has exactly one limit cycle for every $μ>0$. When $ab<0$, it has exactly three limit cycles for sufficiently small $μ>0$ and exactly one for sufficiently large $μ$. When $ab<0$, using Melnikov theory for a deformation of the equation, we prove that, for each fixed $μ>0$ away from two critical values and for sufficiently small nonzero values of the perturbation parameter, there are exactly three, five or one limit cycles, depending on $μ$. This strengthens the conjecture that the equation has at most five limit cycles.

items.title: The Picard number of fibred Mori dream surfaces
items.summary: Let $S$ be a smooth complex projective surface endowed with a fibration $f \colon S \to C$ onto a smooth projective curve $C$. We prove that, if $S$ is a Mori dream space (or, more generally, if its pseudo-effective cone is polyhedral) then the Picard number $ρ(S)$ can be effectively computed by counting the irreducible components of the reducible fibres of $f$. A first simple consequence is that, given an elliptic fibration $f \colon S \to \mathbb{P}^1$ with a section and such that $S$ is a Mori dream space, the Mordell-Weil group of the general fibre of $f$ is finite. The main application is a simple criterion for proving that a surface fibred over a curve is not a Mori dream space. We show that certain Horikawa surfaces, Fermat surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{3}$ of every degree $\ge 4$, particular product-quotient surfaces, and the minimal simply connected numerical Godeaux surface constructed by Craighero and Gattazzo are not Mori dream spaces.

items.title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
items.summary: Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations (PDEs) return posteriors rather than point estimates, but they condition only on equality information: the PDE residual, boundary data, and measurements. Many solutions of interest also obey inequality constraints, including nonnegativity, monotonicity, and absence of arbitrage, which equality conditioning cannot enforce. We prove that conditioning a Gaussian process prior jointly on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is equivalent to conditioning sequentially in terms of Borel measures on the solution space. The physics-informed posterior is therefore a valid prior for the inequality update at virtual points. The combined law is non-Gaussian yet computable through truncated-Gaussian moments, and neither the PDE conditioning nor the inequality update requires modification. We evaluated the construction on a Poisson benchmark, option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields. Under incomplete boundary data, a monotonicity constraint lowered the error of a two-dimensional Poisson reconstruction by $63\%$. On a real S&P 500 option chain thinned to $20$ retained quotes, no-arbitrage constraints reduced held-out extrapolation error by $22\%$ and cut the calendar-arbitrage rate from $10\%$ to $1\%$. On four real air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a Gaussian moment-based sub-zero-tail proxy by $74\%$ at the sparsest monitor count. Changes in mean accuracy and constraint diagnostics differed across data regimes. The probability of the noisy virtual constraint event under the equality posterior measures agreement with the specified bounds before the update. The construction turns admissibility from a post-processing step into conditioning information for probabilistic PDE solvers.

items.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
items.summary: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic à la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic à la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic à la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.

items.title: Minimax Rates for Learning Smooth Populations of Parameters
items.summary: We study pointwise estimation of a smooth binomial mixing density and characterize its minimax rates. Assuming that the mixing density is $s$-Hölder smooth, we first consider the homogeneous setting with a common number of binomial trials $t$. We derive matching lower and upper bounds that reveal three regimes depending on the relative sizes of the sample size $n$ and the number of trials $t$. When $t$ is small, the finite number of trials creates an identification barrier that persists regardless of sample size; at intermediate $t$, more data reduce sampling uncertainty, while the number of trials limits how finely the mixing density can be recovered; and when $t$ is sufficiently large, the usual nonparametric density estimation rate is recovered. Our lower bounds exploit the polynomial structure of the binomial mixture model, while attainability is achieved by a suitably regularized orthogonal series estimator. We then extend the analysis to heterogeneous trial parameters, where the minimax rate depends on the full trial profile through the effective sample size available at each polynomial degree. These results characterize the fundamental statistical limits of learning smooth populations of binomial probabilities under both homogeneous and heterogeneous trials.

items.title: Linearity of Graph Manifold Groups
items.summary: We complete the proof that every compact 3-manifold group is linear. Specifically, we construct a faithful representation in GL5(Q[u]) for a finite-index subgroup of every closed non-geometric graph-manifold group.

items.title: Initialization-Dependent Solution Selection by the Euler-Maruyama Scheme for a Degenerate SDE
items.summary: We study the Euler-Maruyama approximation of the degenerate stochastic differential equation $dX_t = |X_t|^α\,dW_t$, $0 < α< 1/2$, $X_0 = 0$, for which uniqueness in law fails. The Euler scheme started exactly from zero is trapped by the absorbing solution, whereas a nonzero initialization $x_h \to 0$ can select a different weak solution. We identify the initialization-dependent limiting regimes. The critical spatial scale is $r_h = h^{1/[2(1-α)]}$, and the relevant depth parameter is $Θ_h = h\log(1+\log^+(r_h/|x_h|))$. If $Θ_h \to 0$, the scheme converges to the non-sticky weak solution. If $Θ_h \to θ\in (0,\infty)$, it converges to the solution that stays at zero for the deterministic time $θ/|\logα|$ and then evolves as the non-sticky solution. If $Θ_h \to \infty$, the scheme converges to the absorbing solution. The proof is based on an exact scale-invariant Euler chain, a logarithmic exit-time law of large numbers, a discrete Tanaka occupation estimate, and a compact-uniform restart argument. Every finite deterministic delay can be obtained by a suitable vanishing initialization, while oscillating depth parameters yield process-level nonconvergence. Thus a vanishing initialization can survive in the limit as a macroscopic deterministic delay and thereby act as a solution selector for the Euler-Maruyama approximation.

items.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction without Knowing Oracle Smoothness
items.summary: Variance reduction improves the convergence rate of stochastic non-convex optimization under the average smoothness condition. Existing adaptive variance reduction methods are especially designed for average smoothness and do not adapt to standard smoothness. In this paper, we study how one algorithm can adapt to these two settings and the noiseless setting without knowing the smoothness constants or the variance bound. Given the gradient budget $T$, we develop a two-phase method. The first phase compares two independent gradients and switches to normalized momentum when their difference exceeds a threshold. This phase provides both a candidate with standard smooth and noiseless guarantees and also ensures a bounded expected function gap for the second variance reduction phase. The resulting rates are $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, $O(T^{-1/4})$ under standard smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ without noise. When $T$ is unknown, we propose a method with two paths that attain the corresponding rates with logarithmic factors in the stochastic settings. Here, we use a variance reduction path to deal with average smoothness and employ the AdaGrad-Norm for standard smoothness and noiseless setting. Neither method restarts from the initial point or requires a growing number of oracle calls in each round.

items.title: On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins
items.summary: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph that is obtained via changing the direction of all edges which have both endpoints in $X$. The inversion number of $D$, $\operatorname{inv}(D)$, is the minimum number of inversions necessary in order to remove all cycles from $D$. A dijoin $D_1 \to D_2$ is the oriented graph obtained by taking disjoint copies of $D_1,D_2$ and adding edges from all $v \in V(D_1)$ to each $u \in V(D_2)$. It was conjectured by Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1) + \operatorname{inv}(D_2)$ for all $D_1, D_2$. This was disproved by simultaneous constructions of various $D_1$, $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2)-1$. However, no known constructions achieved more than this gain of 1. Moreover, all of the constructions exploit a gap of 1 between $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ and the minimum rank of a family of related matrices, a gap that can never be more than 1, suggesting that perhaps something close to the original conjecture might be true. We prove that in fact additivity fails badly. In particular, for all $\varepsilon>0$ we show that there exist tournaments $D_1$, $D_2$ with arbitrarily large inversion numbers such that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2} +\varepsilon\right)(\operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2))$.

items.title: Analysis of an inexact Schwarz domain decomposition method in 3D
items.summary: We consider an inexact version of the Schwarz domain decomposition method in $3$D to solve a Laplace problem in a domain that is the union of two overlapping spheres. We solve each subproblem approximately by projecting its boundary data $L^2$-orthogonally onto the space of spherical harmonics of degree at most $N$. The model problem arises from the ddCOSMO solver used for implicit solvation in computational chemistry. We analyze the Schwarz-spherical domain decomposition method by establishing a new variant of the maximum principle.

items.title: $J$-class weighted translations on locally compact groups
items.summary: A bounded linear operator $T$ on a Banach space $X$ (not necessarily separable) is said to be $J$-class operator whenever the extended limit set, say $J_T(x)$ equals $X$ for some vector $x\in X$. Practically, the extended limit sets localize the dynamical behavior of operators. In this paper, using the extended limit sets we will examine the necessary and sufficient conditions for the weighted translation $T_{a,ω}$ to be $J$-class on a locally compact group $G$, within the setting of $ L^p$-spaces for $ 1 \leq p < \infty $. Precisely, we delineate the boundary between $J$-class and hypercyclic behavior for weighted translations. Then, we will show that for the torsion elements in locally compact groups, unlike the case of non-dense orbits of weighted translations, we have $J_{T_{a,ω}}(0)=L^p(G)$. Finally, we will provide some examples on which the weighted translation $ T_{a,ω}$ is $J$-class but it fails to be hypercyclic.

items.title: The generator problem for C*-algebras with comparison
items.summary: We show that certain classes of unital, simple, separable C*-algebras with comparison are singly generated, including tracially AF algebras and monotracial crossed products of actions on the Cantor space. In particular, we show that simple, separable, tracially AF algebras have generator rank one.

items.title: Randomized Momentum Transport with Cheap Predictors
items.summary: Momentum methods such as STORM and second-order momentum track the gradient by adding a transport correction to momentum, at the cost of an extra oracle call per iteration. We introduce randomized momentum transport, which evaluates the correction with probability $q$ and otherwise uses a cheap prediction, with importance weighting that preserves the conditional mean and adds $(q^{-1}-1)$ times the prediction loss to the variance. Under transport-bias, second-moment, and residual-control assumptions, linear minimization oracle (LMO) updates, including normalized, sign, and exact spectral (Muon) directions, retain an $O(T^{-1/3})$ stationarity bound for each fixed $q>0$ with a single-gradient initialization. For unnormalized STORM, some $q<1$ lowers the leading coefficient of our sufficient gradient budget if and only if the gradient-difference noise modulus exceeds the smoothness constant, by at most about $10\%$. An online diagonal predictor admits a regret-to-convergence guarantee. At approximately equal oracle cost, querying a quarter of the corrections lowers the final training loss by $18$ to $43\%$ on MNIST1D and raises the test accuracy of Hessian-vector transport on CIFAR-10 by $1.5$ points.

items.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with Constraints
items.summary: We present new algorithms for stochastic optimization problems in which the objective is neither smooth nor convex, subject to a convex constraint set. Our algorithms return a $(δ,\varepsilon)$-Goldstein stationary point, as recently defined for constrained problems by Liu et al. (2024), with improved complexities, and are the first to achieve optimal convergence rates for this task in several settings. In particular, we design projection-based and projection-free algorithms that achieve a $\widetilde O(δ^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using stochastic gradients, which we show to be optimal, and a $\widetilde O(dδ^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using zeroth-order queries, which is also optimal in its dependence on the dimension $d$ and improves over prior work. Notably, our lower bound is given in terms of the Frank-Wolfe gap and holds even for smooth problems, which is of independent interest. These results show that in nonconvex stochastic optimization, the convergence rate is degraded neither by the presence of constraints nor by nonsmoothness. Our analysis is based on a reduction to online linear optimization, extending a related technique from unconstrained optimization.

items.title: Equidistribution of expanding translates of smooth curves in homogeneous spaces under the action of a product of SO(n,1)'s
items.summary: We study the limiting distributions of expanding translates of a compact segment of a smooth curve under a diagonal subgroup of $G=\prod_{i=1}^k\mathrm{SO}(n_i,1)$, where $G$ acts on a finite volume homogeneous space $L/Γ$ as a subgroup. We show that the expanding translates of the curve become equidistributed in the orbit closure of $G$, provided that Lebesgue almost every point on the curve avoids a certain countable collection of algebraic obstructions. Building on Ratner's measure classification theorem and the linearization technique, we establish the result by analyzing polynomial approximations of the curve on shrinking intervals, using Kempf's geometric invariant theory and certain estimates on maximal eigenvalues in $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-representations.

items.title: Leak localisation with a measure source convection-diffusion model
items.summary: Taking a variational approach, study the inverse problem of locating gas leaks from line-of-sight concentration measurements using a convection--diffusion model with the source term a Radon measure. By imposing sparsity-promoting regularisation on this measure, we recover point sources---identifying both their locations and intensities---rather than diffuse approximations. We jointly estimate the underlying physical convection (wind) and diffusion parameters. Our main theoretical contribution is the analysis of Lipschitz dependence of the forward solution of the convection--diffusion equation with respect to its parameters: the measure, and the convection and diffusion fields. Numerically, we employ a semi-grid-free optimisation approach for reconstructing the source measure. Our experiments demonstrate accurate localisation, highlighting the potential of the method for practical gas emission detection.

items.title: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization: Norm-Constrained Oracles with Entropic Weight Updates
items.summary: Multiple-gradient descent is typically formulated in Euclidean geometry, whereas matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms. We analyze a single-loop multi-objective method combining a norm-constrained linear minimization oracle with entropic updates of task weights. For any finite-dimensional norm pair, we establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting, deriving the required trajectory gradient bound from smoothness and lower-boundedness in the unregularized case. With stochastic gradients and a bounded-gradient assumption, one persistent blended-gradient momentum buffer yields an $O(T^{-1/4})$ rate whose leading term has no explicit dependence on the number of tasks. We also establish static regret for the inner weighting objective on arbitrary bounded gradient sequences and, with entropy regularization and a weight floor, iteration-wise inner-gap control after burn-in while retaining ergodic stationarity, conditional on a trajectory gradient bound. The optimal blended gradient can be nonunique in spectral and sign geometries, motivating a selection-independent inner gap. Our analysis extends the spectral construction studied by concurrent MOON to general norms. Experiments compare the method with existing multi-task optimizers and examine its oracle, weighting, and momentum choices.

items.title: Morita Induction and Preservation of Geometric and Dynamical Ideals
items.summary: Given Banach algebras with bounded approximate identities that are Morita equivalent in the sense of Paravicini, we give explicit formulas for the induced correspondence of closed ideals, characterize it via localized Morita submodules, determine when corresponding ideals are Morita equivalent via restricted bimodules, and show that corresponding quotients are always Morita equivalent. We prove preservation of geometric cores associated to compatible dense algebraic cores. For equivalent étale groupoids with paracompact unit spaces, Morita induction preserves dynamical ideals and inner supports. For the Morita equivalence between the $\ell^p$ uniform Roe algebra and the $\ell^p$ uniform algebra, we prove that the latter has a bounded approximate identity of projections, identify its geometric ideals explicitly, and identify corresponding complete-lattice block decompositions of the full ideal lattices with matching extremal ideals. Under property A, or for $p=1$, these blocks collapse; for $p=2$, collapse of the minimal block characterizes property A.

items.title: Pseudofinite abelian groups and asymptotic classes of finite abelian groups
items.summary: This paper studies pseudofinite abelian groups and counting properties of definable sets in finite abelian groups and their ultraproducts. First, we characterize pseudofinite abelian groups in terms of Szmielew invariants and, building on results of Macintyre, extend this analysis to obtain a characterization of pseudofinite $ω$-stable abelian groups. We then give an alternative proof that the class of finite abelian groups forms a multidimensional exact class, explicitly describing the possible cardinalities of definable sets in classes of finite abelian groups. We also investigate $N$-dimensional asymptotic classes of finite abelian groups and provide a series of examples showing that, despite the exactness result, several natural classes of finite abelian groups fail to be $N$-dimensional asymptotic classes for every $N\geq 1$. Finally, in an appendix, we characterize the SU-rank of pseudofinite abelian groups, building on work of Rogers. In particular, we show that for every pseudofinite abelian group $A$, either $\operatorname{Th}(A,+)$ is superstable of finite SU-rank or it is strictly stable.

items.title: Weighted Lojasiewicz inequalities and regularity of harmonic map flow
items.summary: At a finite-time singularity of harmonic map flow in the critical dimension, we show that a Lojasiewicz inequality between the quantities appearing in Struwe's monotonicity formula implies continuity of the body map and the no-neck property for bubble-tree decompositions. We prove such an inequality when the target is $S^2,$ yielding both properties in this case.

items.title: Canonical coordinates for moduli spaces of rank two irregular connections on curves
items.summary: In this paper, we study a geometric counterpart of the cyclic vector which allow us to put a rank 2 meromorphic connection on a curve into a ``companion'' normal form. This allow us to naturally identify an open set of the moduli space of $\mathrm{GL}_2$-connections (with fixed generic spectral data, i.e. unramified, non resonant) with some Hilbert scheme of points on the twisted cotangent bundle of the curve. We prove that this map is symplectic, therefore providing Darboux (or canonical) coordinates on the moduli space, i.e. separation of variables. On the other hand, for $\mathrm{SL}_2$-connections, we give an explicit formula for the symplectic structure for a birational model given by Matsumoto. We finally detail the case of an elliptic curve with a divisor of degree $2$.

items.title: Gorenstein cotorsion pairs induced by balanced pairs
items.summary: Let $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y})$ be an admissible balanced pair in a locally presentable abelian category $\mathcal{A}$, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be its induced exact structure. We study the class $G(\mathcal{X})$ of cycles of two-sided complexes with terms in $\mathcal{X}$ that are both right and left $\mathcal{X}$-acyclic. If $\mathcal{X}$ is closed under direct summands and finite direct sums and is $κ$-Kaplansky for every sufficiently large regular cardinal $κ$, we prove that $(G(\mathcal{X}),G(\mathcal{X})^{\perp *})$ is a hereditary cotorsion pair relative to $\mathcal E$. For relative purity determined by finitely presented modules, we give two criteria for functorial completeness and show that relative periodic modules generate a functorially complete hereditary cotorsion pair. We also compute the relative Gorenstein objects, their right orthogonal, and explicit approximations for a family of exact structures over Dedekind domains.

items.title: Homological periods and higher cycles
items.summary: For any scheme which is algebraic over a subfield of the complex numbers we here construct an homological regulator from Suslin homology to period homology and a higher cycle class map from Bloch's higher Chow group to the period Borel-Moore homology. Over algebraic numbers, making use of the motivic Albanese, we provide a purely geometric description of these period homologies in degree 1 and we characterise the $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$-cokernel of these regulators in terms of torsion zero-cycles, showing that Grothendieck period conjectures imply generalised Roĭtman theorems.

items.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
items.summary: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the KP-II equation with localized initial data. The hypotheses cover all Schwartz functions, data with a half spatial moment in $B^2_{1,1}$, and a class of weighted tensor Besov spaces allowing low regularity in either coordinate. The proof uses the scalar $\bar\partial$ equation associated with the heat operator. A uniform inverse estimate and an exact $L^2$ identity give an inverse construction for large amplitudes. We then estimate the nonlinear remainder on the propagation cones of free solutions and identify the limiting spectral mass through the heat equation. No smallness or zero horizontal mean condition is required. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum.

items.title: Asymmetric minimal mass blow-up for the quintic NLS on a star graph
items.summary: This work is concerned with the focusing quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a star graph with two edges, with a delta interaction of arbitrary strength at the vertex. We construct a non-radial, minimal mass, finite time blow-up solution, whose singularity forms at an arbitrarily prescribed interior point of one edge. Our approach is based on a suitable cut-off of the standard pseudoconformal blow-up solution of the focusing quintic NLS on the line, inspired by Ogawa-Tsutsumi and Burq-Gérard-Tzvetkov. A noteworthy feature of our construction is the persistence of the domain of the Hamiltonian under the flow, obtained by the persistence of regularity method of Kato. We also identify a two-parameter family of distinct blow-up profiles, which should play a central role in the classification of non-radial minimal mass blow-up solutions on the star graph. Our construction is generic and can be extended to a star graph with an arbitrary number of edges. It can certainly also be adapted to other types of metric graphs.

items.title: Estimation, Sensitivity Analysis, and Optimization of Distortion Risk Measures via Simulation
items.summary: We present a simulation-based method for the estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization of distortion risk measures (DRMs), a class of performance measures that capture a wide range of risk attitudes through an underlying distortion function. Existing simulation approaches often approximate DRMs using numerical partitions or empirical distributions. We show that, when the distortion function is piecewise polynomial, the nonlinear structure of a DRM can be handled exactly, without introducing distortion discretization error, using only simulated system outputs. This representation enables the development of a computational method that integrates finite-difference techniques for sensitivity analysis and for solving a broad class of differentiable risk-based optimization problems. Under suitable conditions, we establish strong consistency and convergence rates for DRM estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization. We further extend the approach to non-polynomial distortion functions through polynomial approximation. Numerical experiments on synthetic and calibrated financial examples demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach across a range of applications.

items.title: Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
items.summary: We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean. We show that if both of these metrics are lens rigid then, up to boundary fixing diffeomorphisms, each elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensor is uniquely determined by the lens data whenever it has at least one isotropic point. If none of those points exists, then there are exactly two elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensors with the same lens data. Clearly, not all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms preserve the imposed structure of the slowness surface. We show that the set of well-behaved diffeomorphisms is never a subgroup of all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms. Our proofs are based on an interplay of algebra and geometry, and the key of the proofs is a characterization of the elliptic anisotropy via several polynomial conditions.

items.title: Topping's conjecture for solutions of harmonic map flow with isolated bubbles
items.summary: By establishing a weighted Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality for maps which are close to a fixed harmonic map modulo scaling, we prove Topping's conjecture on continuity of the body map in the case of finite time singularities at which only isolated bubbles form.

items.title: The $E_6$ normal forms: semisimple deformations, geometry, DT invariants, and the $E_{6,\infty}$ order
items.summary: We study the completed Jacobi algebras of $x^3+xy^3+p(y)$ for $\operatorname{ord}_yp=n\ge4$. The explicit normal-form morsification, the filtered length and centre proofs, and the cyclic terminal identities give finite free semisimple deformations. For every parameter of finite order we construct a polynomial curve neighbourhood and a local projective small contraction; the resulting geometric GV and Donaldson--Thomas calculations identify the block multiplicities. The one-dimensional limit $E_{6,\infty}$ is studied separately as an order: we determine its normalization, conductor, radical-idealizer chain, and maximal overorders. The canonical chain yields a nine-dimensional finite quotient whose Ringel dual is isomorphic to its opposite. An expanded construction gives a choice-independent $22$-dimensional quotient and a $40$-dimensional Ringel dual; a corner quotient relates the two finite constructions. The length and centre formulas are proved by a filtered comparison with a homogeneous matrix order and by terminal identities at the exceptional endpoint.

items.title: Tangent-cone cancellation and Maz'ya's $Φ$-inequalities on finitely cornered planar domains
items.summary: Let $0<α<2$ and $p=2/(2-α)$. We study critical nonlinear convolution inequalities for kernels $K:\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}^m$ and functions $Φ:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}$ positively homogeneous of degrees $α-2$ and $p$. We assume angular Lipschitz regularity for $Φ$ and angular $C^{0,γ}$ regularity for $K$, where $0<γ\le1$ and $γ=1$ if $p<2$. On bounded finitely cornered planar domains with a common Dini tangent modulus on the boundary branches, we characterize $|\int_ΩΦ(K*f) dx|\le C\|f\|_{L^1}^p$ for real densities $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, $1<s\le\infty$, by signed angular cancellation on the plane, tangent half-planes, and full vertex tangent cones. An analogous criterion holds on infinite sectors for compactly supported mean-zero densities. For the Newton kernel and each nonzero angularly Lipschitz, positively two-homogeneous $Φ:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ with vanishing half-circle moments, we construct a bounded convex $C^1$ domain $Ω_Φ$, independent of $\varepsilon$, and smooth tests $u_\varepsilon$ satisfying $\|Δu_\varepsilon\|_{L^1(Ω_Φ)}+\|\partial_nu_\varepsilon\|_{L^1(\partialΩ_Φ)}\le2$, while, despite tangent cancellation, their nonlinear integrals grow in magnitude like $\log\log(1/\varepsilon)$. On the Dini class, a constant-preserving linear extension with compact support modulo the domain mean and controlled measure-valued Laplacian yields the same necessary-and-sufficient criterion for the Newton-kernel PDE inequality, without exact corner charts. We also construct infinite-dimensional cancellation spaces containing nonquadratic functions and classify the quadratic locus in polygon moduli.

items.title: Stabilized SQP Method for Convex Piecewise Linear-Quadratic Composite Optimization Problems
items.summary: This paper addresses the local convergence analysis of the stabilized sequential quadratic programming method for a class of composite optimization problems with convex piecewise linear- quadratic (CPLQ) modeling functions. We demonstrate that an appropriate second-order sufficient condition (SOSC) -formulated for composite problems- alone is sufficient to guarantee local superlin- ear convergence of the primal-dual sequence generated by this method. Furthermore, we examine the relaxation of the SOSC and show that it can be replaced with a weaker noncriticality of the associated Lagrange multiplier, provided, the modeling function is polyhedral and a relative interior condition is satisfied. We also present counterexamples showing that the relative interior condition is indispensable and that this relaxation fails for general CPLQ modeling functions.

items.title: Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
items.summary: We obtain sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products whose bases are compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary and whose fibres are closed Riemannian manifolds. These bounds involve the volume of the warped product and of its boundary, as well as the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on the fibre and the Steklov eigenvalues of the base. After separation of variables, these bounds are obtained by comparison with auxiliary Helmholtz-Steklov problems on the base involving weighted Laplace operators naturally induced by the warping function. We also study the effect of various natural geometric constraints, such as the warping function being identically equal to one on the boundary. The proofs make use of various spectral approximation methods, including homogenisation on manifolds when the fibres are one-dimensional.

items.title: Stochastic perturbation and zero noise limit for scalar conservation laws
items.summary: Scalar conservation laws sit at the intersection between being simple enough to study analytically, while being complex enough to exhibit a wide range of nonlinear phenomena. We introduce a novel stochastic perturbation of scalar conservation laws, inspired by mean field games. We prove well-posedness of the stochastically perturbed equation; prove that it converges as the noise parameter is sent to $0$; and that the limit is the unique entropy solution of the conservation law. Thus, the noise acts as a selection criterion for (deterministic) conservation laws. This is the first such result for nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws.

items.title: Adjoint-Based Stochastic Analysis for Fatigue of Aeroelastic and Frictional Systems
items.summary: As engineering systems are optimized to reduce weight and improve performance, vibration behavior, including nonlinear effects, is becoming increasingly important to analyze. While methods such as harmonic balance are popular for analyzing periodic nonlinear vibration behavior, these analyses often only consider deterministic loading. However, real applications experience additional noise in the excitation, and alternative approaches are frequently limited to smaller models. This work expands on a recent approach to calculate a time-varying covariance using a linearized system around a periodic nonlinear response. Specifically, numerical conditioning is addressed and improved for cases increasing from a few degrees of freedom to hundreds of degrees of freedom. The algorithm is then extended to capture correlations across both space and time via a period-spanning covariance matrix. Model reduction is proposed for this calculation to maintain computational efficiency. The period-spanning covariance matrix is used to sample full stochastic cycles and estimate fatigue-relevant statistics up to 1393 times faster than stochastic time integration. Importantly, the present methodology uses the same gradient information as stability analyses and continuation solutions, so it can easily be applied for many nonlinear analyses. The methodology is demonstrated for two beam systems: one with unsteady aerodynamic forces and another with a Bouc-Wen frictional tip force. For the aeroelastic model, statistics are accurately estimated via the present approach. For the frictional system, some errors are introduced compared to stochastic time integration and are attributed to the linear time-periodic nature of the system used in the present stochastic calculations. However, estimated stochastic statistics remain useful given the significant reduction in computation time.

items.title: The Smallest String Attractors of Fibonacci, Period-Doubling, and Thue--Morse Words
items.summary: A string attractor of a string $T[1..|T|]$ is a set of positions $Γ$ of $T$ such that any nonempty substring $w$ of $T$ has an occurrence that crosses a position in $Γ$, i.e., there is a position $i$ such that $w = T[i..i+|w|-1]$ and the intersection $[i,i+|w|-1]\cap Γ$ is nonempty. The size of the smallest string attractor of Fibonacci words and period-doubling words of length at least $2$ is known to be $2$. The size of the smallest string attractor of Thue--Morse words of length at least $25$ is known to be $4$. We completely characterize the set of all smallest string attractors of Fibonacci words, period-doubling words, and Thue--Morse words. For Fibonacci words, we show a recursive formula describing the $2^{n-4} + 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil - 2}$ distinct position pairs that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Fibonacci word for $n \geq 7$. For period-doubling words, we show a formula describing the two distinct position pairs that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th period-doubling word for $n\geq 2$. For Thue--Morse words, we show a formula describing the 32 sets of four positions that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Thue--Morse word for $n\geq 6$. Our results show that strings with the same smallest attractor size can have a drastically different number of distinct smallest attractors.

items.title: A Transform Pair for Doubly Connected Domains
items.summary: A new transform-based technique that generalizes the unified transform method is developed for bounded doubly connected domains as a novel way to numerically solve boundary value problems for holomorphic functions and solutions to the Laplacian. This work builds on the transform methods for multiply connected circular domains developed by Crowdy (2015, IMA J., 80, 1902-1931) and the methods for simply connected bounded domains developed by Hulse et al. (2025, Proc. A, 481 (2319)). The Szegő kernel of the annulus and a corresponding transformation law is pivotal in the derivation of this new technique. The modified Schwarz problem and a boundary value problem for a point vortex inside of a doubly connected domain are implemented in detail to demonstrate the effectiveness of this new method.

items.title: The tensor product of the Fremlin tensor product of Banach lattice algebras
items.summary: We study the Arens regularity of the Fremlin projective tensor product of Banach lattice algebras. We firrst introduce and investigate L-weakly almost periodic functionals, a class of functionals defind in terms of L-weak compactness of their orbits. We obtain a characterization of these functionals in terms of bounded disjoint sequences and use it to analyze the Fremlin projective tensor product. In particular, we prove that, for nontrivial Banach attice algebras A and B, Arens regularity of A j jB implies Arens regularity of both A and B. The converse, however, fails: we construct two Arens regular Banach lattice algebras whose Fremlin projective tensor product is not Arens regular. We also establish several sufficient conditions for the Arens regularity of A j jB, including conditions involving the positive Schur property and order continuity of the norm on the space of regular operators. Finally, we show that when both factors are Banach f-algebras, their Fremlin projective tensor product is Arens regular.

items.title: Lojasiewicz inequalities for maps of the 2-sphere
items.summary: We prove a Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality $$ \left| E(u) - 4πn \right| \leq C \| \mathcal{T}(u) \|^α$$ for maps $u \in W^{2,2}\left( S^2, S^2 \right).$ The inequality holds with $α= 1$ in general and with $α> 1$ unless $u$ is nearly constant on an open set. We obtain polynomial convergence of weak solutions of harmonic map flow $u(t) : S^2 \to S^2$ as $t \to \infty$ on compact domains away from the singular set, assuming that the body map is nonconstant. The proof uses Topping's repulsion estimates together with polynomial lower bounds on the energy density coming from a bubble-tree induction argument.

items.title: List chromatic number of $G(n,r,s)$ graphs
items.summary: We study the list chromatic number of generalized Johnson graphs. Recall that the vertices of such graphs are all possible $r$-element subsets of $[n] = \{1, \dotsc, n\}$ and an edge is drawn between two vertices if and only if corresponding sets have exactly $s$ common elements. We prove that for any fixed $s \geq 1$ and $r \geq 2s + 2$ we have $χ_L(G(n,r,s)) = Θ(n^{s+1}\ln n)$. In case where $s = 0$ we prove that for all $4\ln n \leq r \leq n/20$ we have $χ_L(G(n,r,0)) \geq \frac{n}{120}\ln\left\{\frac{en}{r}\right\}$. Together with previous results of Bulankina, Inozemtsev and Kupavskii this proves that $χ_L(G(n,r,0)) = Θ\left\{n\ln\left\{\frac{en}{r}\right\}\right\}$ uniformly for $2 \leq r \leq (1/2-\varepsilon)n$.

items.title: Profinite rigidity of Kähler groups: Riemann surfaces and subdirect products
items.summary: This paper establishes strong profinite rigidity results for Kähler groups, showing that certain groups are determined within the class of residually finite Kähler groups by their profinite completion. Examples include products of surface groups and certain groups with exotic finiteness properties studied earlier by Dimca-Papadima-Suciu and Llosa Isenrich. Consequently, there are aspherical smooth projective varieties that are determined up to homeomorphism by their algebraic fundamental group. The main tool is the following: the holomorphic fibrations of a closed Kähler manifold over hyperbolic 2-orbifolds can be recovered from the profinite completion of its fundamental group. We also prove profinite invariance of the BNS invariant.

items.title: Holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphism groups via the Symplectic Density Property
items.summary: We show that the cotangent bundle of a holomorphically flexible Stein manifold has the symplectic density property. As application we deduce holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of real cotangent bundles by complex symplectic automorphisms of the complexified cotangent bundles, which preserve the real bundle, in the Carleman sense, i.e. in the Whitney topology.

items.title: PySymmetry: A Sage/Python Framework for the Symmetry Reduction of Linear G-Equivariant Systems
items.summary: Despite the prevalence of symmetry in scientific linear systems, these structural properties are often underutilized by standard computational software. This paper introduces PySymmetry, an open-source Sage/Python framework that implements classical representation theory to simplify G-equivariant linear systems. PySymmetry uses projection operators to generate symmetry-adapted bases, transforming equivariant operators into a more efficient block-diagonal form. Its functionalities include defining and reducing representations, calculating multiplicities, and obtaining the explicit block structure. We demonstrate PySymmetry's versatility through three case studies: a chemistry application, a numerical benchmark on the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation that achieved a performance increase of over 17x compared to standard methods, and a symbolic investigation that enabled the first complete analytical classification of a challenging problem in celestial mechanics. Designed for seamless integration with libraries like NumPy and SciPy, PySymmetry offers a powerful, user-friendly tool for exploring symmetries in theoretical and applied contexts. ```

items.title: The Burnside ring of simple $\mathcal{C}$-sets
items.summary: The Burnside ring of a finite category, introduced by Webb, generalizes the classical Burnside ring of a finite group. However, unlike the classical case, the Burnside ring of a finite category has finite rank if and only if the category is equivalent to a groupoid. In this article, we introduce a new invariant associated with a finite category $\mathcal{C}$, called the \emph{simple Burnside ring} of $\mathcal{C}$ and denoted by $B^S(\mathcal{C})$. This construction is obtained from simple $\mathcal{C}$-sets and generalizes the classical Burnside ring of a finite group. Moreover, the ring $B^S(\mathcal{C})$ always has finite rank. We develop the basic theory of simple $\mathcal{C}$-sets and study several structural properties of the ring $B^S(\mathcal{C})$. In particular, we determine all ring homomorphisms from $B^S(\mathcal{C})$ to $\mathbb{Z}$, describe its prime spectrum, and obtain a decomposition theorem expressing $B^S(\mathcal{C})$ as a product of simple Burnside rings of strongly connected subcategories.

items.title: Jacobson radicals of Ore extensions
items.summary: Let $R$ be a ring, $σ$ be an automorphism of $R$, and $D$ be a $σ$-derivation on $R$ with $Dσ=σD$. We will show that $J(R[x;σ,D])\subseteq A[x;σ,D]$ where $A$ is a collection of all leading coefficients of polynomials in $J(R[x;σ,D])$. In addition, we will prove that $J(R[x;σ,D])\cap R$ is nil if $σ$ is locally torsion and one of the following conditions is given: (1) $R$ is a PI-ring and $D$ is $q$-skew, (2) $R$ is an algebra over a field of characteristic $p>0$ and $D$ is a locally nilpotent derivation such that $σD=Dσ$. This answers partially an open question by Greenfeld, Smoktunowicz and Ziembowski.

items.title: Non-Bloch band theory for finite banded non-Hermitian Toeplitz matrices
items.summary: Non-Bloch band theory recovers the open-boundary spectrum of a non-Hermitian chain from its Bloch Hamiltonian evaluated along the generalised Brillouin zone rather than the unit circle. We develop its finite-size counterpart for banded Toeplitz matrices with real open-boundary spectrum. Reality of the spectrum forces the generalised Brillouin zone to be parametrised by an analytic polar curve, so the known sufficient condition for a real spectrum is also necessary under some mild non-degeneracy conditions. At finite size $n$, the eigenvalues of the original and the symmetrised Bloch Hamiltonians are given by samples at $n$ quantised momenta from the same limiting band, although separated by a phase mismatch of order $1/n$ which we obtain in closed form. Iterating this correction $K$ times yields a quantisation rule on the generalised Brillouin zone reproducing the finite spectrum with an error $\mathcal{O}(n^{-K-1})$ for any fixed $K$. At finite size, the generalised Brillouin zone itself is unchanged and only its parametrisation depends on $n$.

items.title: Bounds and Limitations on Codes Achieving List Recovery Capacity
items.summary: In coding theory, list recoverability is a fundamental concept which robustly captures how ``spread-out'' codewords are in a code. More formally, given a code $C \subseteq Σ^n$ and input lists $S_1, \dots, S_n \subseteq Σ$ of size at most $\ell$, list recoverability requires that there are at most $L$ codewords $c \in C$ such that $c_i \in S_i$ for at least $(1-ρ)n$ choices of $i \in [n]$. List recovery is an important question which has found applications in many areas, including complexity theory, property testing, compressed sensing, streaming algorithms, and cryptography. As our first main result, we establish a tight ``generalized singleton bound''. Formally, we show that for constant $\ell, L,ρ$ and sufficiently large alphabets $Σ$, if we define $R^*=\frac{L+1-\ell}{L}-\frac{L+1}{L}ρ$, it is possible for a $(ρ,\ell,L)$ list-recoverable code to have rate $R^*-ε$ but impossible to have rate $R^*+ε$. One direction of our result already directly generalizes and improves a weaker impossibility result due to Goldberg, Shangguan, and Tamo. For our second main result, we prove that there is a fundamental shortcoming in existing methods that aim to construct explicit, optimal list-recoverable codes. Indeed, recent work has constructed explicit codes achieving list-decoding capacity (along with other related properties) using a framework introduced in the work of Alon--Edmonds--Luby (AEL). We give a meta-analysis of such constructions by presenting an ``AEL framework'' which captures all such recent constructions in the literature. Within this framework, we show that no AEL-based code can break a recently-identified list-recovery barrier for additive and linear codes.

items.title: Relaxed Centralized Circumcentered-Reflection Methods for Convex Feasibility: Convergence and Finite Termination
items.summary: Projection methods are among the most widely used techniques for solving convex feasibility problems due to their simplicity and robustness. However, classical projection-based algorithms and existing circumcentered-reflection methods generally provide only asymptotic convergence. In this paper, we introduce a relaxed version of the centralized circumcentered-reflection method (cCRM) obtained through an extrapolation of the circumcenter step. We first analyze the two-set case and then extend the proposed approach to the successive framework for multiple convex sets, including under- and over-relaxation and a backtracking strategy.
