The convergence analysis establishes Fejér monotonicity and global convergence under suitable conditions, while local error-bound assumptions yield linear convergence and standard regularity assumptions imply superlinear convergence. Motivated by finitely convergent projection methods based on perturbed feasible sets, we further investigate a perturbed relaxed formulation designed to achieve finite termination. Numerical experiments show good practical performance, comparable to and competitive with the finitely convergent PACA method. The results also provide clear numerical evidence of finite termination in the tested instances.

items.title: Sharp exponential integrability of conjugate functions
items.summary: We prove that if a real-valued function $f\in L^1$ on the complex unit circle has a gap of width at least $π$ in its essential range, then $\exp(\tilde f)$ is not integrable, where $\tilde f$ is the conjugate function. More generally, the exponential function can be replaced by any nonnegative convex function $Y$ satisfying $$ \int_0^\infty Y(x) e^{-x}\, dx = \infty. $$ We also establish a local version on arcs of the unit circle: Under a natural condition on the inverse images of the two sides of the gap, $Y(\tilde f)$ fails to be integrable on the arc; in particular, it suffices that one of these inverse images is not an interval modulo null sets. Furthermore, we obtain corresponding results for complex-valued functions and a $Y$-integrability version of Zygmund's result.

items.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ansätze
items.summary: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.

items.title: Sum of Squares and Non Sum of Squares Regimes for the Toeplitz Bottcher Wenzel Form
items.summary: Toeplitz matrices are among the simplest structured models of translation invariance, arising naturally in convolution, stationary covariance models, and discretizations of translation-invariant operators. For a pair of real matrices, the Böttcher--Wenzel form (BW form) is a nonnegative quartic measuring the gap in the corresponding commutator inequality. László conjectured that, when both matrices are Toeplitz, this quartic is a sum of squares for every matrix order. We show that the conjecture is false. More precisely, we identify an explicit family of corner-supported Toeplitz pairs, retaining only the outermost diagonals on the two sides, for which the associated BW form is not a sum of squares at all sufficiently large orders. The proof reduces the complete family of Gram representations to a finite complex test: its Gram-invariant part develops a strictly negative limiting direction, while the remaining Gram-dependent contribution vanishes. We also give an explicit sufficient threshold for the matrix order. The negative result is complemented by two positive regimes. If either Toeplitz factor is symmetric or skew-symmetric, then the corresponding BW form is SoS for every order, with the other factor allowed to be an arbitrary real Toeplitz matrix. For unrestricted Toeplitz pairs, we further prove SoS representability for every $2\le N\le50$, with formal Lean~4 verification through order 20. The large-order non-SoS theorem, including the explicit sufficient threshold, has also been formally verified in Lean 4.

items.title: A 9-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra isomorphic to its complex conjugate admitting no real form
items.summary: We give an explicit example of a 9-dimensional 5-step nilpotent complex Lie algebra, generated by two elements, that is isomorphic to its complex conjugate but has no real form. In contrast to the earlier 10-dimensional examples, our proof is completely elementary and very short.

items.title: Critical Ising model as the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory
items.summary: We construct a linear map from the space of spin polynomials in the critical Ising model on a lattice to the state space of the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory. The kernel of the map consists precisely of null fields, i.e., spin polynomials that vanish in all correlations. For a polynomial $\Op$ which is not a null field, we define its scaling dimension $Δ_{\Op}\in\Z_{\geq0}\cup(\Z_{\geq0}+\frac{1}{8}),$ to be the lowest $\Loper{0}+\Loperbar{0}$ eigenvalue in the decomposition of its image into homogeneous components. We show that as the mesh size $δ$ goes to zero, the rescaled field $δ^{-Δ_{\Op}}\Op$ has a non-trivial scaling limit, when inserted in correlations with other such fields. Moreover, all these limits can be expressed in terms of correlations of primary fields of $M(4,3)$ and the Virasoro action in the continuum. The highest weight vectors of $M(4,3)$, the joint eigenvectors of $\Loper{0}$ and $\Loperbar{0}$ with the same eigenvalues $0,1/16,1/2$ for both, are the images of the constant $1$, the spin at a single lattice vertex, and the energy at a single lattice edge, respectively. For the proof, we construct a map from a larger lattice field space, accommodating also fermion and disorder insertions, to a direct sum of two fermionic Fock spaces. This direct sum contains contains the state spaces of both the $M(4,3)$ and the free fermion CFT. The main technical ingredient of the proof is a new version of the exact fermionic current action on the space of lattice local fields due to C. Hongler, K.K. and F. Viklund, combined with some new advances in discrete complex analysis. Our results are valid on arbitrary isoradial graphs.

items.title: Structure and Decomposition of Deltoids in Abelian Groups
items.summary: Deltoids provide a natural framework for studying defective (partial) matchings in abelian groups, and we develop both structure and existence results in this setting. Given finite subsets $A$ and $B$ of an abelian group $G$, a matching is a bijection $f:A\to B$ such that $af(a)\notin A$ for all $a\in A$, a definition motivated by the study of canonical forms for symmetric tensors. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a partial matching with any prescribed defect, and then describe the minimal unavoidable defect for a pair $(A,B)$. We also define and examine a defective version of Chowla sets in the matching context. We prove a structure theorem identifying obstructions to the existence of partial matchings with small defect. Finally, within the deltoid setup, we establish max-min results on the partitioning of $A$ and $B$ into left- and right-admissible sets. Our tools mix results from transversal theory with ideas from additive number theory.

items.title: The second type of power mean bounds for the hypergeometric mean
items.summary: In this paper, by using signs rule for a class of special power series and for the Laplace integrals, we find the best power mean bounds for the hypergeometric function (sharp at the right endpoint). Our results contain many known conclusions.

items.title: Geometry of the Atomic Condition
items.summary: The class AC of integrands satisfying the atomic condition was introduced by De Philippis, De Rosa, and Ghiraldin in 2018. These integrands give rise to Almgren elliptic geometric functionals as proven by the second author and De Rosa in 2020. Explicit examples in intermediate dimensions include small class 2 perturbations of the area integrand and the recent anisotropies constructed by De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, among them the $\ell^q$ norms in Plücker coordinates for $q$ close to $2$. We reinterpret the atomic condition in terms of convex geometry. We also propose variants of AC, related to the SAC and USAC defined by De Rosa and Tione, which we call the exposed condition EC, the strong exposed condition SEC, and the quadratic exposed condition QEC. For integrands of class 2, QEC is equivalent to validity of a Caccioppoli-type inequality and is stable under class 2 perturbations; every such QEC integrand admits Lipschitzian normals. Combining these results with a result of De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, we prove that a Lipschitz graph whose anisotropic mean curvature for a QEC integrand of class 2 is $p$-integrable, with $k < p < \infty$, is of class $\mathscr{C}^{1,α}$ on an open set of full measure. Finally, for all $k \ge 2$ and $n - k \ge 3$ we construct strictly polyconvex integrands - associated to inner-product norms on $\bigwedge_k \mathbf{R}^n$ - which fail the atomic condition, showing that strict polyconvexity is necessary but not sufficient for AC.

items.title: On a conjecture on Romanoff type representations
items.summary: Let $r_1,\ldots,r_t$ be positive integers, and let $\mathcal A$ be the set of integers of the form $2^{k_1^{r_1}}+\cdots+2^{k_t^{r_t}}$, where $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ are positive integers. For any positive integer $n$, let $r(n)$ be the number of representations $n=p+a$ with $p$ an odd prime and $a\in \mathcal A$. We prove that if $r_1^{-1}+\cdots+r_t^{-1}=1$, then, for every fixed positive integer $m$, the set of integers $n$ with $r(n)\ge m$ has positive lower asymptotic density. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Chen.

items.title: Proof of a magnificent conjecture
items.summary: Motivated by super-Yang-Mills theory on a Calabi-Yau 4-fold, Nekrasov and Piazzalunga have assigned weights to $r$-tuples of solid partitions and conjectured a formula for their weighted generating function. We define $K$-theoretic virtual invariants of Quot schemes of 0-dimensional quotients of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^4}^{\oplus r}$ by realizing them as zero loci of isotropic sections of orthogonal bundles on non-commutative Quot schemes. Via the Oh-Thomas localization formula, we recover Nekrasov-Piazzalunga's weights and derive their sign rule. Our proof passes through refining the $K$-theoretic invariants to sheaves and describing them via Clifford modules, which lets us show that they arise from a factorizable sequence of sheaves in the sense of Okounkov. Taking limits of the equivariant parameters, we then deduce the Nekrasov-Piazzalunga conjecture from its 3-dimensional analog.

items.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets II: general configurations and fractal restricted projections
items.summary: We prove optimal dual Furstenberg estimates for Frostman and Katz--Tao configurations for which the shadings are not locally concentrated near pencils. The starting point is the sticky estimate of Orponen and Shmerkin in a companion paper. We deduce restricted projection theorems in the plane and in higher dimensions. In particular, Ahlfors-regular measures on the circle satisfy a Marstrand-type projection theorem. Applications include restricted projections to surfaces in the $\mathbb{G}(4,2)$ Grassmannian, pinned distances, discretized sum-product, and a new proof of the dimension formula for planar self-affine sets.

items.title: Diffraction of waves by finite thin coatings: asymptotic expansion and effective models
items.summary: We consider the Helmholtz equation in a Dirichlet angular sector (which may be locally perturbed) covered on one side by a thin homogeneous layer. First, we propose an asymptotic expansion of the solution at any order and for any angle when the thickness of the layer tends to 0, using a matched asymptotic expansion. This consists in introducing different asymptotic expansions in three subdomains -- the vicinity of the corner, the layer and the rest of the domain -- that are linked through matching conditions. The presence of the corner makes these matching conditions delicate to derive because the fields have complex singular behaviors. We overcome this difficulty using a novel system of algebraic tools, including formal series and operators on these series. Moreover, we justify the asymptotic expansion with error estimates and provide details on the form of the expansion depending on the angle. We numerically validate this expansion up to order 5. This requires computing the behavior at infinity of some corner profiles. To do this, we introduce a Galerkin-type method enriched by complements at infinity. These complements are known functions that appear in the behavior at infinity of the corner profiles with coefficients that become unknowns of the system. Finally, we propose effective models of order 3, resp. 5 where, far from the corner, the layer is replaced with an effective Robin, resp. Ventcel, boundary condition and, near the corner, an artificial boundary is introduced and a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) type condition is imposed. The DtN map relies on a modal decomposition of the truncated asymptotic expansion at order 3, resp. 5. The modes take into account the singular behavior of the expansion terms, the corner profiles and some algebraic matching coefficients. We prove the well-posedness of our effective models, as well as error estimates, and provide numerical results.

items.title: Differentiable Hybrid Modelling for Learning and Optimising Chemical Transport Processes from Experimental Data
items.summary: Transport models underpin the design and optimisation of chemical processes, yet their constitutive laws are typically hand-picked, their experimental initial conditions are assumed exact, and their computational cost restricts optimisation to a handful of process variables. Here we introduce a differentiable hybrid modelling framework that embeds neural networks within a GPU-accelerated population balance equation solver to discover constitutive laws and assimilate initial conditions directly from experimental crystallisation data. Using thirteen real experiments with multi-dimensional size and shape measurements, we show that treating measured initial conditions as exact yields a physically inconsistent rate law despite improved predictive accuracy, whereas assimilating them recovers a physically consistent, non-linear law and reduces trajectory error sevenfold relative to conventional modelling. End-to-end differentiability further enables gradient-based optimisation of high-dimensional operating profiles, identifying a 300-variable temperature profile that reduces crystal aspect ratio by 25% at constant mass, facilitating superior product attributes. Our framework augments, rather than replaces, mechanistic modelling, offering a general route to learning transport models from data and optimising processes with them.

items.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets I: the sticky case
items.summary: We introduce spread-out measures, a notion of local non-concentration near pencils for measures on Grassmannians. We establish an optimal $δ$-discretized dual Furstenberg estimate for ``sticky spread-out'' shadings. A simple-to-state corollary is the following. Assume that $ν$ is an Ahlfors $s$-regular measure on $\mathbb{G}(2,1)$ with $s > 0$. Let $E \subset \mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a Borel set with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension. Then, $\dim_{\mathrm{H}} Π_{V}(E) = \min\{\dim_{\mathrm{H}} E,1\} \quad \text{for $ν$-a.e. } V \in S^1$. The general $δ$-discretized estimate for ``sticky spread out'' configurations here is the starting point for a more general theorem in the companion paper of Cohen, Shmerkin, Wang and Zakharov, where the ``stickiness'' hypothesis is removed. For instance, the assumption of equal Hausdorff and packing dimension in the result stated above will be dispensed with in the companion paper.

items.title: From Manipulation to Abstraction: The Impact of Flexible Decomposition on Numerical Competence in Primary School
items.summary: This study examines a structured instructional approach to the decomposition and recomposition of large numbers in six primary school classes (three 4th-grade and three 5th-grade, N = 120), using a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design with a control group and a four-week delayed post-test. The 12-week intervention follows the Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract (CPA) progression. The experimental groups achieved mean gains of 34.0 points (4th grade) and 29.6 points (5th grade) out of 100, against 16.4 and 11.1 points in the control groups (all p < 0.001). The Time x Group interaction in the mixed ANOVA gave partial $η^2$ = 0.931. An ANCOVA with the pre-test as covariate estimated an adjusted difference of 18.25 points, 95% CI [17.59, 18.92], F(1, 117) = 2,978.10, p < 0.001, partial $η^2$ = 0.962. The advantage was present on all five components of the test. At the delayed post-test the experimental groups retained 93.7% of their gain, against 78.6% in the control groups. Internal consistency of the instrument at pre-test was acceptable (Cronbach's $α$ = 0.735). The effects are unusually large, and the limits of the design that bear on their interpretation are discussed.

items.title: Statistical inference for rough Burgers-type stochastic partial differential equations
items.summary: We consider the Burgers-type stochastic PDE \[ du = θ\,\partial_x^2 u\,dt + f(u)\,dt + g(u)\,\partial_x u\,dt + σ\,dW(t), \] driven by space--time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, where \(θ>0\) is the diffusivity parameter and \(σ>0\) the noise intensity. The transport term \(g(u)\,\partial_x u\) admits no classical interpretation, and we work with the mild solutions defined via rough paths following~\cite{Hairer2011}, for which the solution decomposes as \(u=ψ+R\) with \(ψ\) a stationary centred Gaussian process solving a damped stochastic heat equation and \(R\) a remainder. We first show that, away from the initial time, \(R\) is Lipschitz in space and Hölder in time of order strictly greater than \(1/2\), hence strictly smoother than \(ψ\) in both variables. We then compute exactly the spatial quadratic variation and the temporal quartic variation of \(ψ\), almost surely and not merely in \(L^{2}(Ω)\), and prove that the corresponding variations of \(u\) are unaffected by the remainder. Combined with an exact time-scaling identity, this separation of regularity scales yields strongly consistent pathwise estimators of \(θ\). To our knowledge this is the first inference procedure for an SPDE whose solution is defined only pathwise, as a measurable function of a rough path, rather than as an Itô process.
authors: Simon Chony Acosta Christian Olivera Ciprian Tudor

items.title: TAP variational formula for 2-spin models with general interaction matrix and marginality
items.summary: We establish a Thouless--Anderson--Palmer (TAP) variational formula for the free energy of spherical $2$-spin models whose interaction matrices have a compactly supported limiting spectral distribution. The formula holds at every inverse temperature and, in particular, extends the TAP representation previously obtained for the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main contribution is a new microcanonical proof designed to handle marginality. We partition the sphere according to the smallest collection of top eigendirections carrying a prescribed fraction of the norm. On every element of this partition, the remaining degrees of freedom are effectively at high temperature and their contribution can be computed through spherical-integral asymptotics. The resulting auxiliary variational problem separates the macroscopic low-temperature contribution from the high-temperature fluctuation term; its maximization recovers the usual TAP functional and Plefka condition. This decomposition also shows why neighborhoods of the TAP maximizers alone do not capture the Gibbs mass: all eigendirections associated with large eigenvalues contribute on the same exponential scale, a manifestation of the marginality of spherical $2$-spin states.

items.title: A discrete analogue of $\mathscr{N}=2$ super Weil-Petersson volumes
items.summary: We introduce a discrete spectral curve from $\mathscr{N}=2$ double-scaled SYK whose topological recursion defines quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. The curve has two edge theories: a local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory at the lower edge and a bosonic theory at the upper edge. Focusing on the local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory, we compute its finite-$q$ volumes and independently check the first few using the string equation. In the $q\rightarrow 1$ continuum limit, these recover the super Weil-Petersson volumes of Turiaci and Witten. Finally, we give an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation of these local volumes on the moduli space of stable marked curves, in terms of a deformed spin class with a gap-dependent $κ$-class dressing.

items.title: The Renormalized Area--Willmore Relation
items.summary: In [1, Proposition 8.1], Alexakis and Mazzeo showed that the renormalized area of minimal surfaces in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^3$ approaching the ideal boundary $\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^3$ is the negative of the Willmore energy of their Euclidean conformal compactifications. In this paper, we investigate whether there are other geometric surface equations for which these two quantities satisfy a universal proportionality relation. We answer this question in the affirmative by extending the Alexakis--Mazzeo result to a broader class of geometric equations containing, as two distinguished cases, the equations defining generalized singular minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and linear Weingarten surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, for rotational linear Weingarten surfaces, we express both energies in terms of generalized hyperelliptic integrals and show that their doubles form a family of rotational tori in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose Willmore energies realize all values in $(2π^2,\infty)$, with a particular subfamily converging to the Clifford torus in $\mathcal{W}^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$, as the optimal value $2π^2$ is approached.

items.title: Conditioning diffusions on a terminal bearing
items.summary: We study sampling of a diffusion on $[0,T]$ conditioned on its terminal position lying on a prescribed ray, i.e. on an exactly observed bearing. For a linear drift we derive closed-form expressions for the Doob $h$-function and its gradient. For a broad class of tracking models admitting a Kronecker block structure, the guiding term is obtained from a single row of a matrix exponential, and the conditioned process decomposes into independent radial and angular components. For a nonlinear drift, we construct a guided process using the $h$-function of the linear model and prove absolute continuity of the law of the true conditioned process with respect to the law of the guided process, with an explicit likelihood ratio. This result is used to devise an auxiliary particle filter for bearings observed sequentially in time without noise. Numerical experiments show that the proposed filter approximates the filtering distribution and estimates the log-likelihood considerably more accurately than the shifted Rayleigh filter, at the cost of a higher computing time.

items.title: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{ω(n)}$
items.summary: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_ω=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{ω(n)}}, \] where \(ω(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_ω(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{ω(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization impossible: the derivative \(D_ω'(0)\) does not exist. This product therefore lies completely beyond the reach of classical regularization methods. We construct the canonical net encoding the sign sequence, define the logarithmic-prefix functional with exponent \(α=2\), and extract a finite value through the weighted evaluation functional of the monoid framework. The evaluation functional is shown to converge absolutely, and this convergence is unconditional: it follows from the classical zero-free region of \(ζ(s)\) (de la Vallée Poussin), which yields the effective bound \(T_ω(x)=O(x\,e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}})\) for some \(c>0\). Numerical computation up to \(N=10^7\) gives the regularized value \[ P_{ω,\mathrm{ren}}\approx 0.7731, \] a new constant of arithmetic origin that cannot be obtained by any classical summation method. We also compute the second derivative of the Dirichlet series at \(s=1\), \[ D_ω''(1)=8\,C_2\ln 2, \] where \(C_2\) is the Hardy--Littlewood twin prime constant, which provides an unconditional analytical link to the arithmetic structure of the sequence \((-1)^{ω(n)}\). A self-contained proof of the natural boundary, based on the Estermann--Dahlquist theorem, is given in Appendix~A.

items.title: Compact lcK manifolds with Gauduchon parallel vector fields
items.summary:
We prove that on a compact locally conformally Kähler manifold, the existence of a non-trivial parallel vector field with respect to a Gauduchon connection $
abla^t$, for $t
e  rac{1}{3}$, forces the metric to be either Vaisman (for $t=-1$), globally conformally Kähler (for $t=1$), or Kähler for all other values of $t$. As a consequence, we characterize compact Vaisman manifolds in terms of their Bismut holonomy group. Moreover, we show that in complex dimension two, the existence of a non-trivial $
abla^ rac{1}{3}$-parallel vector field forces the metric to be globally conformally Kähler.

items.title: The Method of Ellipcenters for strongly convex minimization
items.summary: This work is about ME, the Method of Ellipcenters. ME was recently introduced by these very authors as a first order accelerated scheme for unconstrained minimization. Its iterates are all centers of ellipses carefully designed to somehow capture ill-conditioning of the underlying optimization problem. In the first article on ME, we were able to prove that it converges with linear rate when the objective function is quadratic and strongly convex, while here we derive convergence for any differentiable strongly convex objective. This investigation was inspired by the great performance of ME in quadratic minimization against steepest descent with exact line search, FISTA, Barzilai-Borwein and Conjugate Gradient. The experiments we carry out now, make ME even more attractive from the numerical point of view. On top of that, the theory seems promising for quite more general settings.

items.title: Long time behavior of discrete velocity kinetic equations
items.summary: We study long time behavior of some nonlinear discrete velocity kinetic equations in the one and three dimensions with periodic boundary conditions. We prove the exponential time decay of solutions towards the global equilibrium in the $L^2$ space. Our result holds for a wide class of interaction rates including the Goldstein-Taylor and Carleman equations, and the estimates on the rate of convergence are explicit and constructive. The technique is based on the construction of suitable Lyapunov functionals by modifying Boltzmann's entropy.

items.title: Metastable confinement of particle systems near linearly stable McKean-Vlasov equilibria
items.summary: We establish a general metastability principle showing that the local stability of a McKean-Vlasov equilibrium implies exponentially long confinement of the associated particle system. Consider interacting diffusions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a general smooth and bounded interaction kernel and a globally Lipschitz drift that is dissipative at large distances. Assume the McKean-Vlasov equation has at least one equilibrium which is locally exponentially stable. We prove that the probability that the empirical measure leaves a sufficiently small fixed Wasserstein-1 neighborhood of the selected equilibrium before time $T$ is bounded by $C(1+T)e^{-cN}$, where $N$ is the number of particles and $C,c>0$ are independent of $N$ and $T$. Consequently, confinement holds up to times $e^{γN}$, for every $0<γ<c$, with exponentially small exit probability. The proof combines an explicit Volterra construction of the linearized Fokker-Planck semigroup, a mild representation of empirical fluctuations, and exponential maximal estimates for stochastic convolutions. Our approach does not require a gradient flow structure or reversibility of the equations.

items.title: Deformations of Kähler and Balanced Hyperbolicity
items.summary: We study the deformation stability of Kähler and balanced hyperbolicity. We prove that Kähler hyperbolicity is open under arbitrary small holomorphic deformations, but need not be closed, even in families of smooth projective surfaces. By contrast, balanced hyperbolicity is not open in general: in every complex dimension at least five, we construct a balanced hyperbolic central fibre with non-balanced nearby fibres. We establish criteria for the deformation stability of balanced hyperbolicity using Aeppli cohomology and Lefschetz theory. For principal holomorphic torus bundles over products of curves of genus at least two, we compute the relevant hyperbolic cohomology, obtain a numerical characterization of balanced hyperbolicity, and prove its openness under small deformations.

items.title: Sharpness of the percolation phase transition for weighted random connection models
items.summary: We establish the sharpness of the percolation phase transition for a class of potentially infinite-range weighted random connection models. The vertex set is given by a marked Poisson point process on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq 2$, with intensity $λ>0$, where each vertex carries an independent weight. Given a pair of vertices, an edge is drawn independently with a probability that depends on both their spatial displacement and their respective weights. Our geometric and moment assumptions allow the expected degree to be unbounded over the weights. We prove exponential tails for the number of vertices in the root cluster throughout the subcritical regime. We also obtain a linear lower bound on the percolation probability near criticality from above. The class of systems considered includes min-reach models, Poisson--Boolean overlap models, and suitable softened versions thereof. Our proof combines a finite-volume lattice approximation with Hutchcroft's exploration approach to the OSSS inequality.

items.title: Actions of Fell bundles, II: tensor products and Fourier-Stieltjes algebras
items.summary: In the context of Fell bundles over discrete groups, we introduce and analyze suitable notions of direct sum and tensor product of actions of Fell bundles on Hilbert bundles. For $C^*$-dynamical systems, where actions arise from equivariant representations, we discuss how the tensor product of two such actions is related to the action associated with the tensor product of the underlying equivariant representations. Likewise, since any action gives rise to a $C^*$-correspondence between the full cross-sectional $C^*$-algebras of the involved Fell bundles, we examine the connection between the $C^*$-correspondence associated with the tensor product of two given actions and the tensor product of the associated $C^*$-correspondences. We also discuss how the tensor product of actions naturally appears in Rieffel-like induction processes. Finally we present related results on the Fourier-Stieltjes and Fourier algebras of a Fell bundle.

items.title: Finding the Birman-Series set
items.summary: By a celebrated result of Birman and Series, the set of simple complete geodesics form a nowhere dense subset of a hyperbolic surface. We show that a segment of finite length is in a (small) neighborhood of this set if it can be "extended simply" in both directions for long enough. We deduce that, for large enough genus $g$, there exist surfaces with a Birman-Series set that is roughly $\frac{1}{g^{\sfrac{2}{3}}}$-dense.

items.title: The Upper Clique Transversal Problem: Hardness and Algorithms
items.summary: A clique transversal in a graph is a set of vertices intersecting all maximal cliques. The problem of determining the minimum size of a clique transversal has received considerable attention in the literature. In this paper, we initiate the study of the ''upper'' variant of this parameter, the upper clique transversal number, defined as the maximum size of a minimal clique transversal. We investigate this parameter from the algorithmic and complexity points of view, with a focus on various graph classes. We show that the corresponding decision problem is NP-complete in the classes of chordal graphs, chordal bipartite graphs, cubic planar bipartite graphs, and line graphs of bipartite graphs, but solvable in linear time in the classes of split graphs, proper interval graphs, and cographs, and in polynomial time for graphs of bounded cliquewidth. We conclude the paper with a number of open questions.

items.title: Private and Distributionally Robust Federated Multiclass Classification
items.summary: Fault diagnosis in asset-intensive industries requires multiclass models trained on noisy, sensitive data collected across geographically distributed client sites. Federated learning enables collaborative training without centralizing data, but most approaches do not provide formal privacy guarantees for individual records stored at client sites and can degrade under label noise. To address these limitations, we develop a differentially private, distributionally robust framework for federated multiclass classification that provides sample-level privacy for records stored at each client. We build on a federated Wasserstein distributionally robust multiclass objective with the Crammer-Singer loss, solved using an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based algorithm. To protect the released client updates, our method injects calibrated Gaussian noise into the proximal linearized client updates of both the local model and the local distributionally robust variable before aggregation at the central server, and we quantify the cumulative privacy loss using the moments accountant. We provide per-round sample-level $(ε,δ)$-differential privacy guarantees and an overall composed privacy guarantee across all training rounds, together with convergence results and an explicit privacy-utility tradeoff. Experiments on simulated industrial fault data and UCI benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms differentially private federated empirical risk minimization and stochastic gradient descent baselines in most tested settings, with the largest gains under strong privacy-induced noise.

items.title: Intuitionistic Linear Logic with Subexponentials: Type Theory, Categorical Models and Realisability
items.summary: In this paper, we present a typed lambda calculus ${\bf SILL}(λ)_Σ$, a type-theoretic version of multiplicative intuitionistic linear logic with subexponentials, that is, we have many comonadic resource modalities with some interconnections between them given by a subexponential signature $Σ$. We introduce the concept of a $Σ$-assemblage to characterise models of ${\bf SILL}(λ)_Σ$ by expanding the concept of a linear category where one has multiple resource comonads and symmetric lax monoidal comonad morphisms. We also generalise several known results from linear logic and show that every $Σ$-assemblage can be viewed as a symmetric monoidal closed category equipped with a family of monoidal adjunctions and morphisms by modernising and generalising Benton's results by involving the formal theory of comonads in the fashion of Street. We give a stronger 2-categorical characterisation of $Σ$-assemblages and show that the 2-category of $Σ$-assemblages 1,2-fully faithfully embeds into the 2-category of particular families of monoidal adjunctions, their left morphisms and transformations, that is, polymodal expansions of linear-non-linear models. In the final section, we describe realisability models for the particular case of a three-element subexponential signature by describing BCI algebras with extra operators viewed as applicative morphisms and assemblies over them.

items.title: An inverse spectral problem for the wave equation with a varying Robin parameter at the boundary
items.summary: An inverse spectral problem for a $(1+1)$-dimensional wave equation with wave speed $c(x)$ is considered. The spectral data consist of the eigenvalues of the Neumann--Dirichlet problem for the operator $-c^2(x)\partial_x^2$ together with their derivatives with respect to a Robin parameter at the boundary. We propose a two-step recovery procedure. In the first step, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map $Λ$ is reconstructed from the spectral data using the results of arXiv/0406582. In the second step, the reconstructed $Λ$ is used within the regularization strategy for the boundary control method presented in arXiv:1509.04478. As an improvement, the regularization of the control problems employs a weighted combination of $L^2$ and $H^1$ penalty terms, and we prove a uniform convergence result for the family of optimal controls, thereby allowing the regularization parameters to be tuned simultaneously. We also prove that the forward spectral map, which assigns to a wave speed its spectral data, is Lipschitz continuous, and that the inverse spectral map underlying the reconstruction procedure is Hölder continuous on a subclass of wave speeds. The method is implemented numerically and validated on both smooth and piecewise smooth wave speed profiles. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the recovery of the wave speed exhibits high accuracy and robustness.

items.title: A concise proof of the 8 case of Sylvester's conjecture
items.summary: The 150 years old Sylvester's conjecture asserts that every prime $p\equiv 4,7,8\mod 9$ is the sum of two rational cubes. Recently, a proof of this old problem is obtained by the work of mine for the case 4,7 \cite{Yin} and the work of Burungale-Tian for the case 8 \cite{BT}. In this paper we give a shorter proof by deep mining my result in \cite{Yin} combining with the ideas of my previous work on case 8 in \cite{Yin8}. In particular, we use the ordinary trace and the Kronecker congruence of modular functions, but do not use the $\sqrt{-3}$-division boundary and Fermat isogeny as in \cite{BT}.

items.title: Energy conserving compatible space--time FEM for deterministic and stochastic rotating shallow water
items.summary: We present a fully discrete energy conserving discretisation of the rotating shallow water equations with arbitrary order in space and time. A space time finite element discretisation is used, built from compatible finite element methods in space and continuous Petrov-Galerkin schemes in time. Projected auxiliary variables for Hamiltonian derivatives are necessary for exact energy conservation. We provide an iterative solver approach based on monolithic patch smoothers, which allows us to efficiently converge a Newton method sufficiently that energy errors due to the solver are very small. We extend this construction to the energy conserving Stochastic Forcing by Lie Transport formulation. Then we demonstrate the convergence, conservation and robustness in numerical tests.

items.title: Yet Another Family of Complex Structures on $S^6$
items.summary: Following a similar path as the recent construction of a complex structure on $S^6$ we construct another such family, disjoint from the known ones.

items.title: Global Existence of Strong and Weak Solutions to the 2D Compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson System in Bounded Domains with Large Data and Vacuum
items.summary: We study the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system in a general simply connected bounded domain with Navier-slip boundary conditions and a positive, possibly non-flat, doping profile. We establish the global existence of a unique strong solution and of a global weak solution for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum when the shear viscosity is a positive constant and the bulk one proportional to a power of the density with the power bigger than 4/3. The main difficulties arise from the interaction between the Poisson force and the general boundary geometry. To overcome them, we introduce a modified material derivative and derive quantitative $L^p$ estimates for the density by means of a Neumann duality argument together with a harmonic correction generated by the Navier-slip boundary condition. We further obtain a pointwise representation of the effective viscous flux by pulling back the Neumann Green function on the unit disk through a conformal mapping. The resulting commutator estimates, combined with elliptic estimates for the Poisson equation, yield a uniform-in-time upper bound for the density and allow us to close the higher-order a priori estimates. Finally, the global weak solution is constructed through a charge-preserving approximation and compactness argument.

items.title: Relative ($τ$), Expanders, and Decay of Correlations for certain Expanding Maps
items.summary: Relative ($τ$) is equivalent to a statement that the sequence of Cayley graphs associated to group quotients $Γ_q=Γ/N_q$, $q\in\mathbb{N}$, form an expander family. There is a philosophy that expander graphs give rise to good mixing; for instance, one has exponential mixing for the geodesic flow uniformly the along a family of congruence covers of the modular surface, stemming from the symmetry in the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ action and the uniform spectral gap for the Laplacian. Do we see similar phenomena in less structured settings? We investigate this question for a tower of finite sheeted covers of certain expanding dynamical systems. We use transfer operator machinery that applies in particular in the cases of subshifts of finite type and expanding interval maps. We make fruitful connections with KMS states of Cuntz--Krieger algebras.

items.title: Global Existence and Partial Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes System in a Half-Space
items.summary: We establish endpoint partial regularity for suitable weak solutions to the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes system with constant sensitivity and linear consumption in a half-space under no-slip and no-flux boundary conditions. The full space--time singular set, including its boundary part, has vanishing one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This follows from a Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg type criterion at the natural $r^{-1}$ dissipation scaling, valid at interior and boundary points without additional pressure smallness. The key estimate combines weighted mass control with the localized entropy--energy inequality to close the iteration without a separate $n\log n$ quantity and accounts for the mass term generated by rescaling. Boundary-compatible pressure and caloric decompositions yield local Hölder regularity. We also prove a lower-order criterion requiring smallness only of the velocity, signal gradient, and pressure oscillation, with a threshold depending on an arbitrary finite density mass bound. We construct global suitable weak solutions under natural entropy and energy assumptions without smallness restrictions on the initial data. The potential is time-independent with bounded gradient; boundedness of the potential itself is assumed only for the large-time results. If its gradient is also Hölder continuous, a solution can be selected to become bounded and classical throughout the closed half-space after a finite waiting time. For the same solution, we obtain decay and Neumann Gaussian asymptotics for both scalar components without initial spatial moment assumptions. The profile coefficients are the conserved bacterial mass and the limiting signal mass, respectively, and the latter is strictly positive whenever the initial signal is nonzero.

items.title: Fast Rates for Nonstationary Weighted Risk Minimization
items.summary: Weighted empirical risk minimization is a common approach to prediction under distribution drift. This article studies its out-of-sample prediction error under nonstationarity. We provide a general decomposition of the excess risk into a learning term and an error term associated with distribution drift, and prove oracle inequalities for the learning error under mixing conditions. The learning bound holds uniformly over arbitrary weight classes and accounts for the effective sample size induced by the weight vector, the complexity of the weight and hypothesis classes, and potential data dependence. We also analyze the drift error in the square loss setting and provide explicit bounds for structural-break and smoothly drifting processes. We then combine the learning and drift analysis in (auto-) regression problems with linear models, basis approximations, and neural networks. In all cases, the optimal weights are characterized by a bias--variance trade-off between learning and drift, while minimax-optimal rates (up to logarithmic factors) are recovered when specialized to unweighted and stationary settings.

items.title: Convergence analysis of GMRES applied to Helmholtz problems near resonances
items.summary: The finite element solution of Helmholtz problems near resonant or quasi-resonant frequencies poses significant challenges, as iterative solvers typically suffer from severely degraded convergence. We analyze the convergence behavior of GMRES applied to linear systems arising from such configurations. Theoretical convergence estimates are derived based on harmonic Ritz values, highlighting their proximity to small eigenvalues as a key determining factor. We further examine deflation strategies and their interplay with preconditioning techniques, using the Complex Shifted Laplacian preconditioner as a case study. Numerical experiments on resonant and quasi-resonant test cases validate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of deflation strategies. This study provides new insights and practical guidance for analyzing and improving iterative solvers for time-harmonic problems near resonances.

items.title: Non-resonant angles in a Robin eigenvalue problem
items.summary: In an earlier study of the Laplacian eigenvalues with strongly attractive Robin boundary conditions in polygons it was found that if each corner is either concave or non-resonant, then the asymptotic behavior of the individual eigenvalues is determined by an effective one-dimensional operator on the boundary with Dirichlet boundary conditions at the corners. The non-resonance condition was formulated in terms of an eigenvalue bound on truncated sectors, and it was only shown to be satisfied by the right and obtuse opening angles. In the present work, we determine the full range of non-resonant angles: it turns out that the non-resonance condition fails only for the opening angles $\fracπ{2n+1}$ with $n=1,2,3,\dots$, and these critical values are equivalently characterized in terms of the jumps of the eigenvalue counting function and the existence of bounded generalized eigenfunctions. This resolves the numerically supported conjecture stated by Dauge and Lafranche.

items.title: Beyond Discrepancy: Oracle Drift in Nonstationary Weighted Risk Minimization
items.summary: We analyze distributional drift in nonstationary weighted risk minimization by decomposing the excess risk into estimation, drift, and approximation components. The drift error is commonly bounded through discrepancy-type quantities that control changes of the risk over classes of predictors. We instead relate the drift error directly to the movement of the best predictor within the model class and analyze its behavior in parametrized regression models. Our analysis shows that discrepancy-type quantities can be overly conservative: unlike our oracle drift, they may scale at a larger order than the resulting excess-risk contribution and can respond to changes in the risk surface that do not affect the optimal predictor. For linear regression, we characterize this gap sharply and combine the resulting drift bounds with estimation guarantees. We further extend the analysis to nonparametric regression.

items.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
items.summary: We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $Σ_1,Σ_2,Γ$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,λ\in (0,1)$: \[ γ_{Σ_1}(K)^{1-p} γ_{Σ_2}(L)^p \le \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-λ} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}λ \right)^p \right)^{n} γ_Γ((1-λ) K + λL) , \] whenever $Γ\leq Σ_1 \sharp_p Σ_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $Σ_1,Σ_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $Σ_1 = Σ_2 = Γ$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=λ$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $λ\in [0,1]$: \[ γ(a K)^{1-λ} γ(b L)^λ \leq γ\left ( a^{1-λ} b^λ\left ((1-λ) K + λL \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.

items.title: Transfer maps in symplectic cohomology for convex symplectic domains
items.summary: We construct transfer maps in symplectic cohomology for convex symplectic domains, assuming that the complement of a subdomain is exact. The construction uses an action filtration by Reeb periods, inspired by that of McLean--Ritter. The transfer maps yield the invariance of symplectic cohomology under subcritical handle attachment to convex symplectic domains. As an application, we obtain infinitely many exotic convex symplectic structures on certain domains via McLean's exotic Stein balls.

items.title: The conformal Poisson embedding method for the anisotropic Calderón problem with a potential
items.summary: We prove that the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of $Δ_g+q$ determines a compact connected real-analytic Riemannian manifold of dimension at least three and a real-analytic real-valued potential, up to a diffeomorphism fixing the observed boundary and the conformal gauge of the equation. The result is new even when \(q\) is constant, i.e. for the fixed-frequency (Helmholtz) equation \(Δ_g u+λu=0\). The measurements are restricted to an arbitrary nonempty open boundary set $Γ$. The proof develops conformal Poisson embeddings method and uses coordinates given by quotients of solutions.

items.title: Preconditioning proximal Galerkin: mesh and degree robust solvers for variational inequalities
items.summary: The proximal Galerkin algorithm is a structure-preserving solver for variational inequalities that results in discretization-independent nonlinear iteration counts. However, in large three-dimensional simulations, the arising Newton saddle point systems cannot be feasibly solved by direct methods. To leverage an iterative linear solver, we propose a robust and scalable block preconditioner. Instead of using the usual dual Schur complement that acts on the latent variable, we design a preconditioner for the primal Schur complement. This leads to a block preconditioner that requires two approximate inverses of the latent block and only one of the primal Schur complement. The latent block represents an algebraic equation which, after a small perturbation, can be cheaply inverted. We then introduce two choices of approximations for the primal Schur complement: a PDE-operator-based and an algebraic approach. Either approximation can be efficiently inverted by geometric multigrid. We investigate the effectiveness of these strategies when proximal Galerkin is applied to obstacle, Signorini, and strain-constrained elasticity problems and also compare with a monolithic multigrid approach. Choices of standard relaxation methods, in the block preconditioner route, lead to robust iteration counts with respect to the mesh size and discretization degree. Moreover, in the context of the Signorini, specialized relaxation and prolongation also result in effective solvers for nearly-incompressible elastic materials. The linear solves are parameter-robust in 2D, with only mild growth in 3D. This allows for the solution of a three-dimensional contact problem, with a Poisson's ratio of 0.499, discretized with over ten million degrees of freedom.

items.title: Lower Bounds for Randomized Linear-Oracle Optimization over Strongly Convex Sets
items.summary: Recent results [arXiv:2602.04378, arXiv:2602.22608] have established worst-case objective-error lower bounds of order $1/T^2$ after $T$ linear minimization oracle (LMO) calls, matching the upper bound [arXiv:1406.1305] in its dependence on $T$ and thereby resolving a long-standing open question. Upon close inspection, however, both lower bounds are somewhat brittle. The first [arXiv:2602.04378] applies only to the standard Frank--Wolfe algorithm, and, as we show, its prescribed slow exact-line-search trajectories can amplify sufficiently small initialization errors exponentially, corresponding to roughly one additional bit of initialization accuracy per iteration. The second [arXiv:2602.22608] obtains lower bounds for any deterministic LMO-based first-order method via a resisting oracle that adversarially adapts to the queries of the algorithm. In both cases it is conceivable that randomization may circumvent these lower bounds; in particular, neither establishes a lower bound for unrestricted randomized first-order LMO methods. We close this gap by proving an $Ω(L\operatorname{diam}(S)^2/T^2)$ distributional lower bound for randomized first-order linear minimization oracle methods over strongly convex sets. While our construction reuses the family of [arXiv:2602.22608], our proof characterizes the conditional distribution of the hidden permutation after adaptive queries and bounds the expected decrease of a combinatorial statistic controlling optimizer variance. We further show that the same error threshold holds with probability at least $3/4$ and yields a stopping-time tail bound.

items.title: On the Cohomology Classes of Certain Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
items.summary: We study the de Rham cohomology and Deligne splitting for a class of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms by introducing a modular weight grading. As an application, we compute a particular cohomology class that gives rise to generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves.

items.title: Exact and extremal values of chromatic villainy
items.summary: Chromatic villainy measures the largest number of vertices that must change color to repair a rearrangement of an optimal coloring while preserving every color multiplicity. Weak villainy allows different multiplicities in the repair. On the odd cycle $C_{2r+1}$, we determine the largest repair distance from arbitrary color assignments with a prescribed color-count vector (profile) $\mathbf m$ to proper colorings with any realizable target profile $\mathbf p$: it equals $2r+1-\sum_X\min\{p_X,\lceil m_X/2\rceil\}$. In particular, every feasible profile $(a,b,c)$ has ordinary and weak repair radius $\lfloor a/2\rfloor+\lfloor b/2\rfloor+\lfloor c/2\rfloor$, and $B(C_{2r+1})=r$ for $r\ge2$, answering a question of Clark et al. For arbitrary complete multipartite graphs, we give an arithmetic formula for ordinary villainy with at most $k^2$ candidates and an exact finite formula for weak villainy, where $k$ is the number of parts. Both values are fixed-parameter tractable in $k$ for binary-encoded part sizes. We also determine the maximum of each parameter among all $n$-vertex $k$-chromatic graphs. For $k\ge3$, the ordinary maximum is $\min\{n,4(n-k)\}$, except when $n=4(n-k)-1$ or $(n,k)\in\{(5,3),(7,3)\}$, when it is $n-1$. For $k\ge2$, the weak maximum is $n-\max\{\lceil n/k\rceil,2k-n\}-\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$ is determined explicitly by $n$ and $k$. Both extrema are attained by complete multipartite graphs, and a weak extremizer needs at most three distinct part sizes.

items.title: A Unifying Framework for Global Optimization: From Theory to Formalization
items.summary: We introduce an abstract measure___theoretic framework that serves as a tool to rigorously study stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms as a unified class. The framework is formulated in terms of probability kernels, which, via the Ionescu--Tulcea theorem, induce probability measures on the space of sequences of algorithm iterations, endowed with two intuitive properties. This framework answers the need for a general, implementation___independent formalism in the analysis of such algorithms, providing a starting point for formalizing global optimization results in proof-assistants. To illustrate the relevance of our tool, we show that common algorithms fit naturally in the framework, and we also use it to give a rigorous proof of a general consistency theorem for stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms (Proposition 3 of (Malherbe, et al., 2017). This proof and the entire framework are formalized in the Lean proof assistant. This formalization both ensures the correctness of the definitions and proofs, and provides a basis for future machine-assisted formalizations in the field.

items.title: Boundary stabilization of multi-dimensional first-order quasilinear hyperbolic systems
items.summary: We study the long-time behaviour of multi-dimensional first-order symmetrizable quasilinear hyperbolic systems with nonlinear feedback boundary conditions. Assuming strict interior and boundary Lyapunov inequalities for the linearized system and non-characteristic boundaries, we prove global existence for small initial data and exponential H^s decay, with s>d/2+1 an integer. We consider both bounded smooth domains and flat periodic cylinders, and illustrate the results with physical examples and numerical simulations.

items.title: Finite type invariants in low degrees and the Johnson filtration
items.summary: We study the behaviour of the Casson invariant $λ$, its square, and Othsuki's second invariant $λ_2$ as functions on the Johnson subgroup of the mapping class group. We show that since $λ$ and $d_2 = λ_2 - 18 λ^2$ are invariants that are morphisms on respectively the second and the third level of the Johnson filtration they never vanish on any level of this filtration. In contrast we prove that the invariant $λ_2-18λ^2 +3λ$ vanishes on the fifth level of the Johnson filtration, $\mathcal{M}_{g,1}(5)$, and as a consequence we prove that, for instance, the Poincaré homology sphere does not admit any Heegaard splitting with gluing map an element in $\mathcal{M}_{g,1}(5)$. Finally we determine a surgery formula for Othsuki's second invariant $λ_2$.

items.title: Appell Sequences in Analytic Number Theory: Shifted Expansions and Dirichlet L-Functions
items.summary: We place the Appell shift theorem for asymptotic expansions inside a Borel--Laplace framework and apply it to two classical functions of analytic number theory: the Hurwitz zeta function \(ζ(m,q)\) and the Lerch transcendent \(Φ(z,m,a)\). The resulting shifted expansions have coefficients given by Appell polynomials evaluated at the shift, with remainders controlled uniformly on compact sets. The generating sequences are identified explicitly in terms of the Taylor coefficients of the Borel kernels. In a second direction, we extend the Appell--Mellin framework of Navas, Ruiz and Varona to Dirichlet \(L\)-functions. For a primitive non-principal character \(χ\) modulo \(q\), we construct an explicit Appell--Mellin generating function \(A_χ(t)\) whose associated Appell sequence satisfies \(R_n^χ(x) = L(-n,χ,x)\), and we prove the functional equation \(A_χ(t) = χ(-1)A_χ(-t)\). We further establish five structural properties of the polynomials \(R_n^χ\): identification with generalized Bernoulli polynomials, a difference equation, an explicit formula, a Fourier expansion, and the trivial zeros of \(L(s,χ)\). To the best of our knowledge, these results do not appear in the literature.

items.title: An infinite-dimensional representation of Ray-Knight theorems for the Bass-Burdzy flow
items.summary: [Bass and Burdzy 1999] introduced a stochastic flow of homeomorphisms of the real line $\mathcal R_t:x\mapsto \mathcal R_t(x)$, driven by a Brownian motion. Ray-Knight theorems for the process $\mathcal R_t^{-1}(0)$ were later obtained by [Hu and Warren 2000]. We extend their results by proving an integral representation driven by a common white noise for the local times of $\mathcal R_t^{-1}(0)$, in analogy with the case of the standard Ray-Knight theorems [Aïdékon, Hu and Shi 2024]. We generalize this representation to the setting of a Bass-Burdzy flow driven by a drifted Brownian motion perturbed at its maximum, and use this framework to answer a question of [Aïdékon, Hu and Shi 2026] concerning the description of the conditional law of a perturbed reflecting Brownian motion given its occupation measure in terms of Bass-Burdzy flows.

items.title: Identifying secondary critical mass levels in two- and higher-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
items.summary: The parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} u_t = Δu - \nabla \cdot (u\nabla v), \\[1mm] 0 = Δv - μ+ u, \qquad μ:=\frac{1}{|Ω|} \int_Ωu, \end{array} \right. \qquad \qquad (\star) \] is considered under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions in the ball $Ω=B_R(0)\subset {\mathbb R}^n$, where $n\ge 2$ and $R>0$. The main results identify a mass level $m_\star(n,R)>0$ as critical in the sense that $\bullet$ whenever $0<m<m_\star(n,R)$, the constant equilibrium of ($\star$) given by $u\equiv v\equiv \frac{m}{|B_R|}$ is locally asymptotically stable with respect to the norm in $L^\infty(B_R)$, but that $\bullet$ if $m>m_\star(n,R)$, then any solution of ($\star$) emanating from nonnegative and nonconstant continuous radial initial data $u_0$ with $\int_{B_R} u_0=m$ and $\frac{1}{|B_r|} \int_{B_r} u_0 \ge \frac{m}{|B_R|}$ for all $r\in (0,R)$ blows up in finite time. The value of $m_\star(n,R)$ can be determined in an essentially explicit manner in dependence on principal zeroes of appropriate Bessel functions of the first kind; in particular, $m_\star(2,R)\approx 14.68197 \cdot π$ for all $R>0$. Accordingly, as a supplement to known mass-dependent blow-up dichotomies these findings reveal a genuinely secondary critical mass phenomenon for ($\star$) especially also in its two-dimensional version in which no precedent of this form seems known.

items.title: High order integration of stochastic dynamics on Riemannian manifolds with frozen flow methods
items.summary: We present a new class of numerical methods for solving stochastic differential equations with additive noise on general Riemannian manifolds with high weak order of accuracy. In opposition to the popular approach with projection methods, the proposed methods are intrinsic: they only rely on geometric operations and avoid coordinates and embeddings. We provide a robust and general convergence analysis and an algebraic formalism of exotic planar Butcher series for the computation of order conditions at any high order. To illustrate the methodology, an explicit method of second weak order is introduced, and several numerical experiments confirm the theoretical findings and extend the approach for the sampling of the invariant measure of Riemannian Langevin dynamics.

items.title: $\mathcal{P}(Φ)_2$ Theory from many-body quantum Gibbs states
items.summary: We derive the $\mathcal{P}(Φ)_2$ measure on the two-dimensional unit torus as the rigorous limit of many-body quantum Gibbs states. In particular, the quantum model corresponding to the $Φ^{2p}_2$ measure is formulated in the grand-canonical ensemble with a general symmetric $p$-body interaction potential which is not required to have a factorized form. Unlike in the $Φ^4_2$ case investigated by Fröhlich--Knowles--Schlein--Sohinger in \cite{FKSS25}, in the treatment of higher-order interactions, Wick renormalization generates a full hierarchy of lower-order interactions which we organize systematically using a graphical formalism. One key ingredient of our analysis is a logarithmic stability estimate for both the nonlocal Hartree functional and the many-body Hamiltonian that is uniform in the interaction range, allowing us to use the positivity of the leading $p$-body interaction to control all lower-order terms generated by the Wick counterterms.

items.title: Disjoint unions and fixed-parameter algorithms for chromatic villainy
items.summary: Chromatic villainy is the maximum, over rearrangements of optimal graph colorings, of the minimum Hamming distance to a proper coloring with the same color multiplicities. Weak villainy allows the repair to change these multiplicities. We give exact composition laws for disjoint unions and determine the eventual growth under repetition. Write $mG$ for the disjoint union of $m$ copies of $G$. For every graph $G$, with $k=χ(G)$, weak villainy satisfies $B_{\mathrm w}(mG)=mF_k(G)$ whenever $k\mid m$, where $F_k(G)$ is the maximum distance to a proper $k$-coloring over all assignments of $k$ color labels to vertices. Its bounded defect from $mF_k(G)$ is eventually periodic; we give an explicit stabilization bound and identify the least period, which divides $k$. For ordinary villainy, we obtain a computable rational slope $Λ(G)\ge F_k(G)$ such that $B(mG)=mΛ(G)+O_G(1)$, where the error is bounded independently of $m$ and eventually periodic, with a computable period and threshold. Consequently the difference between the two values is bounded exactly when $Λ(G)=F_k(G)$, and otherwise grows linearly. The slope is determined by a finite optimization using at most $k$ source assignments. We also answer the unrestricted superadditivity questions negatively: for every $C>0$, a connected graph can lose more than $C$ in weak villainy after union with a triangle, and some connected $3$-chromatic graph $G$ satisfies $B(G\sqcup G)<2B(G)-C$. Finally, both exact values on an $n$-vertex graph can be computed in time $f(B_{\mathrm w}(G))(n+1)^{O(1)}$, without either value being supplied. Threshold recognition is fixed-parameter tractable as well.

items.title: Strict Hausdorff-dimension drop for Quartic Salem Bernoulli convolutions
items.summary: For every quartic Salem number $β$, we prove that the equal-weight Bernoulli convolution $ν_{β^{-1}}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than one. The main step converts large Fourier coefficients at geometrically separated frequencies into a deficit in the Shannon entropy of a finite convolution. A positive trigonometric product gives the entropy estimate, while the algebraic norm controls the number of distinct atoms in each spatial cell. For the two quartic Salem numbers in $(1,2)$, reciprocal differences at suitable return times produce the required Fourier coefficients. A finite block cover then gives the dimension bound. This proof is independent of numerical computation. Separate exact calculations give $\dimHν_{β_1^{-1}}<1-1.4\cdot10^{-23}$ and $\dimHν_{β_2^{-1}}<1-7.8\cdot10^{-22}$, where $β_1<β_2$ are the two parameters in $(1,2)$. The accompanying verification programs use rational interval arithmetic and the Python standard library.

items.title: Infinitesimal Operator World Models: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Offline Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Continuous-time stochastic processes underlie many natural and engineered systems. In healthcare, autonomous driving, and industrial control, direct interaction with the environment is often unsafe or impractical, motivating offline reinforcement learning from historical data. However, there is limited statistical understanding of the approximation errors inherent in learning policies from offline datasets. We address this by linking reinforcement learning to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation and proposing an operator-theoretic algorithm based on a simple dynamic programming recursion. Specifically, we represent our world model in terms of the infinitesimal generator of controlled diffusion processes learned in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. By integrating statistical learning methods and operator theory, we establish global convergence of the value function under sufficiently small generator-approximation error and derive explicit finite-sample guarantees with bounds tied directly to system properties such as smoothness and stability. Our theoretical and proof-of-concept results indicate that operator-based approaches may hold promise for solving offline reinforcement learning using continuous-time optimal control.

items.title: Spectral Theory and Descriptive Combinatorics for Non-Regular Borel pmp Graphs
items.summary: We continue the systematic study initiated in arXiv:2602.05185 of the relationship between the spectral theory and descriptive combinatorics of bounded-degree Borel pmp graphs, particularly in the non-regular setting. We first adapt a classical result of Nikiforov to give a new spectral lower bound on the approximate measurable chromatic number. For certain non-regular graphs, this bound improves on the approximate measurable version of Hoffman's classical bound established in arXiv:2602.05185. Next, we strengthen a characterization in arXiv:2602.05185 of approximate measurable bipartiteness in terms of the spectrum of the adjacency operator by generalizing to the case of non-regular graphs. Finally, we introduce the measurable domination number and adapt several classical results of Lu, Liu, and Tian to give a bound on the spectral gap of the Laplacian operator in terms of the measurable domination number.

items.title: AI and humanity's long conversation
items.summary: These are notes to accompany my public lecture at the International Congress of Mathematicians, in Philadelphia in July, 2026. The goal is to discuss some developments at the interface of AI and mathematics in the context of the long conversation of mathematics.

items.title: Stationary Ergodic Mean-field Games of Constrained Singular Controls
items.summary: We study a stationary ergodic mean-field game of scalar type where the representative player controls a diffusion through two-sided singular controls exerted only at the jump times of an independent Poisson process. For each mean-field parameter, we solve the novel constrained ergodic singular control problem, proving that the optimal policy is of threshold type: the diffusion is reset at Poisson arrival times to the nearest boundary point of an interval. Our explicit probabilistic derivation of the stationary distributions induced by Poissonian threshold singular controls is a key contribution of independent interest. This distribution is used to construct the mean-field fixed-point map. We prove existence and uniqueness of the stationary mean-field equilibrium by combining the stationary density with the monotonicity and continuity of the optimal thresholds in the mean-field parameter. The model provides a tractable framework for a case study of partially reversible investment with singular adjustments under exogenous intervention constraints.

items.title: Learning to accelerate Krasnosel'skii-Mann fixed-point iterations with guarantees
items.summary: We introduce a principled learning to optimize (L2O) framework for solving fixed-point problems involving general nonexpansive mappings. Our idea is to deliberately inject summable perturbations into a standard Krasnosel'skii-Mann iteration to improve its average-case performance over a specific distribution of problems while retaining its convergence guarantees. Under a metric sub-regularity assumption, we prove that the proposed parametrization includes only iterations that locally achieve linear convergence-up to a vanishing bias term-and that it encompasses all iterations that do so at a sufficiently fast rate. We then demonstrate how our framework can be used to augment several widely-used operator splitting methods to accelerate the solution of structured monotone inclusion problems, and validate our approach on a best approximation problem using an L2O-augmented Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm.

items.title: Analysis and Detection of Stagnation in Floating-Point Summation
items.summary: Stagnation in the summation of floating-point numbers occurs when the running sum, or the accumulator, does not change its value despite addends being greater than zero. Here we define different types of stagnation - commonly referred to as swamping or absorption, where one operand in an addition is nearly or completely rounded off---in floating-point summation, and propose algorithms for detecting it in numerical code that uses floating-point arithmetic. Whilst cancellation in floating-point arithmetic has been studied, for example by Lam et al. in `Dynamic floating point cancellation detection', stagnation has not been exploited as a property for detecting and reporting accuracy loss in floating-point operations. We have built prototype dynamic stagnation detection tools in two languages, MATLAB and Julia, and applied them to applications ranging from basic summation of a vector, to matrix multiplication, to a fluid flow simulation model. With this tool, users are able to identify areas of their floating-point code where stagnation occurs - in those areas of the code one may need to switch to a higher precision number format, apply stochastic rounding, or use different summation algorithms such as compensated summation. To the best of our knowledge we provide a first rigorous definition of stagnation in floating-point summation.

items.title: Forcing and cardinal invariants of universally null sets
items.summary: We study universally null sets in forcing extensions and the cardinal invariants of their ideal $\mathcal{UN}$. We prove that the Miller model contains a nonmeager universally null set of cardinality $\aleph_2=\mathfrak{c}$, answering a question of Brendle and Larson. The proof uses preservation of universal nullity by countable support iterations of Miller forcing and shows that the set of Miller reals added during the iteration is universally null. We also prove that every universally null set in the $\mathbb{PT}_{f,g}$ model has cardinality at most $\aleph_1$, and show that there is consistently a forcing destructible universally null set. For the cardinal invariants, we show that $|X|<\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{UN})$ for every $X\in\mathcal{UN}$, and that $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal{N})=\mathfrak{c}$ implies $\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{UN})=\mathfrak{d}_{\mathfrak{c}}$. Finally, we prove the consistency of $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal{UN})<\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{UN}) <\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{UN})<\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{UN})$.

items.title: On a maximum principle in discretization with spherical harmonics
items.summary: Spherical harmonics have been studied extensively and are used in many fields of application. We consider the probably earliest application of spherical harmonics, namely for a representation of the solution of the Laplace equation on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere where the boundary data are represented in a spherical harmonics basis. We consider general $d \geq 2$. For the solution $u$ of the Laplace equation the fundamental maximum principle holds. If one approximates the boundary data in the finite dimensional space spanned by all spherical harmonics of degree at most $N$, the resulting discrete solution, denoted by $u_N$, does in general not satisfy the maximum principle. In this paper we derive sharp estimates for $r_N^{\rm max}$ such that the maximum principle holds for $u_N(x)$ for all $x \in \Bbb{R}^d$ with $\|x\| \leq r_N^{\rm max}$. We show that for $d=3$ one has $r_N^{\rm max} \gtrsim 1- 3 N^{-1} \ln\big( 2^\frac13 N \big) $. Similar estimates are derived for $d \neq 3$. We also study the sharpness of these estimates.

items.title: Hölder regularity of solutions to parabolic equations associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators
items.summary: In this paper, we study Hölder regularity of local weak super-solutions to the parabolic equation associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators $$ \partial_t u(t,x)-\text{p.v.}\int_{\R^d}|u(t,y)-u(t,x)|^{p-2}(u(t,y)-u(t,x))J(t;x,y)\,dy=0,\quad (t,x)\in \R\times \R^d, $$ where $\text{p.v.}$ denotes the principal value, $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the kernel $J(t;x,y)$ is comparable (uniformly with respect to $(t;x,y)\in\R\times\R^d\times\R^d$) to the fractional $p$-Laplacian kernel $|x-y|^{-d-sp}$ with $s\in(0,1)$. Our contribution extends the fundamental work of Kassmann and Weidner to the nonlinear case $p\ne 2$. In particular, we provide an explicit nonlocal parabolic tail condition in terms of an $L^{1+\varepsilon}$-norm in the time variable (for a suitable $\varepsilon>0$) for all $p\in(1,\infty)$, under which Hölder regularity holds. Our proof is based on the method of expansion of positivity, which is the key ingredient in the reduction-of-oscillation argument.

items.title: Isoparametric Hypersurfaces of $\mathbb H^n\times\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R$
items.summary: We classify the isoparametric hypersurfaces and the homogeneous hypersurfaces of $\mathbb H^n\times\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R$, $n\ge 2$, by establishing that any such hypersurface has constant angle function and constant principal curvatures.

items.title: Hsiang cubics as spherical Chebyshev polynomials: equioscillation and idempotent quadrature
items.summary: A Hsiang cubic is a cubic form on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose zero set is a minimal cone; equivalently, it is the cubic form of a commutative nonassociative metrized algebra satisfying a single identity of degree four. We show that the intrinsic geometry of such an algebra, encoded in its idempotents and their Peirce decompositions, is the geometry of a Chebyshev-type extremal problem on the sphere. A Hsiang cubic equioscillates on $S^{n-1}$: its maximum set is the set of normalized idempotents, and on suitable great circles through an idempotent it restricts to the Chebyshev polynomial $T_3$. For the spherical analogue of the problem of least deviation, the minimization of $\|p\|_\infty^2/\|p\|_2^2$ over harmonic cubics, a sharp lower bound based on Kellogg's inequality shows that Cartan's isoparametric cubics are the global minimizers in dimensions $5$, $8$, $14$ and $26$. In general, we compute the ratio of every Hsiang cubic in terms of the Killing form and characterize stationarity by a Kolmogorov criterion: it amounts to a positive measure on the idempotent variety. Such measures are given explicitly in several cases which together cover every Hsiang cubic known to exist; in particular, all of them are stationary.
