These measures give quadrature identities on the idempotent variety whose moments are invariants of the algebra; they are spherical designs exactly in the Einstein (Killing metrized) case, i.e.\ when the Killing form is proportional to the inner product. Distinguished low-dimensional Hsiang cubics are strict local minimizers, whereas a polar Hsiang cubic is a stationary non-minimizer.

items.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
items.summary: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.

items.title: Quadratic-size Random Permutations are Universal
items.summary: A permutation is $n$-universal if it contains every permutation of length $n$ as a pattern. We prove that a uniformly random permutation of length $32n^2$ is $n$-universal with probability at least $1-\exp(-c n/\log n)$, for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$. This removes a $\log\log n$ factor from an earlier result of He and Kwan~\cite{He-Kwan} and resolves an open problem of Alon~\cite{Alon2016}. The proof was found by GPT-6 Pro.

items.title: Campana strong approximation on generalised Markoff surfaces
items.summary: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.

items.title: On the Kantorovich contraction of Markov semigroups
items.summary: We develop an operator-theoretic framework for the contraction properties of Markov semigroups with respect to a general class of Kantorovich semi-distances, which includes Wasserstein distances and weighted total variation norms. The framework is based on Kantorovich contraction coefficients, which extend Dobrushin's ergodic coefficient from the total variation distance to general transport costs. Our main result shows that a geometric drift condition, combined with a local contraction condition on the sub-level sets of the Lyapunov function, implies that the Markov operator is a strict contraction with respect to an explicit modification of the underlying Kantorovich cost. This yields, in a unified way, the existence and uniqueness of invariant measures and exponential decay estimates in Wasserstein distances, for both discrete time and continuous time Markov semigroups, as well as for time-varying semigroups. We illustrate the scope of the framework with (i) Markov transitions on models with boundary states, including bounded domains with entrance boundaries, (ii) operator products of a Markov kernel and its adjoint, including two-block Gibbs samplers, (iii) iterated random functions, including Euler-type schemes, (iv) diffusion models, including overdamped Langevin diffusions with potentials that are convex at infinity, jump-diffusions on compact manifolds, and Jacobi and Riccati matrix diffusions, and (v) time-varying and nonlinear semigroups, including Feynman-Kac distribution flows and Sinkhorn bridges. In several of these settings we obtain new contraction estimates, while in others we recover known results through short and elementary arguments.

items.title: A Lower Bound for the First Non-zero Basic Eigenvalue on a Singular Riemannian Foliation
items.summary: In the paper, we provide a lower bound of the first non-zero basic eigenvalue on a closed singular Riemannian manifold $(M^n,\mathcal{F})$ having basic mean curvature that depends on the given lower bound of the Ricci curvature $Ric(M)\geq (n-1)K$ and the diameter of the leaf space $d_{M/\mathcal{F}}$. For foliations given by points, the results cover estimates of the first non-zero eigenvalues lower bounds, which are Zhong-Yang estimate, Yang estimate and Shi-Yang estimate. We also show a rigidity result that corresponds to the case of $Ric(M)\geq 0$. This is a generalization of Hang-Wang rigidity, which is the equality case of Zhong-Yang estimate.

items.title: Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians
items.summary: This paper gives a survey of propositional modal logic in an intuitionistic setting. Mainly intended for readers already familiar with classical modal logic, we discuss why there are two prominent families of such logics, intuitionistic modal logics (IMLs) and constructive modal logics (CMLs), what motivates their study, and how they compare with each other. We then take a look at the logics lying between the CML and IML traditions, and survey various extensions and $\Diamond$/$\Box$-free fragments. We further record several observations which seem to be implicit or absent in the literature; we point out a small defect in the original semantics for $\textbf{CK}$ and prove Lyndon interpolation theorems for $\textbf{CK}$ and $\textbf{WK}$.

items.title: A strict amplitude lower bound for the van der Pol equation and extensions to symmetric Liénard systems
items.summary: We prove that the amplitude of the unique limit cycle of the van der Pol equation $\ddot{x}+μ(x^2-1)\dot{x}+x=0$ is strictly greater than $2$ for every $μ>0$. The proof combines orbit comparison in the relaxation oscillation regime, trigonometric comparison curves in the weakly nonlinear regime, and polynomial energy estimates in the intermediate regime. The polynomial sign conditions arising in the latter two regimes are certified using exact rational arithmetic and Bernstein coefficients. The orbit comparison method also applies to a class of symmetric Liénard systems. Under suitable monotonicity assumptions, we establish a sufficient criterion for the limit cycle amplitude to exceed a critical value determined by the damping function.

items.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Discrete-Time Self-Attention Dynamics in Transformers
items.summary: In machine learning, a self-attention dynamics describes the attention mechanism of transformers, and is obtained treating the layer index of a transformer as time index. Even though naturally discrete-time, this dynamical system is most often studied in continuous-time. Scope of this paper is to provide a thorough investigation of the discrete-time version of the self-attention dynamics: a complete classification of its equilibria is given, and their stability properties are studied, in both the single-head and the multihead case. We show that in both cases the main attractor of the dynamics is a consensus equilibrium aligned with the principal eigenvector of the value matrix (in the single-head case, a corresponding matrix of weights in the multihead case), even though other locally asymptotically stable bipartite equilibria can be show to exist at least in the single-head situation. The behavior is confirmed by looking at the learned weight matrices of a real transformer.

items.title: On the weak invariance principle for strictly stationary sequences in some Besov spaces
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate the weak invariance principle in some Besov spaces for strictly stationary sequences. In particular, we provide sufficient conditions on the moments and the dependence of a strictly stationary sequence to guaranty the weak invariance principle in these Besov spaces. Several dependence structures are considered, including projective conditions, $α$-dependent, $ρ$-mixing, and $τ$ -dependent conditions. The main tools in the proofs are martingale approximation and deviation inequalities for weakly dependent sequences. Our results cover a large range of strictly stationary sequences that were not treated previously in the literature. Moreover, the presented conditions are sharp.

items.title: Short scale asymptotics in nonlocal spectral problems
items.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of nonlocal convolution-type operators $$L_\varepsilonρ=-\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{d}}\int_ΩJ\left({\frac{|x-y|^2}{\varepsilon^2}}\right)ρ(y)dy+a(x)ρ(x),$$ (with a continuous sufficiently fast decaying at infinity function $J\geq 0$) when the scaling parameter $\varepsilon>0$ tends to zero. Assuming that the minimum of the function $a(x)$ is attained at a point $x_0\in \overlineΩ\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and is non-degenerate, we establish several terms in the asymptotic expansion of the first eigenvalues $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}$ of $L_\varepsilon$. If $x_0$ is an interior point of the domain $Ω$, we show that $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilonμ^{(k)}+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$, where $μ^{(k)}$ are eigenvalues of a harmonic oscillator (obtained by the blow up analysis), the corresponding eigenfunctions of $\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon$ are concentrated near $x_0$ on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$. If $x_0\in\partial Ω$ then the asymptotic expansion of the eigenvalues of $L_\varepsilon$ has the form $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilon^{2/3}Λ_0+\varepsilon(μ^{(k)}+αp_0)+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$. The corresponding eigenfunctions are represented as the product of a function depending on the distance to $\partialΩ$ and concentrated on the scale $\varepsilon^{2/3}$, and functions localized on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ and asymptotically independent of the distance to $\partialΩ$. The latter functions converge (after rescaling) to eigenfunctions of a harmonic oscillator (in tangential variables), $μ^{(k)}$ being their eigenvalues. The former function is given, to the leading term, by the scaled Airy function, and $Λ_0$, $α$ and $p_0$ depend on $J(|x|^2)$ and $a(x)$.

items.title: Compactly supported instability of Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metrics
items.summary: On the Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metric of dimension $n\geq 4$, we show that the destabilizing TT tensor of Ozuch lies in the image of the ``TT-tensor machine''. By continuity, it can then be approximated, in suitable weighted Sobolev spaces, by smooth compactly supported TT tensors, on which the stability quadratic form is still negative. This proves instability in the usual sense for noncompact manifolds. To our knowledge, no exact smooth compactly supported destabilizing TT tensor was known before, even in 4D.

items.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
items.summary: Semi-Markov networks provide a natural framework for describing stochastic transitions between coarse-grained states with non-exponential dwell times, with applications ranging from biophysics and neuroscience to epidemiology and finance. Here, it is shown that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph. These representations yield asymptotic results, including a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem to semi-Markov networks, in which the rate constants replaced by pseudo-rates given by the inverse mean sojourn time weighted by the exit probability through this channel, as well as the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short proof of the constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to show that weak ergodicity breaking occurs generically for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks.

items.title: Blocking of bistable front propagation: Application to Wolbachia population replacement
items.summary: In order to control epidemics of mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue, for which there is still no vaccine available, several strategies aim to directly target the mosquito population. One technique involves introducing a symbiotic bacterium called Wolbachia into the population, which blocks the transmission of pathogens. A mathematical model of the introduction of this bacterium and the replacement of the mosquito population with a population carrying this bacterium has been developed, proving that in a homogeneous environment, there is spatial propagation of the replacement. The objective of this paper is to study the blocking of this propagation in cases where the environment is not homogeneous. In particular, we are considering scenarios where the environmental carrying capacity varies significantly across different regions of the spatial domain. To achieve this objective, we first reduce the original 2x2 reaction-diffusion system to a single closed equation, providing a simplified framework for studying the dynamics of Wolbachia propagation. We then investigate the blocking of the propagation in the population replacement process, focusing on the effects of spatial variations in the environmental carrying capacity. Numerical simulations have been performed to validate the theoretical results.

items.title: Efficient quadratic entropy with distance sketches
items.summary: We detail scalable methods for approximating the quadratic entropy $p^T d p$ for arbitrary distributions $p$ and common distances $d$ of negative type. We focus on the Euclidean and spherical geodesic cases, which both use random feature embeddings and projections to dramatically improve computational complexity within a simple framework. Amortization of a single large matrix multiplication and control variates further enable computation at large scale with low memory and runtime in situations where $d$ is held constant while $p$ varies. We demonstrate this with a comparison against direct pair sampling and bibliometric/scientometric examples on Open Graph Benchmark datasets, revealing papers, fields, and institutions with both particularly narrow and broad interdisciplinary reach from their citations and text features alone.

items.title: Quasinormal and hyponormal operators in the $β(H)$-class
items.summary: Following \cite{BR} we study hyponormal operators in the strictly larger class $β(H)$ of operators whose restriction to every non-zero reducing subspace is norm attaining. The Weyl-type characterization of positive operators via the essential spectrum used in the absolutely norm attaining case is replaced by a well-ordering condition on the eigenvalues (Theorem~\ref{thm:positive}). We prove a transfinite, block-diagonal representation $T=\bigoplus_iλ_iS_i$ (with isometries $S_i$) for the $β(H)$-operators whose $|T|$-eigenspaces are reducing, equivalently the quasinormal operators with $|T|\inβ(H)$, and we show by examples that hyponormality alone does not give such a decomposition. For normal operators we obtain a complete representation, and for hyponormal $β(H)$-operators we show that normality is equivalent to the spectrum having planar Lebesgue measure zero. An analogous area-zero criterion for normality is proved for hyponormal operators attaining the minimum modulus on every non-zero reducing subspace.

items.title: Estimating ratio of variance components in a balanced one-way random effect model
items.summary: This paper considers the problem of estimating the ratio of variance components of a balanced one-way random effects model. Existing estimators of ratio of variance, such as the ANOVA and maximum likelihood estimators, can take negative values and are inadmissible under quadratic loss. We therefore study the problem under a general class of scale-invariant loss functions. We characterize the class of scale-equivariant estimators of ratio of variance and obtain the best equivariant estimator. We then derive a class of estimators that dominate the BEE and extend this class to obtain further improved estimators. We propose a smooth improved estimator of ratio of variance. For interval estimation of ratio of variance, we derive an asymptotic confidence interval, bootstrap confidence intervals, a generalized confidence interval and a highest posterior density credible interval. The performance of the proposed improved point estimators and confidence interval procedures is assessed through an extensive simulation study. Finally, we provide a real data analysis for implementation purposes.

items.title: A simple algorithm for computing Hamilton paths on independent set polytopes
items.summary: The independent set polytope, or stable set polytope, of a graph $G$ is the 0/1-polytope defined by the convex hull of the characteristic vectors of all independent sets of $G$. We present a simple algorithm for computing a Hamilton path on the independent set polytope of a given $n$-vertex graph $G$ with amortized delay $\mathcal{O}(n)$. The independent sets are listed such that two consecutive sets differ either in removing a vertex, or adding a vertex and removing its neighbors from the independent set, i.e., the symmetric difference between two consecutive independent sets induces a star in $G$. As applications of this result, we obtain an algorithm to compute a Hamilton path on the matching polytope of an $m$-edge graph $G$ with worst-case delay $\mathcal{O}(m)$, which lists all matchings of $G$ in such a way that the symmetric difference between two consecutive matchings is a path on at most three edges. Furthermore, we obtain an algorithm to compute a Hamilton path on the chain polytope and order polytope of an $n$-element poset $P$ with amortized delay $\mathcal{O}(n)$, which lists all antichains of $P$ or all ideals of $P$, respectively, by star exchanges. Our algorithms are derived from the generic framework proposed by Merino and Mütze (FOCS'23+SICOMP'24) for computing Hamilton paths on arbitrary 0/1-polytopes, which uses a linear optimization procedure as a black box. Our algorithms bypass solving the computationally intractable maximum weight independent set problem by a simple and purely combinatorial greedy rule.

items.title: Reconstruction of graphs and surfaces from derived categories
items.summary: A pair of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$ is a \emph{Fourier--Mukai (FM) pair} if there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories of derived sheaves of abelian groups \[\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))\simeq \operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z)).\] An FM pair $(X,Y)$ is \emph{non-trivial} if $X$ and $Y$ are not homeomorphic. We consider the question of whether non-trivial FM pairs $(X,Y)$ exist for which $X$ and $Y$ are both "nice" spaces, which in this article means admitting a triangulation. We show that the answer is no if $X$ is second-countable and either (i) one-dimensional, (ii) a surface, or (iii) the 3-sphere. In order to prove this, we define two invariants of dualizable categories. The first invariant is an extension of \emph{Tate--Hochschild cohomology} (aka singular Hochschild cohomology) to a class of dualizable categories satisfying a countability assumption. For a homology manifold $X$, we relate the Tate--Hochschild cohomology of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))$ to the homology at infinity of $X$ (in the sense of proper homotopy theory). The second invariant takes the form of a subcategory $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{Gor}}\subseteq\mathcal D$ called the \emph{Gorenstein locus}, defined for every dualizable stable category $\mathcal D$. For a triangularizable space $X$ and a field $k$, we show that the Gorenstein locus of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(k))$ is equal to the full subcategory of sheaves supported on the $k$-homology manifold locus of $X$.

items.title: On the probability that a random Latin square is all-even
items.summary: In a Latin square, every row can be interpreted as a permutation, and therefore has a parity (even or odd). We prove that in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square, the probability that all rows are even is of the form $2^{-n+o(n)}$. This fills a gap left by recent work of Kwan, Petrova and Sawhney: they proved that the row parities behave like a sequence of independent coin flips in a variety of different senses, but they were not able to lower-bound the all-even probability, as their approach had a small number of "exceptional rows" whose parities they could not control. In fact, we prove a more general theorem on the probability of any possible prescription of row parities, column parities and symbol parities. Our approach extends the ideas of Kwan, Petrova and Sawhney, introducing a new way to "bootstrap" intercalate switchings to control more complex switching operations.

items.title: Weighted Liouville Theorems and A Priori Bounds for Indefinite Superlinear Equations with Pucci's Maximal Operator
items.summary: Consider \begin{equation*}\ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\mathcal_{λ,Λ}^{+}(D^{2}u)&=μu+a(x)u^{p}\quad\text{in}~Ω,\\ u&=0\quad\text{on}~~\partialΩ, \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*} where $ \ Omega$ is a smooth bounded domain, $a$ is a continuous function which is allowed to change sign. Moreover, the set of zeros of $a$ may have a non-empty interior. The main objective of this article is to establish a uniform bound on the set of positive solutions of the above problem. This approach requires a suitable Liouville-type theorem. We first prove the Liouville-type theorem for $-\mathcal_{λ,Λ}^{+}(D^{2}v)=h(x_{1})f(v),$ where \(h\) is a strictly increasing one-dimensional weight and \(f\) is positive and nondecreasing.

items.title: Faster and simpler traversal of 0/1-polytopes
items.summary: Recently, Merino and Mütze (FOCS'23+SICOMP'24) presented an algorithm for computing a Hamilton path on the skeleton of any 0/1-polytope ${\rm conv}(X)$, where $X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$. The algorithm uses as a black box an algorithm for solving the classical linear optimization problem $\min\{w\cdot x\mid x\in X\}$ for some weight vector $w\in\mathbb{R}^n$. The resulting delay per visited vertex on the Hamilton path is only by a $\log n$ factor larger than the time to solve one instance of the optimization algorithm. In this paper, we make the Hamilton path algorithm simpler and faster. Namely, we obtain an amortized delay that is only by a constant factor larger than the running time of the optimization algorithm, thus removing the $\log n$ factor. As concrete results, this yields improved algorithms for generating bases and independent sets in a matroid, spanning trees, forests, matchings and maximum matchings in a graph, vertex covers, minimum vertex covers, independent sets and maximum independent sets in a bipartite graph, and antichains, maximum antichains and ideals in a poset. All of these listings correspond to Hamilton paths on the corresponding polytopes. Furthermore, we obtain an $\mathcal{O}(t_{\rm LP})$ amortized delay algorithm for the vertex enumeration problem on 0/1-polytopes $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid Ax\leq b\}$, where $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}^m$, and $t_{\rm LP}$ is the time needed to solve the linear program $\min\{w\cdot x\mid Ax\leq b\}$. This improves upon the $\mathcal{O}(t_{\rm LP} \log n)$ delay algorithm of Merino and Mütze, and the previous $\mathcal{O}(t_{\rm LP}\,n)$ delay algorithm of Bussieck and Lübbecke from 1998.

items.title: BKT transition for $\mathsf{Sine}_β$
items.summary: We prove the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase transition in the large-distance behaviour of the two-point correlation function of the $\mathsf{Sine}_β$ point process for all $β>0$, confirming the first term of an asymptotic expansion predicted by Forrester.

items.title: Regularisation and Parameter Choice Rules for Composite Linear Inverse Problems
items.summary: In this paper we propose a novel regularisation strategy for structured linear inverse problems of the form $Ax=F \circ G x = z$. Instead of using the operator $A$ or a complex scheme involving both $F$ and $G$ simultaneously, combining already existing and simpler regularisations for $F$ and $G$ allows the use of established and optimised programs for high-speed computations. As classical parameter choice rules fail in the scenario when no source conditions are known because intermediate error bounds may be unavailable, we provide both a-priori and a-posteriori rules with a convergence speed analysis given source conditions. We test the proposed method on the pre-clinical medical imaging technique of magnetic particle imaging with different choices of regularisation and on a convolution problem for an analysis of the convergence speed.

items.title: Hamilton paths and cycles in flip graphs of (almost-)perfect matchings
items.summary: We consider the set of matchings of a graph and a local change operation, called a flip, between them. In the combinatorial setting, the base graphs are either complete graphs or complete bipartite graphs, and in the geometric setting, the graphs are embedded on point sets in the plane, with the requirement that edges must be drawn as straight lines and must not cross. For base graphs with an even number of vertices, we consider perfect matchings, i.e., all vertices are matched, and for base graphs with an odd number of vertices, we consider almost-perfect matchings, i.e., all but one vertex of the graph are matched. A 2-flip between two perfect matchings exchanges two edges, and a 1-flip between two almost-perfect matchings exchanges one edge. The corresponding flip graph has the set of perfect or almost-perfect matchings as vertices, with pairs of them connected by an edge if they differ in a 2-flip or 1-flip, respectively. In this work, we provide a comprehensive picture of Hamiltonicity properties of these flip graphs. We prove that the flip graphs in the combinatorial setting are Hamilton-connected, i.e., they admit a Hamilton path between any two vertices, or, if the flip graphs are bipartite, we prove that they are Hamilton-laceable, i.e., they admit a Hamilton path between any two vertices from different partition classes. In the geometric setting, we prove that any path in them misses exponentially many vertices, in particular, they have no Hamilton paths or cycles. For points in convex position and almost-perfect matchings under 1-flips, we complement this by constructing a cycle in the flip graph that visits almost all vertices.

items.title: Exact bounds on the distribution function of isotropic log-concave distributions
items.summary: For each real $b$, exact upper and lower bounds on the probability $\mathsf P(X\ge b)$ over all random variables $X$ with log-concave p.d.f.'s such that $\mathsf E X=0$ and $\mathsf E X^2=1$ are obtained, as well as the best constant factor $C$ in the inequality $\mathsf P(X\ge b)\le C e^{-b}$ for all real $b\ge0$. Exact upper and lower bounds on the corresponding exponential moments (Proposition 9.4) and explicit exponentially decreasing upper bounds on the mentioned p.d.f.'s (Propositions 9.2 and 9.3) are given as well. Some general results concerning log-concave p.d.f.'s are also obtained.

items.title: SAT-sampling for statistical significance testing in sparse contingency tables
items.summary: Exact conditional tests for contingency tables require sampling from fibers with fixed margins. Classical Markov basis MCMC is general but often impractical: computing full Markov bases that connect all fibers of a given constraint matrix can be infeasible and the resulting chains may converge slowly, especially in sparse settings or in presence of structural zeros. We introduce a SAT-based alternative that encodes fibers as Boolean circuits which allows modern SAT samplers to generate tables randomly. We analyze the sampling bias that SAT samplers may introduce, provide diagnostics, and propose practical mitigation. We propose hybrid MCMC schemes that combine SAT proposals with local moves to ensure correct stationary distributions which do not necessarily require connectivity via local moves which is particularly beneficial in presence of structural zeros. Across benchmarks, including small and involved tables with many structural zeros where pure Markov-basis methods underperform, our methods deliver reliable conditional p-values and often outperform samplers that rely on precomputed Markov bases.

items.title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
items.summary: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) can be applied to large nonlinear systems with complex objectives while enforcing constraints, but the cost of solving the underlying optimization problems limits real-time application for systems with fast dynamics or many states. Neural networks can reduce this online cost by approximating the control law, but may violate constraints and typically require many precomputed optimizer solutions for training. The learning-based iterative solver for constrained optimization (LISCO) instead learns to predict primal-dual steps toward satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions through self-supervised training without precomputed solutions, but its dense, monolithic architecture grows with the prediction horizon. We remove this horizon dependence by exploiting the temporal structure of the problem in the solver architecture, which makes the network size independent of the horizon while leaving the training loss and the solver iteration unchanged. A closed-loop resampling strategy further aligns the training distribution with closed-loop operation at no additional sampling cost. On an economic NMPC benchmark of a CSTR cascade, the proposed solver scales to larger problems than monolithic LISCO and achieves median speedups of up to a factor of four over IPOPT. In closed loop, it achieves comparable control performance to IPOPT with no observed constraint violations.

items.title: Complex Monge-Amp{è}re equations with boundary values: a variational approach
items.summary: Let $Ω$ ___ C n be a bounded hyperconvex domain and $Φ$\,: $Ω$ $\rightarrow$ R a maximal plurisubharmonic function in $Ω$ (possibly unbounded). We introduce a new class E 1 $Φ$ ($Ω$) of plurisubharmonic functions with boundary values equal to $Φ$ in the sense of Cegrell and finite $Φ$-energy on $Ω$. Then given a Borel measure $μ$ on $Ω$, we apply a variational approach to prove that $μ$ is the Monge-Amp{è}re measure of a function u $\in$ E 1 $Φ$ ($Ω$) if and only if it satisfies the integrability condition We also establish a quantitative version of this condition extending previous results of Cegrell and others. Using a logarithmic transformation, we obtain analogous results for the real Monge-Amp{è}re equations with (unbounded) boundary data.

items.title: Harmonic analysis and circuit approximation of Sobolev functions on quantum input spaces
items.summary: We derive approximation rates for Sobolev functions defined on the complex unit sphere and complex projective space, representing quantum states, and on the special and projective unitary groups, representing quantum unitary operations. By using harmonic analysis on compact groups and compact homogeneous spaces, we characterize the corresponding Peter--Weyl decompositions and Sobolev spaces via irreducible representations and the Laplace--Beltrami operator. Combining spectral truncation with finite-depth quantum-circuit approximation, invoking the Solovay--Kitaev theorem, we establish quantitative rates that separate the spectral truncation error from the circuit approximation error.

items.title: Beyond QAOA: A Review of AI and Quantum Computing for Adaptive Combinatorial Optimization
items.summary: Near-term quantum approaches to combinatorial optimization are limited by qubit counts, circuit fidelity, sampling cost, and the difficulty of encoding constraints, while machine learning is increasingly used to configure and control quantum optimization workflows. We call such workflows adaptive: decisions conventionally fixed in advance, from formulation and penalties to shot budgets, backends, and whether to invoke a quantum processor at all, are made by learned policies that respond to the instance, the progress of the solve, or the hardware. This review examines three paradigms, AI for quantum optimization, quantum for AI-driven optimization, and AI-quantum co-optimization, and organizes the literature by the decision being learned rather than by application. A structured search identified a 119-paper corpus, of which 67 papers form an evidence core coded in detail. The evidence is considerably stronger for AI-assisted quantum optimization than for the reverse direction: learning already reduces quantum evaluations, improves initialization, supports decomposition and penalty control, and mitigates noise, whereas evidence that quantum computation improves learned optimizers remains largely confined to small-scale simulation. Experimental controls are thin: of 52 studies in the three paradigms, 22 include no classical baseline, the quantum contribution is fully isolated in 10 of 24 where an ablation applies, and the median largest experiment uses 16 qubits. We introduce an M0-M5 evidence hierarchy, from simulation to practical quantum advantage, and find no broadly convincing result at the highest level. We argue that scaling is increasingly a systems problem: the question is not only whether a problem fits on a quantum processor, but how classical and quantum resources should be allocated across the optimization process.

items.title: Each simplex in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has a point with at least $14$ emanating normals to its boundary
items.summary: We prove that each simplex in $\mathbb{R}^4$ contains a point with at least $14$ emanating normals to the boundary. Earlier, the authors proved that each generic simple polytope in $\mathbb{R}^4$ contains a point with at least $12$ emanating normals to the boundary. This problem belongs to a piecewise linear counterpart of a longstanding problem concerning normals to smooth convex bodies.

items.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four
items.summary: Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.

items.title: On the Moments of Least $s$-Gaps of Partitions and a Conjecture of Baruah and Talukdar
items.summary: Andrews and Newman \cite{AN19, AN20} defined the minimal excludant or mex of a partition. The mex of a partition is the smallest positive integer which is absent from the partition. Baruah, Bhoria, Eyyunni and Maji \cite{BBEM} studied the sum of mex split according to parity, together with its $\ell$-th moments. Ballantine and Merca \cite{BM20} generalized mex to the least $s$-gap, which is the smallest natural number that does not occur minimum $s$ times in the partition. Baruah and Talukdar \cite{BT} conjectured a corresponding asymptotic equivalence between the sums of odd and even least $s$-gaps for every $s>1$, generalizing a theorem of Barman and Singh \cite{BS} for the classical mex. In this article, we derive exact formulas for the $\ell$-th moments of $\smex(π)$ for every fixed $\ell\ge 1$, in terms of partition functions. We give a complete proof of the conjecture of Baruah and Talukdar \cite{BT} for every natural number $s>1$. We also generalize an identity of Hopkins, Sellers and Stanton \cite{HSS} to the least $s$-gap setting.

items.title: Sharp Bounds for Limits of $N$-Point Correlation
items.summary: We consider the question which functions $f$ may appear as limiting functions of the $N$-point correlation. We obtain sharp point-wise lower and upper bounds. The explicit examples constructed to show the sharpness of the bounds are based on van der Corput sequences.

items.title: AlgMortar: a fully algebraic multiscale mortar preconditioner
items.summary: The solution of large-scale symmetric positive definite (SPD) linear systems arising from discretizations of second-order elliptic equations is challenging, especially in applications with highly heterogeneous coefficients, such as flow in porous media, which can lead to severely ill-conditioned systems. In this context, multiscale methods have recently been used to accelerate Krylov subspace methods, owing to their favorable parallel scalability. In this work, we present AlgMortar, a fully algebraic realization of the Multiscale Mortar Mixed Finite Element Method (MMMFEM). The method uses only information extracted from the fine-grid system matrix, which facilitates its implementation in existing solvers. AlgMortar uses graph partitioning to define a domain decomposition directly from the matrix graph. On each subdomain, it builds local linear systems that mimic Dirichlet problems, and couples the resulting local solutions through an algebraic interface condition that recovers the weak flux-continuity mechanism of MMMFEM. We prove that the method is well posed when the matrix is SPD. Numerical experiments on fine-grid linear systems arising from finite-volume discretizations of Darcy flow problems show that, when used as a preconditioner for the conjugate gradient method, the proposed approach exhibits good scalability and is competitive with state-of-the-art algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods for challenging heterogeneous, high-contrast test cases, including highly irregular corner-point grids. Additional tests with SPD matrices arising from problems other than finite-volume discretizations of Darcy flow showed competitive performance with AMG.

items.title: Brown's loss function and estimation of the scale parameter and the entropy in scale mixture models with unknown location
items.summary: This paper deals with the problems of decision theoretic estimation of the scale parameter, $σ$, and the entropy (Shannon or Renyi) in general scale mixture models with unknown location. Employing Kubokawa's approach, under convexity of the loss $L(t)$ either in $t$ or in $lnt$, improved estimators of $σ$ are derived. If $L(t)$ satisfies an additional condition, the problem reduces to estimating $σ$ in the degenerate (scale mixture) model. As the entropy is a linear translation of $lnσ$, its estimation under a loss $L_0(u)$ amounts to estimating $σ$ under $L(t)=L_0(lnt)$, with the quadratic loss $L_0(u)=u^2$ and Brown's loss $L(t)=(lnt)^2$ being a typical case. Thus, in the case that $L_0(u)$ is convex improved estimators of the entropy are directly obtained from respective estimators of $σ$. The results are applied to scale mixtures of normal and exponential distributions, including the multivariate $t$ and multivariate Lomax distributions.

items.title: Matrix Kloosterman sums and product-trace estimates for semisimple algebras
items.summary: Let $k=\mathbb{F}_q$, $E=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ and $\mathrm{Tr}=\mathrm{Tr}_{E/k}$. For $r\ge 2$, $a\in k^{\times}$ and $x\in E^{\times}$, let $\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)$ be the number of $r$-tuples $(x_1,\cdots,x_r)$ in $(E^{\times})^r$ satisfying $x_1\cdots x_r=x$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(x_1+\cdots+x_r)=a$. We prove $\left|\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)-\left((q^n-1)^{r-1}+(-1)^r\right)/q\right|\le (r^n-1) q^{\frac{(r-1)n-1}{2}}$. This proves the square-root estimate predicted in Wan's conjecture and generalizes a previous result of Moisio and Wan. For a finite semisimple algebra $B=\prod\limits_{i=1}^s M_{d_i}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n_i}})$ over $k$ and a regular element $x\in B^{\times}$, the same method combined with Zelingher's formula leads to analogous square-root estimates.

items.title: The DP color function of joins and vertex-gluing of hypergraphs
items.summary: The DP color function $P_{DP}(\mathcal{H}, k)$ of a hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ is defined as the minimum possible value of $P_{DP}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{F})$ taken over all $k$-fold covers $\mathcal{F}$ of $\mathcal{H}$. It serves as an extension of the classical chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we investigate the DP color function for two constructions: the join of a hypergraph with a complete graph and vertex-gluings of certain hypergraphs. Both constructions extend some results of Becker et al.

items.title: Utility-Based Recovery Risk Measures: Redundancy and Approximation for Portfolio Optimization
items.summary: Recovery risk measures incorporate explicit liability-recovery requirements into asset-liability risk assessment. We study their specialization to optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs), allowing the underlying utility specification to vary across recovery levels and encompassing Recovery Average Value at Risk (RecAV@R) as a special case. For finite recovery specifications, we use the dual penalty representation to characterize redundant recovery regimes and derive position-independent screening conditions. For a subfamily of the Cressie-Read power-divergence family, including entropic and truncated-quadratic specifications, we obtain an exact characterization on atomless probability spaces: universal redundancy is equivalent to a two-dimensional convex-hull condition involving recovery levels and divergence-scale parameters. On such spaces, universal redundancy for RecAV@R reduces to pairwise dominance, whereas for power-divergence OCEs it can arise from the joint effect of several recovery regimes. For nonlinear OCE utilities, we develop a certified piecewise-linear approximation framework for portfolio optimization. In finite-scenario models, the approximating problems are finite-dimensional linear programs, while utility approximation errors transfer directly to the Recovery OCE, yielding explicit error bounds and convergence rates. Uniform approximation over the portfolio domain further implies convergence of optimal values and stability of optimal solutions. A numerical asset-liability study illustrates the effects of recovery-dependent risk preferences and the accuracy and convergence of the approximation.

items.title: An Optimal Control Approach to Finite-Time Stabilization of Linear Systems
items.summary: This paper presents a finite-time stabilization method for the integrator chain via optimal control techniques by introducing a tailored cost function. We analyze key properties of the resulting value function to derive the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. Numerical simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the approach.

items.title: A complex associated to a family of ideals and applications to subspace arrangements
items.summary: We reprove and generalize a result of Derksen describing the Hilbert polynomial of the vanishing ideal of a transversal subspace arrangement in projective space. When the subspaces have all codimension 2, we describe explicitly the local cohomology modules of the corresponding defining ideal. This is achieved via a complex naturally associated to the subspace arrangement, whose basic properties are also investigated.

items.title: Butcher series for Hamiltonian Poisson integrators through symplectic groupoids
items.summary: We exhibit a new pre-Lie algebra in the framework of symplectic groupoids and, in turn, use Butcher trees to compute the Taylor series of a solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation on any symplectic groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M.$ The impact of this new algebraic approach is twofold. On the geometric side, it yields algebraic operations to approximate Lagrangian bisections of $\mathcal{G}$ using the Butcher-Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra and, in turn, aims at a better understanding of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of $M.$ On the computational side, we define a new class of Poisson integrators for Hamiltonian dynamics on Poisson manifolds.

items.title: Learning by Compression: Risk Estimates Attain the Law-of-Large-Numbers Rate
items.summary: Compression schemes provide a general framework for deriving data-dependent risk bounds for learning algorithms. For learning rules based on preferent compression, existing results upper-bound the risk in terms of a sample-dependent complexity $\boldsymbol{k}$, defined as the cardinality of the compression augmented by the training examples on which the reconstructed hypothesis is inappropriate. These results, however, yield a margin of order $O(\sqrt{\ln N/N})$ above $\boldsymbol{k}/N$. In this paper, we establish that the logarithmic factor is not intrinsic. We prove that, for every fixed confidence level $1-δ$, the risk is bounded with probability at least $1-δ$ by $$ \frac{\boldsymbol{k}}{N} + O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right), $$ uniformly over all possible values of $\boldsymbol{k}$. Thus, risk estimates for learning algorithms based on preferent compression attain the same law-of-large-numbers rate as the empirical estimate of the probability of a fixed event. We also show that the leading term $\boldsymbol{k}/N$ is necessary and investigate its relation to the empirical risk. In particular, we identify regimes in which the empirical risk retains the $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ convergence rate, as well as regimes in which it converges more slowly or ceases to be consistent, while the complexity-based estimator preserves the $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ rate.

items.title: Threshold Geometry, Bifurcation, and Data-Driven Analysis of a Vaccination-Treatment Model for Hepatitis B
items.summary: Despite the availability of excellent vaccines and antiviral medicines, hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health problem. In this work, we develop a mathematical vaccination-treatment model for HBV transmission to investigate threshold conditions for illness persistence as well as the level of intervention. The analysis gives the characterisation of both disease-free and endemic equilibria and determines the basic reproduction number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, by the next-generation matrix approach. The model indicates that $\mathcal{R}_0=1$ is a critical threshold dividing disease-free from endemic states and characterises a forward transcritical bifurcation regarding the transmission parameter. Numerical equilibrium continuation and stability assessments confirm the analytical results. A two-parameter study of transmission and vaccination rates identifies threshold geometries and assesses impacts of important parameters using sensitivity analysis. The model is calibrated with India-specific data, such as HBsAg prevalence, HBV incidence and mortality rates and fits epidemiological targets closely through limited nonlinear calibration. Additionally, multi-start optimisation and practical identifiability profiling are used to investigate parameter uncertainty. Robustness analyses reveal that the calibrated $\mathcal{R}_0^*=1.1744$ is associated with a super-threshold regime; however, parameter flexibility permits both sub-threshold and super-threshold regimes. This combined analytical and data-driven framework connects epidemic thresholds, bifurcation structures, intervention efficacy, and parameter uncertainty. It provides a quantitative framework for analysing HBV persistence and evaluating control options, especially in the absence of epidemiological evidence.

items.title: Deformation cones of 2-cubical combinatorial zonotopes
items.summary: We prove that the dimension of the deformation cone of any polytope combinatorially equivalent to a 2-cubical zonotope is bounded above by the number of generators of the zonotope. This bound is tight, and we show that it cannot be improved to an identity. We further extend our results to any 2-cubical polytope whose normal fan is combinatorially isomorphic to a pseudohyperplane arrangement, but we show that it cannot be extended to arbitrary 2-cubical polytopes.

items.title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups of type ${}^2 A_3$ and ${}^2 A_4$ over Local Rings
items.summary: We give a complete classification of the automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$, and of their elementary subgroups, over commutative local rings $R$ containing $1/2$ and equipped with a non-trivial involution $θ$. The classification covers all isogeny types and, together with our higher-rank result~\cite{EB&DM1}, completes the description for type ${}^2A_{\ell}$ with $\ell\geq3$.

items.title: $D^L$, $D^Q$ Spectrum and Eigenvalue-free Interval of Cayley Graphs over Finite Nilpotent Groups
items.summary: For a finite group $G$ and a symmetric connection set $S$, we study the distance Laplacian ($D^L$) and distance signless Laplacian ($D^Q$) spectrum of the Cayley graph $\Cay(G,S)$ for $G$ a finite nilpotent group. Using the internal direct product decomposition over Sylow subgroups, we reduce every question to a single (possibly non-abelian) prime-power factor. In this setting, the required tools are furnished by ordinary representation theory rather than character theory. Based on this framework, we then derive a complete and explicit formula for every eigenvalue, with multiplicity, of the distance matrix, distance Laplacian, and distance signless Laplacian of $\Cay(G,S)$ for $G$ nilpotent: each eigenvalue is indexed by a tuple of irreducible characters of the Sylow factors. Finally, we use the explicit spectrum, together with Perron--Frobenius theory, to determine the eigenvalue-free interval of $D^L$ and $D^Q$.

items.title: Minimum-Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems
items.summary: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be \emph{small}, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices. Finally, we show that there exists a fundamental lower bound on the optimal control energy which cannot be overcome by increasing the time horizon of the problem.

items.title: Isoperimetry of singular CMC hypersurfaces
items.summary: We produce the first examples of singular isoperimetric boundaries with non-zero constant mean curvature in Riemannian manifolds. The main technical ingredient is establishing that, for constant mean curvature hypersurfaces containing isolated singularities modelled on strictly stable, strictly minimising regular tangent cones, weak strict stability implies local unique volume-constrained minimisation.

items.title: On the Finiteness of Anosov flows on $3$-manifolds via Contact Geometry
items.summary: In dimension 3, following Eliashberg-Thurston and Mitsumatsu, one can associate a transverse pair of oppositely oriented contact structures to any Anosov flow. We show that when the ambient manifold is hyperbolic, the isotopy classes of these contact structures completely determine the flow up to isotopy orbit equivalence. This then implies that on any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold, the number of Anosov flows modulo isotopy orbit equivalence is finite. This approach also yields an explicit bound on the number of orbit equivalence classes of Anosov flows in terms of the number of universally tight contact structures. In addition, we show finiteness of pseudo-Anosov flows for which the complement of the singular orbits is atoroidal and, in the non- hyperbolic case, we obtain a control on the dynamics of Anosov flows on the hyperbolic pieces of the JSJ-decomposition.

items.title: A Vector-Valued Extension of a Theorem of Marciszewski
items.summary: We establish a vector-valued extension of a theorem of Marciszewski. Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space, let $Γ$ be a set, and let $X$ be a nonzero Banach space containing no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. We prove that if $C(K)$ embeds isomorphically into $c_0(Γ,X)$, then $C(K)$ is isomorphic to $c_0(Λ)$ for some set $Λ$. Moreover, when $Γ$ is infinite, the optimal distortion of embeddings of $C(K)$ into $c_0(Γ,X)$ equals that of embeddings into $c_0(Γ)$. The classification result answers a question posed in an earlier paper.

items.title: Path homology of circulant digraphs
items.summary: We study GLMY path homology of circulant digraphs through step-word complexes and infinite cyclic lifts. We first prove chain retractions for interval connection sets. For a fixed finite positive connection set $S$ containing $1$, the infinite lift yields a split exact sequence and all-degree stability over every field. We then encode the short additive relations of $S$ in a lattice lift and obtain exterior homology in arbitrarily high degrees for collision-free step sets. Under an exact Freiman admissibility condition, we classify all connection sets with three positive steps. For arbitrarily many steps, we compute rectangular additive configurations and arithmetic progressions over every field, and doubling strings in characteristic zero, including their boundary ranks.

items.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
items.summary: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(π_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the

items.title: Shadowing in CR-Dynamical Systems
items.summary: A CR-dynamical system is a pair $(X, G)$, where $X$ is a compact metric space and $G$ is a closed relation on $X$. We introduce four $(i,j)$-shadowing properties, obtained by independently varying the quantifiers in the definitions of pseudo-orbit and shadowing. These properties coincide with the classical shadowing property for single-valued systems, while $(2, 2)$-shadowing agrees with the established notion of shadowing for set-valued dynamical systems. We investigate how the classical characterisations of shadowing for the identity map, periodic maps and isometries extend to closed relations. In particular, we obtain rigidity results for $(2, 1)$-shadowing and positive results for $(1, 2)$-shadowing on totally disconnected spaces. Finally, whenever the infinite Mahavier product is non-empty, we prove that a closed relation has the $(2, 2)$-shadowing property if, and only if, its associated Mahavier dynamical system has the shadowing property. This removes the surjectivity hypothesis from a recent corresponding result for set-valued dynamical systems.

items.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
items.summary: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.

items.title: Removal of singularities in Morse-Bott symplectizations
items.summary: Hofer-Wysocki-Zehnder and Bourgeois proved that a finite energy punctured pseudoholomorphic curve in the symplectization of a Morse-Bott contact manifold either has a removable singularity or asymptotes to a Reeb orbit. We give an alternate proof of this result.

items.title: Ruling out Infinite-Time Bubbling under $SO(4)$-Equivariant Yang--Mills Flow on $\mathbb{S}^4\times SU(2)$
items.summary: We study the Yang--Mills flow on $\mathbb{S}^4$ restricted to $\mathrm{SO}(4)$-equivariant connections on the trivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ bundle. It was expected that antipodal instanton--anti-instanton configurations would lead to infinite-time singularities along the flow. We show that this does not occur. Moreover, for any smooth equivariant initial condition, the flow converges to the trivial flat connection.

items.title: An inverse theorem for all finite abelian groups via nilmanifolds
items.summary: We prove a first inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all finite abelian groups that uses only nilmanifolds (rather than possibly more general nilspaces). This makes progress toward confirming the Jamneshan--Tao conjecture. The correlating function in our theorem is a projected nilsequence, obtained as the fiber-wise average of a nilsequence defined on a boundedly-larger abelian group extending the original abelian group. This result is tight in the following sense: we prove also that $k$-step projected nilsequences of bounded complexity are genuine obstructions to having small Gowers $U^{k+1}$-norm. This inverse theorem relies on a new result concerning compact finite-rank (CFR) nilspaces, which is the main contribution in this paper: every $k$-step CFR nilspace is a factor of a $k$-step nilmanifold. This new connection between the classical theory of nilmanifolds and the more recent theory of nilspaces has applications beyond arithmetic combinatorics. We illustrate this with an application in topological dynamics, by proving the following result making progress on a question of Jamneshan, Shalom and Tao: every minimal $\mathbb{Z}^ω$-system of order $k$ is a factor of an inverse limit of $\mathbb{Z}^ω$-polynomial orbit systems of order $k$, these being natural generalizations of nilsystems alternative to translational systems.

items.title: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations with an application to elliptic boundary value problems
items.summary: We establish a spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations on a Hilbert space. The proof relies on the Arens decomposition of a closed linear relation into an operator part and a purely multivalued part, reducing the problem directly to the classical spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators. No finite-dimensionality condition is imposed on the multivalued part. We also prove a finiterank approximation theorem for compact bounded linear relations and a Fredholm alternative for compact self-adjoint linear relations. As an application, we employ the theory of boundary triples to show that the inverse of the Neumann Laplacian on a bounded domain is a compact self-adjoint linear relation. The abstract spectral theorem then recovers the classical eigenfunction expansion of solutions to the Neumann problem: an L2-convergent series in terms of the non-constant Neumann eigenfunctions together with an arbitrary additive constant. The framework extends naturally to general elliptic boundary value problems with finite-dimensional kernel.

items.title: Bicompact torsion classes and conjectures on brick infinite algebras
items.summary: In the category $\operatorname{\mathsf{mod}} A$ of finitely generated modules over a finite dimensional algebra $A$, a torsion class $\mathcal{T} \subset \operatorname{\mathsf{mod}} A$ is said to be compact if there exists a module $M \in \operatorname{\mathsf{mod}} A$ such that $\mathcal{T}$ is the smallest torsion class containing $M$. If a torsion class satisfies this and the dual condition, then we call it a bicompact torsion class. We conjecture that bicompact torsion classes are precisely functorially finite torsion classes, and prove it for hereditary algebras and also for semistable torsion classes. This gives that Demonet's Lattice Point Conjecture implies Enomoto's Infinite Semibrick Conjecture, both of which are important conjectures on brick infiniteness.

items.title: The Riemannian Convex Bundle Method
items.summary: We introduce the convex bundle method to solve convex, non-smooth optimization problems on Riemannian manifolds of bounded sectional curvature. Each step of our method is based on a model that involves the convex hull of previously collected subgradients, parallelly transported into the current serious iterate. This approach generalizes the dual form of classical bundle subproblems in Euclidean space. We prove that, under mild conditions, the convex bundle method converges to a minimizer. Several numerical examples implemented using Manopt$.$jl illustrate the performance of the proposed method and compare it to the subgradient method, the cyclic proximal point algorithm, as well as the proximal bundle method.

items.title: On the simultaneous zero inclusion property and characterization of Inner product space
items.summary: We show that if a Banach space $X$ is smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund and if satisfies the following \[0\in W(T) \implies 0\in W(T^{-1})\] for all invertible bounded linear map on $X$ then Birkhoff-James orthogonality in $X$ is symmetric. This result, therefore, characterizes the inner product spaces out of all smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund spaces having three or more dimension via simultaneous zero inclusion property, introduced by Bračič et al. [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 449 (2017) 1413-1423]. Further, this gives answers to some open questions asked by E. Poon [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 534(2024), 128052].

items.title: Projective dimension of closed neighborhood hypergraphs via extended double covers
items.summary: Let $G$ be a finite and simple graph without isolated vertices. We investigate the projective dimension of the closed neighborhood hypergraph $\mathcal{N}[G]$ and its relationship with the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the extended bipartite double cover $\mathfrak{B}_e(G)$ of $G$. We establish the general upper bound $\operatorname{prod-dim} (\mathcal{N}[G]) \leq \operatorname{reg}(\mathfrak{B}_e(G))$ for all graphs. Furthermore, we prove that the exact equalities $\operatorname{prod-dim} (\mathcal{N}[G]) = \operatorname{reg}(\mathfrak{B}_e(G)) =α(G)$ hold when $G$ belongs to several prominent graph classes, including König-Egerváry (contains all bipartite graphs), cographs, co-chordal, chordal and comparability graphs, where $α(G)$ denotes the independence number. Our method of proofs relies on connecting algebraic invariants to the underlying combinatorial structure of graphs through covering, domination and matching parameters, together with the use of homology tools.

items.title: On the fault-tolerant metric dimension of maximal outerplanar graphs
items.summary: Given a graph $G$, a set $W$ of vertices of $G$ is a resolving set if, for any pair of vertices $z_1$ and $z_2$ of $G$, there is a vertex $w\in W$ such that $d(w,z_1)\ne d(w,z_2)$, where $d(u,v)$ denotes the length of a shortest path between the vertices $u$ and $v$. The metric dimension of a graph $G$, $β(G)$, is the minimum cardinality of a resolving set of $G$. A resolving set $W$ is fault-tolerant if $W\setminus \{w\}$ is a resolving set for any $w\in W$. The fault-tolerant metric dimension of a graph $G$, denoted by $β'(G)$, is the minimum cardinality of a fault-tolerant resolving set of $G$. In this paper, we study the fault-tolerant metric dimension problem in maximal outerplanar graphs. In particular, we show that there are exactly two maximal outerplanar graphs with $β'(G)=3$. We also show that $4\le β'(G) \le 6$ for any maximal outerplanar graph $G$ of order at least 7 and metric dimension 2. Moreover, we establish the upper bound $β'(G) \le \left\lceil \frac{2n}{3} \right\rceil$ for maximal outerplanar graphs $G$ of order $n\ge 5$, by building in linear time a fault-tolerant resolving set of cardinality $\left\lceil \frac{2n}{3} \right\rceil$.

items.title: asdex: Automatic Sparse Differentiation in JAX
items.summary: Many tasks in scientific computing and machine learning require the Jacobian or Hessian matrix of a function. Automatic differentiation (AD) computes these derivatives to machine precision, but materializing a dense $m \times n$ Jacobian requires $n$ forward-mode or $m$ reverse-mode AD passes, one per column or row. For a large class of functions, each output depends on only a few inputs, making the derivative matrix sparse. Automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) exploits this structure in four steps: detection of the input-agnostic sparsity pattern, coloring of a graph to group columns or rows that can share an AD pass, compressed differentiation to compute a compressed derivative matrix with one AD pass per color, and finally decompression into the original sparsity pattern. The number of colors, and hence of AD passes, is often independent of the problem dimension: a banded Jacobian with $b$ contiguous bands, for instance, only ever requires $b$ colors, regardless of its size. asdex offers the first standalone ASD toolkit in the popular JAX ecosystem. With $\texttt{asdex.jacobian}$ and $\texttt{asdex.hessian}$, it provides sparse drop-in replacements for $\texttt{jax.jacobian}$ and $\texttt{jax.hessian}$.

items.title: On $p$-groups with one nonlinear codegree
items.summary: For an irreducible character $χ$ of a finite group $G$, its codegree is defined by $cod(χ)=|G:\kerχ|/χ(1)$. In this paper, we characterize fnite $p$-groups whose nonlinear irreducible characters all have the same codegree.

items.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part~1: expectation under the uniform null
items.summary: We study the expectation of the discrete total variation statistic $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$ of counts $X_1,\dots,X_n$ over $n$ ordered bins with sample size $N$, under the uniform multinomial null. In the notation used throughout the series, a reference distribution $\mathbf r$ defines $d_{\mathbf r}(x)=\|x-N\mathbf r\|_V$; here $\mathbf r=\mathbf u$ is uniform and we write simply $d$. We obtain an exact single-sum formula, a closed form in central trinomial coefficients valid for every $n\ge2$, with one-term evaluations at $n=2,4$ and a complete D-finite characterization for $n=3$. The per-edge expectation $W_N=E|X_2-X_1|$ satisfies an exact three-term recurrence, from which we derive its complete $1/N$ expansion with the $n$-independent constant $E(d^\circ/\sqrt{Nn})\to 2/\sqrtπ$ for the cyclic statistic $d^\circ=d^\circ_{\mathbf u}$, independent of the number of bins; the complementary sparse regime (fixed $N$, $n\to\infty$) is treated in a separate paper. Conditioning on a two-bin total reduces each edge to a symmetric random walk; as the subsequent parts of the series will show, this method carries the analysis to non-uniform reference laws.

items.title: Short Recurrences and Straight-Line Programs for Primes
items.summary: We give a short autonomous recurrence that generates every odd prime, in increasing order, from the single initial value $8$. Its integer state determines both its output and its next update: the lowest set bit gives the next prime, while the highest set bit determines the sieve period. The same state also determines the following prime gap. A related recurrence represents the prime-counting function as the $2$-adic valuation of a single integer. Independently, a direct packing of a finite divisor sieve yields fixed arithmetic constructions for the $n$-th prime, the prime-counting function, and the twin-prime counting function. We express these constructions as straight-line programs using addition, truncated subtraction, multiplication, integer division, exponentiation, and remainder. Counting operations with reuse of computed values gives programs of lengths $166$, $132$, and $167$, respectively; one autonomous recurrence update uses $99$ operations. Explicit arithmetic subroutines remove all auxiliary operations, including bitwise AND. The programs unfold into fixed arithmetic terms without variable-length sums, products, or searches.

items.title: Finite-Sample Bounds for Fréchet Means of Dependent Data in Metric Spaces with Curvature Bounded Above
items.summary: We prove finite-sample risk bounds for empirical quadratic and power Fréchet means in geodesic metric spaces with curvature bounded above for observations with arbitrary joint law. We compare the sample with exchangeable copies in which one observation is redrawn independently of the original sample and the others move to preserve the joint law. These displacements control the error, with no entropy or dimension assumptions. For quadratic Fréchet means, this yields a general ``coupling bound'' in any separable complete $CAT(κ)$ space, where for $κ>0$ the observations must lie in a closed convex set of circumradius below $π/(2\sqrtκ)$. This bound is exact on the real line for nonnegatively correlated Gaussian observations and for comonotone functions of a common factor. We apply it in two settings. Under local dependence, the resulting risk bound grows linearly with the average size of the dependency neighborhoods. Under transport sensitivity and for bounded metric variances, summable sensitivities of the conditional laws to a change in one observation preserve the parametric mean squared error rate, while nonsummable polynomial decay gives explicit slower rates. We verify transport sensitivity for stationary reversible Markov chains with Wasserstein-contractive kernels and for bi-Lipschitz images of Gaussian sequences. In the more challenging setting of heavy-tailed, dependent data with possibly infinite variance, we consider power Fréchet means of order $α\in(1,2)$. Under nonpositive curvature, we bound their $L^α$ risk assuming only finite $α$-th moments.

items.title: Banach space, Birkhoff--James orthogonality, James constant, von Neumann--Jordan constant
items.summary: We provide a strengthened answer to the questions posed by Alonso, Martín, and Papini [Studia Math. 188 (2008), 135--150] concerning the comparison between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants . The classical inequality $\CNJ(X)\leq J(X)$ between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants was established by Takahashi and Kato [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 359 (2009), 602--609], Wang [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 138 (2010), 695--701], and Yang and Li [Appl. Math. Lett. 23 (2010), 277--281], while related sharp estimates were obtained by Kato and Takahashi [Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) Suppl. 82 (2010), 75--91]. We sharpen this inequality to $\CNJ(X)\leq\JB(X)$, where $\JB(X)$ is the Birkhoff--James orthogonal James constant introduced by Baronti and Papini [Constr. Math. Anal. 5 (2022), 37--45]. Our proof employs optimal distance ellipses and alternating contact directions.

items.title: Chasing rotational symmetry in the spectre tiling
items.summary: We identify the rotational symmetry centers in the spectre tiling. We find that both 2-fold and 3-fold symmetry centers are coexisting, with two different types of 3-fold centers. Local and global symmetry operations are distinguished, and characterized in terms of substitution systems. We introduce a decomposition of the spectre tiling in terms of three metatiles named diabolo, 2-arms and 3-arms, valid at any substitution level. We propose geometrical constructions for generating patches of the spectre tiling with 2-fold and 3-fold global rotational symmetry.

items.title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
items.summary: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert--Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.

items.title: On the Convergence of the Mesh-Free Discretization of a Non-Linear Bond-Based Peridynamic Model with a Bond-Breakage Criterion
items.summary: We show the convergence of a commonly used mesh-free discretization of a dynamic non-linear bond-based peridynamic model with irreversible damage implemented via a bond-breakage criterion for a fixed horizon $δ>0$. The model chosen here is a mathematically well-posed regularization of a discontinuous peridynamic operator often found in the literature, which assumes that fracture results from strain in tension only. We explicitly include the one-point quadrature used in this scheme in the analysis. The convergence is with respect to the natural norm of the solution space given by $C^1([0,T],L^\infty(Ω)^d)$, and therefore $L^\infty(Ω)^d$ in the spatial coordinates. This result heavily constrains the spatial regularity of the continuous solution which we prove afterwards. More specifically, for locally $L$-Lipschitz continuous input data, local Lipschitz bounds are derived for the displacement, regardless of damage. This is consistent with interpreting the peridynamic model used here as an approximation to a truly discontinuous fracture model with a length-scale parameter given by the horizon $δ>0$. We note that we do not deal with the limit of the solutions as $δ\searrow 0$.

items.title: Circuit-Embedded Feeder-State Reconstruction for Low-Voltage Distribution Networks under Extreme Measurement Sparsity
items.summary: Low-voltage (LV) distribution feeders increasingly require internal state information, yet real-time telemetry is often limited to feeder-head active and reactive power, while downstream demand and production are described only by static contract metadata. This paper proposes a physics-based AC circuit-embedding reconstruction framework for this extreme-sparsity regime. Feeder-head measurements, matched metadata, and class-level profiles first determine bus-level load and production priors. These priors parameterize auxiliary constant-power elements coupled to the physical feeder through impedance branches, and the feeder state is reconstructed by solving the resulting nonlinear AC circuit equilibrium. The resulting AC equilibrium enforces the assigned virtual-element powers, while weighted least squares (WLS) reconciles measurements and pseudo-measurements through weighted residual fitting. The method is evaluated on a real 459-bus Portuguese LV feeder model using an in-sample-calibrated synthetic benchmark of 672 fifteen-minute snapshots. The proposed method converged for all 672 snapshots and achieved voltage RMSE, MAE, and maximum absolute error of 0.0033, 0.0014, and 0.0337 p.u., respectively, outperforming both static-prior WLS baselines. Under the same constructed priors, matched-prior WLS achieved a lower RMSE of 0.0029 p.u., while the proposed circuit embedding reconstructs the feeder state by solving the nonlinear AC equilibrium, bypassing WLS residual fitting entirely and requiring no specification or tuning of pseudo-measurement variances.

items.title: Thurston's Legacy at the Interface of Surface Dynamics, Train Tracks, and Arithmetic
items.summary: In this chapter, we discuss the interaction between low-dimensional dynamics, symbolic dynamics, and geometric topology, focusing on the algebraic characterization and asymptotic behaviour of stretch factors or equivalently pseudo-Anosov dilatations. We first review the algebraic foundations linking Perron--Frobenius theory, multi-variable Euclidean algorithms, and Lind's characterization of topological entropy for shifts of finite type, emphasizing recent constraints on the Perron--Frobenius degree of expansion constants. We then relate these dynamical invariants to the combinatorial world, examining train tracks for surfaces and automorphisms of free groups. Finally, we briefly review the relevance of fibered 3-manifolds, detailing how the Thurston norm, Fried's concavity theorem over fibered cones, and McMullen's Teichmüller polynomial come into play.

items.title: Spectrum of Directed Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
items.summary: We study the spectrum of the adjacency matrix $A_n$ of directed inhomogeneous random graphs on $n$ vertices. We assume that $A_n$ has independent entries and diverging average degree scale $s_n$. This framework includes, as special cases, the directed Chung--Lu random graph and directed stochastic block models. Assuming boundedness of the variance profile and that $s_n$ diverges faster than $\log(n)^2$, we show that the rank-one Chung--Lu model satisfies a non-homogeneous version of the circular law, which in some situations allows for an explicit expression. Moreover, under mild conditions, we identify the asymptotic singular value distribution using tools from free probability. Finally, for finite-rank directed models, we establish that eigenvalues outside the bulk have joint Gaussian fluctuations at the scale $\sqrt{s_n/n}$, with an explicit covariance matrix. These results extend the theory of spectral outliers and their fluctuations to directed inhomogeneous random graphs.

items.title: Loss of derivatives for hyperbolic operators with coefficients oscillating in time
