While reducing risk of safety-critical systems is generally desirable, defense systems are required to produce intended mission effects, which may include harm to an attacking target. In both cases, not all risk can be eliminated. The complex risk constellation of defense systems has implications for the systems' designs. We compare the concepts of risk in existing standards from both the civilian and the military domains. An extended constellation of risks needs to be considered, including risk caused by external threats to security. By including this risk constellation in public communication about defense systems, we aim to stimulate a productive debate.

items.title: Selective Depthwise Separable Convolution for Lightweight Joint Source-Channel Coding in Wireless Image Transmission
items.summary: Depthwise separable convolutional (DSConv) layers have been successfully applied to deep learning (DL)-based joint source-channel coding (JSCC) schemes to reduce computational complexity. However, a systematic investigation of the layerwise and ratio-wise replacement of standard convolutional (Conv) layers with DSConv layers in JSCC systems for wireless image transmission remains largely unexplored. In this letter, we propose a configurable lightweight JSCC framework that incorporates a selective replacement strategy, enabling flexible Conv-to-DSConv replacement at different replacement ratios and positions. By varying the replacement ratio, we obtain models with different computational complexities and analyze their impact on reconstruction performance. Furthermore, we investigate how replacements at different encoder and decoder depths influence reconstruction quality under a fixed replacement ratio. Our results show that Conv-to-DSConv replacement at the intermediate layers of the encoder and decoder achieves a favorable complexity-performance trade-off, revealing layer-wise redundancy in DL-based JSCC systems. Extensive experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves substantial parameter reduction with only slight performance degradation, enabling flexible complexity-performance trade-offs for resource-constrained edge devices.

items.title: What Do Audio-Language Judges of Generated Music Listen For? Four Probes with Controls from Expert Ratings
items.summary: Open audio-language models are used as judges of generated music: given a clip and its text prompt, the model rates the clip, and the judge is validated by how well its ratings correlate with expert ratings. The correlation does not show what the judge responds to: the music, the text prompt, or the way the question is asked. We propose four probes that test each of these, three of them read against a control computed from the human ratings: removing the audio, replacing the clip with another model's clip for the same prompt, swapping the order of two clips in pairwise judging, and rewording the instruction. We apply them to five open judges on all 2,748 clips of MusicEval, and the last two to the SongEval songs. Without audio, no judge exceeds what the prompt alone predicts from the human ratings, and for prompt alignment every judge falls below it. With audio, every judge follows the clip it hears when rating prompt alignment, two do when rating musical quality, and the strongest judge's quality score tracks the experts' alignment rating more than their quality rating. The pairwise verdicts of the four smaller judges follow the position of a clip in the pair (its slot) rather than its quality on both rating sets. For musical quality, rewording the instruction moves the correlation of most judges as much as changing the judge. MusicEval's prompt assignment bounds any prompt-only judge at the model level. We recommend reporting the four probes with every music judge.

items.title: The Predictability Bias of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning in Medical Imaging
items.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting teacher representations of masked regions from visible context. Point prediction summarizes the conditional target distribution and cannot reproduce variation that the context does not resolve. We call this constraint predictability bias. In computed tomography (CT), recurrent anatomy is predictable from context, whereas the sporadic, localized pathology that determines clinical interpretation often is not. We introduce TAP-JEPA, a ViT-B/3D trained on 113,611 CT volumes that is competitive with state-of-the-art encoders (COLIPRI, Merlin, VoxelFM) in scan-level classification. We then audit the learned predictive pathway by replaying the exact masking, teacher, and predictor computations used during training. Prediction lowers the mean Skill (prevalence-normalized average precision) from 0.388 to 0.271 for pathology, but only from 0.921 to 0.873 for anatomy. Along the teacher direction, separating pathology from matched control regions in the same organ, prediction moves pathology 34.7% toward the controls and controls 13.6% toward pathology, with larger shifts farther from visible context. Replacing visible matched-control representations increases surrounding-target prediction loss more than fully replacing pathology representations across four pathology categories. Downstream, removing all final-layer pathology tokens reduces the decision margin by at most 0.45% in four of seven scan-level probes. Together, these results show that contextual predictability is not a sufficient proxy for clinical relevance in medical representation learning. Training objectives should therefore retain diagnostic features regardless of their predictability from surrounding anatomy.

items.title: Robustness of Reinforcement Learning-Based Congestion Management in Low-Voltage Grids
items.summary: Increases in photovoltaic generation, charging of electric vehicles and heat-pump demand challenge operating limits in low-voltage distribution grids. This requires curative curtailment methods that can operate under sparse observability, noisy measurements, and imperfect grid models. Unlike prior end-to-end reinforcement-learning approaches for partially observable curtailment, this work decouples congestion detection and control by combining a random-forest violation pre-classifier with an actor-critic controller, and evaluates its robustness to measurement noise and grid-parameter mismatch. The framework is tested on a real low-voltage grid using synthetic future operating scenarios with low observability and controllability. With accurate grid parameters, the controller reduces total violation magnitude by 98.9%, and this performance remains nearly unchanged under the tested measurement-noise settings. Grid-model mismatch proves to be more challenging, but the controller still mitigates most violations under the tested mismatch assumptions.

items.title: QC-MI-OVSEL: Benchmarking Query-Conditioned Multi-Instance Open-Vocabulary Sound Event Localization
items.summary: We study query-conditioned multi-instance open-vocabulary sound event localization (QC-MI-OVSEL), where a system must recover all active physical sources matching a natural-language category query, including when the queried category is absent. We introduce the QC-MI-OVSEL benchmark, a 40,000-scene first-order Ambisonics benchmark with 80,000 balanced present/absent query views over 83 classes, including 17 novel classes excluded from training and development. Each frame is annotated with the activity and 3-D direction of every query-matching source, with up to three simultaneous targets. We further propose Q-RSet, which uses query-conditioned source slots and responsibility-based evidence aggregation for source-set prediction. Experiments show improved source recovery, localization recall, cardinality estimation, exact-set recovery, and absent-query suppression over complementary baselines. Analysis indicates that novel categories, paraphrased queries, and higher source multiplicity mainly impair source discovery and set completion, while directional accuracy remains comparatively stable for successfully recovered sources.

items.title: Featurized Occupation Measures for Structured Global Search in Numerical Optimal Control
items.summary: Numerical optimal control is split between globally structured but dimensionally intractable Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) methods and scalable but local trajectory optimization. We introduce Featurized Occupation Measures (FOM), a finite-dimensional primal--dual interface where HJB subsolutions guide primal search and primal occupation data can inform certificate refinement. Explicit and implicit realizations, based on finite Liouville tests and rollout-sampled residuals, are proved asymptotically consistent with the exact occupation-measure LP. FOM also identifies when HJB-type certificates avoid full state-space representation. For factor graphs induced by compatible passivity-based interconnections, blockwise HJB inequalities yield block-additive OM-dual certificates, including blockwise approximate variants. The curse of dimensionality is then shifted from state dimension to interconnection topology. Approximate certificates remain reusable under time shifts and bounded model perturbations, with explicit degradation bounds. A static obstacle-avoidance benchmark illustrates how tighter certificates improve sample-based global search.

items.title: How Should We Evaluate Naturalness for Synthetic Speech with a Foreign Accent?
items.summary: Recent advances in speech synthesis technology have enabled the generation of speech with diverse characteristics. One such characteristic is a foreign accent. In our preliminary experiments, we found that UTMOS, a widely used automatic speech quality assessment system, tended to assign lower scores to speech with stronger foreign accents, even though it is produced by a human speaker. This observation raised a question: How do humans evaluate the naturalness of foreign-accented speech? We conducted a large-scale subjective evaluation involving both native and non-native listeners under different evaluation instructions. The results showed that humans also considered accentedness when evaluating naturalness, but that defining naturalness in terms of human-likeness and selecting raters who have greater exposure to the target accent may enable more appropriate evaluation. This study aims to provide a starting point for future discussions on fairer and more appropriate evaluation of synthetic speech with a foreign accent.

items.title: Modelling the Nordic power system expansion with PyPSA-Eur: a comparison with the Nordic Grid Development Perspective 2025
items.summary: We compare the Nordic Grid Development Perspective 2025 (NGDP) with a least-cost transition pathway for the Nordic power system obtained with PyPSA-Eur for the period 2025-2050 under a net-zero CO$_2$ constraint. The model co-optimises generation, storage, and transmission expansion with hourly system operation while constraining the Nordic generation mix to remain consistent with NGDP milestone ranges. Overall, the optimised capacity pathways reproduce the broad NGDP expansion of wind and solar power, with Denmark emerging as the main locus of offshore wind and solar deployment, Finland as a major site for onshore wind expansion, and Norway and Sweden relying more strongly on existing hydropower and nuclear capacity. The main discrepancy between the two pathways does not lie in the broad build-out of variable renewables, but in the timing and role of hydrogen. Whereas the NGDP treats hydrogen as an early and steadily increasing component of industrial demand and system development already from 2030, PyPSA-Eur delays substantial hydrogen deployment until 2045-2050, when it becomes cost-effective primarily as a flexibility and seasonal storage option in a strongly variable-renewable-energy-dominated system. This contrast suggests that early hydrogen build-out in the Nordics is not a robust outcome of cost optimisation alone, but depends strongly on assumptions regarding industrial demand growth, sector coupling, and anticipatory infrastructure planning. We therefore argue that hydrogen remains the principal strategic uncertainty in the Nordic transition, with the NGDP representing a more anticipatory planning perspective and PyPSA-Eur a more conservative least-cost timing of deployment.

items.title: Extended Neighborhood Message Passing for Inference in Loopy Factor Graphs
items.summary: Belief propagation (BP) is widely used for inference on probabilistic graphical models but often suffers from non-convergence and poor accuracy on loopy factor graphs, yielding inexact variance estimates in the Gaussian case. Generalized BP (GBP) improves accuracy but relies on manual design or application-specific heuristics for region-graph construction. We propose extended neighborhood message passing (ENMP), which automatically constructs extended neighborhoods of variable nodes from the bipartite factor graph topology, capturing loop-induced correlations without manual region design. The framework applies to general distributions on factor graphs with a tunable accuracy-complexity trade-off. In the exact regime, message updates converge to the unique fixed point of the ENMP equations in finitely many iterations, yielding exact marginals; in the approximate regime, ENMP provides approximate marginals. For Gaussian factor graphs, we derive closed-form update rules enabling exact variance estimation in the exact regime, addressing the long-standing inaccurate variance estimates of loopy Gaussian BP. We evaluate ENMP on densely loopy Gaussian factor graphs from power-grid benchmarks and on a discrete Ising factor graph. Results show accuracy improves with neighborhood size, with exact marginals achieved on several systems in both settings. On larger Gaussian systems, ENMP outperforms regularized Gaussian BP (sGaBP-m) in both mean and variance estimation accuracy.

items.title: Rethinking Entropy Allocation in LLM-based ASR: Understanding the Dynamics between Speech Encoders and LLMs
items.summary: Integrating large language models (LLMs) into automatic speech recognition (ASR) has become a dominant paradigm. Although recent LLM-based ASR models have shown promising performance on public benchmarks, it remains challenging to balance recognition quality with latency and overhead, while hallucinations further limit real-world deployment. In this study, we revisit LLM-based ASR from an entropy allocation perspective and introduce three metrics to characterize how training paradigms allocate entropy reduction between the speech encoder and the LLM. To remedy entropy-allocation inefficiencies in prevailing approaches, we propose a principled multi-stage training strategy grounded in capability-boundary awareness, optimizing parameter efficiency and hallucination robustness. Specifically, we redesign the pretraining strategy to alleviate the speech-text modality gap, and further introduce an iterative asynchronous SFT stage between alignment and joint SFT to preserve functional decoupling and constrain encoder representation drift. Experiments on Mandarin and English benchmarks show that our method achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art models using only 2.3B parameters, while also effectively mitigating hallucinations through our decoupling-oriented design.

items.title: Does Location Matter? A Black-Box Causal Audit Reveals Model-Dependent Audio Grounding in LALM Hallucination
items.summary: Large audio-language models (LALMs) frequently exhibit object hallucination, affirming absent sounds. The dominant mitigation, Audio-Aware Decoding (AAD), contrasts logits under real audio against an all-zero "blank" waveform, flagged by prior review as out-of-distribution. We introduce a black-box causal test that isolates the claimed evidence itself: localize a claim's evidence region via CLAP similarity, remove it by spectral gating, and compare against a random-window control across a 2x2x2 grid on three LALMs. On Qwen2-Audio-7B, localized ablation's raw AUROC trails blank's (0.613 vs. 0.721); this is a duration confound, not a localization failure, since blank removes the entire clip versus the grid's 2-4 s. Holding duration fixed, localization beats random removal at every cell on both models. Raw detection value remains model-dependent, especially on Audio Flamingo 3. The same evidence corrects decoding: contrastive decoding combining blank and language-prior contrasts, gated and ensembled, raises Qwen2-Audio accuracy from 57.1% to 71.9%, beating AAD alone. A unified causal-grounding profile does not transfer between models, indicating different grounding regimes. The source code and a detailed report of our findings, including identified limitations, are available at https://github.com/khalooei/causa.

items.title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
items.summary: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.

items.title: From 2.1M Hours of Raw Broadcast Audio to Finnish Speech SSL: Confidence Filtering and Architectural Analysis at Scale
items.summary: Broadcast archives offer scale and diversity for self-supervised learning (SSL) but contain substantial noisy, non-speech, and multilingual content. Prior work typically relies on voice activity detection or language identification (LID) to extract speech, ensuring presence rather than quality. Whether and how to filter unlabeled speech by quality for SSL, particularly from noisy broadcasts, remains underexplored. We present a large-scale Finnish SSL study starting from 2.1M hours of unconstrained broadcast audio. We propose automatic speech recognition (ASR) confidence as a proxy for pretraining data quality and show 3-7% relative WER improvements over LID-based filtering despite a smaller training set. We further address the lack of controlled architectural comparisons in speech SSL by evaluating Transformer, Macaron-Net, Conformer, and E-Branchformer at matched parameter budgets. Our models improve upon prior Finnish SSL baselines, particularly at Base scale and out-of-domain.

items.title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
items.summary: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.

items.title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count
items.summary: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.

items.title: AV-FlowEdit: Training-Free Prompt-Driven Audio-Visual Editing with Event-Aware Spectral Trajectory Preservation
items.summary: Joint audio-video diffusion models generate synchronized content, but editing existing clips requires target changes without disrupting non-target structure or cross-modal correspondence. We present AV-FlowEdit, a training-free and inversion-free framework for prompt-driven audio-video editing. Our key insight is that source--target flow differences provide both cross-modal editing directions and preservation cues. Under shared perturbations, they jointly update the video and audio branches, supporting visual-only, audio-only, and joint edits while retaining pretrained cross-modal interactions. To suppress drift accumulated during sampling, Cross-Modal Event-Aware Spectral Trajectory Preservation combines flow saliency, aligned audio activity, multiscale low-frequency displacement, and diffusion-stage scheduling. This adaptively preserves unsupported regions while allowing intended audio-visual events. AV-FlowEdit requires no model training, external masks, or optimization-based inversion. Experiments show strong prompt alignment and temporal consistency, together with competitive audio quality and cross-modal coherence.

items.title: Learning event-triggered controllers for linear parameter-varying systems from data
items.summary: Nonlinear dynamical behaviors in engineering applications can be approximated by linear-parameter varying (LPV) representations, but obtaining precise model knowledge to develop a control algorithm is difficult in practice. In this paper, we develop data-driven control strategies for event-triggered linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems with stability verifications. First, we theoretically analyze the $θ$-persistence of excitation condition for LPV systems, which leads to feasible data-based representations. Then, in terms of the available perturbed data, we establish the stability certificates for event-triggered LPV systems with the aid of Petersen's lemma, in the sense of robust control, resulting in computationally tractable semidefinite programs whose feasible solutions yield the gain-scheduling controllers. Besides, we generalize the data-driven event-triggered LPV stabilization methods to the case of trajectory tracking, and discuss robust tracking stability accordingly. Finally, we verify the effectiveness of our theoretical derivations through numerical examples.

items.title: LiveSynth: A Streaming Neural Synthesizer for Instrument Cloning and Text-to-Instrument
items.summary: Recently, generative neural synthesizers have enabled zero-shot instrument cloning from reference recordings and timbre generation from text prompts. However, existing systems generate complete audio segments offline, precluding their use as playable instruments. We present LiveSynth, a streaming neural synthesizer with flexible timbre control and interactive generation capabilities, including zero-shot instrument cloning and text-to-instrument synthesis. A feedback-free causal Transformer conditioned on MIDI events and a CLAP timbre embedding outputs continuous audio latents at 100 Hz, which a causal variational autoencoder decodes into audio. Frame-wise timbre conditioning enables continuous timbre morphing, while MIDI-conditioning dropout enables autonomous continuation from a performed prefix. On the NSynth and Slakh datasets, LiveSynth achieved timbre similarity and spectral reconstruction quality comparable to offline baselines. On an M3 MacBook Air, LiveSynth required 8.8 ms of computation per 10 ms audio frame (an RTF of 0.88) with 10 ms algorithmic latency, enabling real-time interaction with a performer.

items.title: Fairness-Guided DQN-Based TXOP Control for NR-U/Wi-Fi Coexistence
items.summary: New Radio operating in unlicensed spectrum (NR-U) and Wi-Fi employ different contention parameters and channel-occupancy durations, which can produce severe coexistence imbalance. This correspondence develops a fairness-guided deep Q-network (DQN) that adjusts the NR-U transmission opportunity (TXOP) using the observed per-node throughput ratio. Two reward designs, Q1 and Q2, expose complementary operating regimes. Q1 promotes strict per-node throughput balance, whereas Q2 admits a broader inter-radio-access-technology fairness region and rewards throughput improvement in an intermediate fairness band. The policies are compared with the default Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) listen-before-talk (LBT), an adapted multi-armed-bandit method, a utility-fairness-based tabular Q-learning comparator, and a default-referenced fixed-TXOP baseline. Experiments across four priority classes and asymmetric populations report aggregate throughput, user-level Jain fairness, and concave throughput utility over 20 independent trials. The results characterize the cost of strict fairness, efficiency recovery under moderate relaxation, and transfer from symmetric to asymmetric deployments.

items.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
items.summary: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.

items.title: Virtual Transmission Lines from Data Center Workload Migration: Coordinated Multi-Year Transmission Expansion Planning
items.summary: The rapid growth of electricity demand from AI data centers is creating a dual mismatch in power systems: a temporal mismatch between fast-rising demand and slow transmission expansion, and a spatial mismatch between concentrated data-center loads and geographically dispersed renewable resources. These mismatches can exacerbate transmission congestion, resulting in unserved data-center load and renewable-energy curtailment. This study models geographic workload migration as a virtual transmission line (VTL) that changes nodal data-center demand without transferring physical electricity. A mixed-integer linear programming model is then developed to co-optimize multi-year candidate-line construction and workload migration, subject to construction delays, renewable-energy curtailment, unserved data-center load, workload-balance requirements, communication-bandwidth constraints, and link-latency limits. The model is evaluated over an eight-year planning horizon on a modified IEEE 14-bus system. The results show that coordinating VTL with physical transmission expansion reduces total system cost, unserved data-center load, and renewable-energy curtailment while alleviating transmission congestion. VTL-aware planning also requires one fewer candidate line than build-only planning. However, VTL alone cannot meet system demand and does not eliminate the need for physical transmission reinforcement. Sensitivity analysis indicates that VTL provides the greatest value when transfer capacity is tight, construction costs are high, load growth is rapid, and data-center flexibility is greater. Additional validation on the IEEE 118-bus system over a five-year planning horizon shows that coordinated planning retains its cost and reliability benefits while reducing physical expansion requirements.

items.title: One-Bin Fourier Challenges for Dimension-Free Reconstruction Certification
items.summary: Partial-Fourier measurement underlies computational imaging, and its reconstructions increasingly come from iterative or learned solvers whose recovery guarantees are conditional on a signal model, a sampling law, and solver accuracy. None of those guarantees transfers to a particular committed output: it can satisfy every acquired coefficient while remaining badly wrong in the unmeasured nullspace. Native Fourier holdout does not repair this, since a spectrally concentrated error is missed unless its bin is drawn, so uniform worst-case risk needs a number of hidden bins proportional to the dimension. We propose a post-commit acceptance test: secret finite-phase masks turn one fixed Fourier readout into dense randomized residual checks, and a median-of-means threshold handles calibrated readout noise. We prove that errors above $E_{\rm rej}$ are rejected and errors below $E_{\rm acc}$ are accepted with confidence $1-δ$ once $q\ge C(1+Nσ^2/E_{\rm rej})^2\log(1/δ)$, explicitly exposing the one-bin resolution floor $Nσ^2/\sqrt q$; in the zero-noise limit, QPSK gives $4^{-q}$ soundness versus $97.9\%$ minimax false acceptance for a worst-case ordinary-bin error. At a fixed noise-to-threshold ratio, measured screening false acceptance fell from about $21\%$ at 16 checks to $5\%$ at 64; a data-consistent learned nullspace failure with NMSE $0.200$ was rejected by $96.9\%$ of challenge banks while 16 ordinary bins missed it $98.9\%$ of the time; and error statistics at 16 checks stayed stable from 128 through $65{,}536$ dimensions. The test supports solver acceptance, model selection, and stopping certification, with a certified fresh-bank error interval.

items.title: Quadratic Characterizations for Reachability Analysis of Neural Networks
items.summary: Quadratic constraints (QCs) are widely used to characterize nonlinearities and uncertainties, but generic analytical characterizations can be conservative on bounded domains. This paper develops a framework for constructing verified quadratic characterizations of scalar relations in the two-dimensional real plane. Candidate quadratic inequalities are locally generated by solving convex quadratic programs using samples from the relation and exterior sample points. They are then verified globally using sum-of-squares certificates over an exact semialgebraic description or, in the case of nonpolynomial relations, over relaxed polynomial descriptions. The resulting verified constraints define a sound overapproximation of the scalar relations over the considered domains. These constraints are directly compatible with existing analysis frameworks based on QCs and pointwise integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) for static nonlinearities and uncertainties, and they can also be embedded in QC-based semidefinite programs for reachability and safety analysis of feedforward neural networks. For smooth activations such as $\tanh$, the method yields domain-dependent quadratic characterizations that constitute an alternative to generic sector- or slope-based descriptions. For ReLU networks, we give methods to reduce conservatism in QC-based reachability analysis of feedforward networks by exploiting dependencies between neurons and tighter local bounds. Numerical examples demonstrate improved reachability results for smooth activations, reduced conservatism for ReLU networks, and applicability beyond neural networks through an example involving saturation.

items.title: Compressibility is not Feedback: A Random-access Gap in Causal Semantic Repair
items.summary: Semantic feedback can repair a noisy first decode without retransmitting the whole message, but current end-to-end evaluations hide where a feedback design fails. An oracle that sees both the source-side state and receiver observation may describe a useful correction with few bits, while the receiver, which sees only its own observation, may not know which correction to request. We formulate these as distinct direct and receiver-constrained coding problems, connect repair distortion to retained local utility and prove a random-access separation: one direct bit is exact although receiver utility vanishes with the number of source-conditioned alternatives. A synthetic ladder verifies the exact law. In paired populations of eight Reuters text-JSCC codecs, the trained recurrent population retains over three times more direct 16-bit repair value than the trained DeepSC population despite comparable full-repair opportunity. Nevertheless, an entropy-valid receiver audit across all eight recurrent checkpoints does not resolve against repetition, source-only or shuffled-index controls. The results show that compressible repair is an upper bound, not evidence of deployable feedback, and motivate reporting both rate curves under matched resources.

items.title: Mean Gain Is Not a Guarantee: Risk-Controlled Open-Loop Scheduling for Ka-Band LEO Semantic Downlinks
items.summary: A low-Earth-orbit satellite has only minutes to downlink imagery on a limited power budget, and some moments in a pass carry far better channels than others. Spending more power on the good moments and skipping hopeless ones should deliver more images, but the channel cannot be measured in time, so the schedule is planned in advance from weather statistics using a safety margin. That margin is sized so the forecast is statistically reliable, and the scheduler is judged by whether it beats uniform power on average. Both targets are wrong for a satellite that gets one attempt per pass: on real Sentinel-2 imagery, a scheduler gaining one to two images per pass on average still delivers fewer than uniform power on a quarter to a third of individual passes, and a genie knowing the weather exactly does no better. We instead size the margin by measuring, on recorded passes, how often it would have backfired, keeping only settings that provably backfire rarely. The procedure declines to schedule our learned codec and certifies scheduling for codecs with a sharper cliff.

items.title: E3-System: Expressive EmoData, Explicitly Controllable, Easy-to-Use TTS
items.summary: Recent zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems can clone unseen speakers, yet controllable expressiveness remains limited by a gap between semantic intent and acoustic realization. Text descriptions offer a natural control interface but provide weak acoustic grounding, whereas speech style prompts provide concrete prosody but entangle style with the prompt speaker's timbre. To bridge this gap, we propose E3-System, a unified intent-to-speech framework for expressive zero-shot TTS that couples three requirements: Expressive style modeling, Explicit timbre-style control, and Easy-to-use natural-language interaction. Given a target speaker and either a natural-language style description or a speech style prompt, E3-System generates expressive speech while preserving the target timbre. The key idea is to close the full control loop: building a large expressive style space, grounding user intent into usable acoustic style references, and synthesizing speech with disentangled timbre and style. To realize this loop, EmoData provides a thousand-hour multilingual emotional speech dataset, Style-RAG grounds text descriptions into high-quality acoustic style prompts from these data, and Dual-TTS transfers the grounded style to arbitrary target speakers through VC-augmented timbre-style disentanglement. Experiments show that E3-System achieves strong speech quality, speaker preservation, and explicit expressive controllability.

items.title: Emo-BPO: Emotion Bidirectional Preference Optimization for Diffusion-based Emotional TTS
items.summary: Diffusion-based TTS has demonstrated strong capability in emotional speech generation. However, existing emotion alignment methods primarily reinforce target emotional expressions while overlooking modeling of competing emotional modes, limiting fine-grained controllability. This issue becomes more pronounced under classifier-free guidance (CFG), which relies on contrasting conditional trajectories to shape generation. We propose Emotion Bidirectional Preference Optimization (Emo-BPO), a simple effective framework that jointly learns emotion-aligned and emotion-contrastive score functions from reordered same-text emotional pairs. Our method requires neither auxiliary reward models nor additional annotations, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing diffusion-based TTS systems to improve emotional controllability and expressiveness.

items.title: Low, High, and Semantic-Level Vision-Language Learning for AI-Generated Image Detection
items.summary: Driven by advances in diffusion models and autoregressive models, the fidelity and resolution of AI-generated images now rival those of real images. However, existing AI-generated image detection methods often downsample the images,inevitably overlooking critical low-level texture details in high-resolution AI-generated images, thereby limiting their detection performance. In addition, the continuous emergence of unknown generative models makes large-scale pre-training datasets inaccessible. To address these challenges, we propose a novel AI-generated image detector, termed LHSDet (Low-, High-, and Semantic-level Detection). Specifically, we formulate the AI-generated image detection task as a Visual Question Answering problem, leveraging a fine-tuned vision-language framework to fully exploit the complementary information between visual and textual modalities. Recognizing that the default visual encoder of existing vision-language models is not tailored for AI-generated image detection, we redesign a visual encoder to better capture both the low-level and high-level artifacts inherent in AI-generated images. Furthermore, we incorporate a semantic-level textual branch to enable multi-modal feature fusion and detection. Consequently, LHSDet employs a triple-branch architecture to extract complementary multi-modal features: a low-level visual branch that aggregates non-overlapping patches for local texture cues, a high-level visual branch based on SigLIP2 for global perception feature extraction,and a semantic-level textual branch that generates captions using BLIP-2. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that LHSDet achieves strong detection accuracy and robust performance across diverse generative models.

items.title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors
items.summary: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.

items.title: SecFD-FL: Frequency-Decoupled Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation for Charging Load Forecasting in Internet of Electric Vehicles
items.summary: Accurate charging load forecasting is essential for the reliability and efficiency of the Internet of Electric Vehicles (IoEV), yet it is challenging on two fronts: charging demand is highly stochastic, and the data collected by distributed sensors is privacy-sensitive. Although federated learning (FL) preserves data privacy, collaborative training still remains vulnerable to an honest-but-curious server that can invert shared model updates to reconstruct private data. To address both data volatility and privacy concerns, we propose SecFD-FL, a frequency-decoupled federated learning framework for IoEV comprising: 1) a dual-stream gated recurrent unit (GRU) network that separately models short-term and long-term charging load volatility, and 2) a lightweight secure aggregation layer for privacy preservation. Specifically, the secure aggregation layer employs a zero-sum additive masking protocol that perturbs each client's upload with high-variance noise, preventing the server from reconstructing private data while preserving the exact aggregate. Extensive experiments have been conducted on both EV-level and charging station-level using real datasets. The experiment results show that SecFD-FL reduces global RMSE by up to 60% over centralized baselines, achieving Jain's fairness up to 0.991 across clients, and reduces DLG-attack reconstruction correlation by 8 times to 15 times relative to FedAvg -- all with no additional per-round communication cost beyond a one-time key exchange.

items.title: Fast-DeePC: Fast Data-Enabled Predictive Control using Soft-constrained Scheme
items.summary: Data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) replaces the explicit system model of model predictive control with a data-driven predictor built directly from recorded input-output trajectories, but the original hard-equality formulation keeps its coordinate vector as an online decision variable whose size grows with the offline data length, so the online problem grows more expensive as more data is used to enrich the behavioral representation. This article proposes Fast-DeePC, a framework which relaxes this consistency relation into the control objective with a quadratic ridge on the coordinate vector in place of the customary sparsity-promoting penalty, admitting a closed-form, offline elimination of the coordinate vector and reducing the online problem to a fixed-size box-constrained quadratic program solved by a structure-exploiting interior-point method. On identical soft quadratically regularized problems, the result matches a general-purpose solver's solution and is up to two orders of magnitude faster.

items.title: Credit-Based vs. Discount-Based Congestion Pricing: A Comparison Study
items.summary: Credit-based congestion pricing (CBCP) and discount-based congestion pricing (DBCP), which respectively allot travel credits and toll discounts to subsidize low-income users' access to tolled roads, have emerged as promising policies for alleviating the societal inequity concerns of congestion pricing. However, since real-world deployments of CBCP and DBCP remain limited, transportation agencies lack clear guidance on which policy better achieves travel cost reduction and revenue generation objectives. In this work, we compare the efficacy of deploying CBCP and DBCP in reducing user costs and increasing toll revenues. We first formulate a non-atomic congestion game in which low-income users receive a travel credit or toll discount for accessing tolled lanes. We establish that, in our formulation, Nash equilibrium flows always exist and can be computed or well approximated via convex programming. Our main result establishes a set of practically relevant conditions under which DBCP provably outperforms CBCP in inducing equilibrium outcomes that minimize a given societal cost, which encodes user cost reduction and toll revenue maximization. Finally, we validate our theoretical contributions via a case study of the 101 Express Lanes Project, a CBCP program implemented in the San Francisco Bay Area. Our results provide theoretical and computational foundations for evaluating equity-oriented congestion pricing policies and offer practical guidance for transportation agencies seeking to design congestion pricing programs that better balance travel cost reduction and revenue generation objectives.

items.title: Closed-loop domain generation enhances battery health diagnosis
items.summary: Reliable electrode-level degradation diagnosis is essential for accurate health estimation and non-destructive monitoring in advanced battery management. Diagnosis models developed under controlled laboratory conditions can fail when operating conditions change, while acquiring sufficient full-lifespan data in new target domains remains prohibitively time-consuming and practically unfeasible. Here, we propose a closed-loop domain generation framework to enable cross-domain battery health diagnosis under dynamic conditions. Physics-constrained domain generation is achieved through Variational Autoencoder-based latent extrapolation, which maps the source data and few-shot early-life target domain data into a shared latent space and generates cross-domain samples within physical boundaries. Bayesian optimization closes the generation-diagnosis loop by automatically calibrating the sampling, latent regularization, extrapolation, perturbation, and generation-volume hyperparameters using leakage-free development validation, thereby strictly excluding later-life target data from optimization and ensuring the quality and quantity of generated data. Numerical results demonstrate that, across four cross-domain cases, the proposed framework achieves average root mean square errors of 1.53%, 2.15%, and 2.02% for positive electrode active material loss, negative electrode active material loss, and lithium inventory loss, respectively, whereas traditional methods suffer from notably higher errors or even complete failure. This framework provides a general pathway for onboard and physics-consistent electrode-level degradation diagnosis, independent of downstream diagnosis models.

items.title: A Multi-Scenario UAV RF Dataset with Real-World Acquisition and Signal Processing Benchmarking
items.summary: We present a real-world multi-scenario unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) radio frequency (RF) dataset, namely DRFF-R2, which is collected using a dedicated acquisition platform under diverse operational conditions. All signals are acquired within a unified framework to ensure consistency in hardware configuration and environmental settings. The dataset is systematically organized into seven well-defined subsets corresponding to different operational and signal composition scenarios to facilitate structured experimentation. Each file follows a clearly annotated naming convention to enable convenient data indexing and reproducible analysis. The dataset contains RF recordings from 26 UAV units spanning 8 distinct models, captured across varying flight states, altitudes, speeds, acquisition days, and receiver configurations. By covering diverse acquisition settings and signal compositions, the dataset provides a comprehensive resource for future UAV RF signal research, including RF fingerprinting (RFF) identification, model-level recognition, flight state analysis, time-varying RFF study, and interference-aware signal processing.

items.title: Input-Correlated Supervision Noise Limits the Benefits of OTA Training for Learned Receivers
items.summary: While learned wireless receivers are typically studied using synthetic data, the impact of over-the-air (OTA) measurements for training remains unclear. We conducted a 5.88 GHz measurement campaign with a 5G/6G-like orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system across diverse environments and mobility conditions, and trained a neural channel estimator and a capacity-matched end-to-end neural receiver using mixtures of measured and synthetic data. Increasing the OTA fraction revealed a fundamental asymmetry: measured data consistently improved the end-to-end receiver, whereas the channel estimator peaked at an intermediate fraction and degraded with fully measured training. We identified supervision quality as a key contributor: OTA channel labels are derived from noisy received signals and therefore contain supervision errors correlated with the receiver input, whereas decoded bits validated by a cyclic redundancy check (CRC) provide effectively error-free supervision. Denoising the channel labels mitigated the degradation, and a controlled simulation showed that label noise of equal power degrades the estimator far more when it is correlated with the input. For OTA training, end-to-end receivers thus benefit from fully measured data, whereas channel estimators benefit from moderate OTA fractions but require improved label quality.

items.title: Demonstration Calibrated Port-Hamiltonian Retuning for Manipulation Policies
items.summary: Diffusion and VLA policies for manipulation are often deployed through downstream impedance controllers. The stiffness and damping gains of these controllers affect task success, yet are commonly inherited from data collection rather than selected for the deployed policy. Although empirical gain sweeps can improve performance, they require repeated evaluation rollouts. We introduce PHRetune, an offline method that derives controller gains for a frozen policy without evaluation rollouts or gain search. Our approach learns a port-Hamiltonian model from demonstrations to estimate the effort and energy associated with the policy's predicted actions. The policy is applied to recorded demonstration observations, and its predictions are assessed against demonstration-derived effort and energy budgets. From this comparison, we derive a single gain scale in closed form, adjusting the downstream controller while preserving the policy and its action representation. The gains are fixed before evaluation, without requiring a prior manipulator model, task rewards, policy retraining, or additional runtime computation. Across LIBERO suites, PHRetune improves Diffusion Policy success by up to 9.4 percentage points, with the derived gains achieving the highest observed success rates in empirical gain sweeps. On all four real-world manipulation tasks, PHRetuned Diffusion Policy outperforms the nominal policy, alternative gain-tuning methods, and a policy-retraining baseline. The same procedure improves success with SmolVLA and OpenVLA-OFT on every task, while reducing acceleration and jerk for both VLA backbones.

items.title: Adaptive Node Distribution via Probability Density Functions for Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
items.summary: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.

items.title: Inverse Synthesis of Shock Time Series from Shock Response Spectra Using Ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders
items.summary: The shock response spectrum (SRS) characterizes the peak responses of single-degree-of-freedom systems to transient acceleration. Because the mapping from an acceleration time series (waveform) to its SRS is many-to-one, inverse synthesis seeks candidate waveforms consistent with a prescribed spectrum. We extend an earlier conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) framework with a recurrent decoder that predicts multiscale wavelet coefficients and reconstructs waveforms through an inverse discrete wavelet transform. Individual models exhibit limited variability under latent sampling, motivating an ensemble of independently trained models spanning different mother wavelets and decomposition levels. Each member produces a separate candidate waveform for the same target SRS. Evaluation on four held-out benchmark datasets shows lower mean and median spectral errors for the illustrated wavelet model than for the earlier direct time-domain CVAE and a sum-of-decayed-sinusoids (SDS) baseline. A conditioning study examines frequency-grid and encoding choices. Comparisons with published inverse-SRS methods demonstrate superior performance across four holdout benchmark datasets (two operational shock datasets, one earthquake dataset, and one synthetic shock dataset) and competitive performance on synthetic targets reported by Brake. Single-model inference requires approximately 0.1-0.6 ms per waveform during batched inference compared with 5-8 s for SDS, excluding offline training. This low inference cost enables rapid generation of distinct SRS-compatible candidate waveforms across the ensemble, although their physical suitability requires assessment beyond spectral agreement.

items.title: Deploying RDMA for Large-Scale Inference and Training Workloads
items.summary: RDMA can reduce communication overhead in distributed machine learning systems, but realizing these benefits in production requires more than replacing TCP. Variable-size messages, concurrent connections, bursty incasts, and service failures introduce challenges that hardware offload alone cannot address. This paper reports our experience deploying ByteExpress, a software communication layer over hardware RDMA, in ByteDance's parameter-server-based inference and training systems. We present three lessons from the deployment: efficient RDMA requires buffer management across application and transport layers; scalable communication requires coordinated management of connections, receive capacity, and outstanding data; and service availability requires recovery above the transport layer. ByteExpress combines an RDMA-aware allocator, zero-copy transfers, QP multiplexing, receive-credit flow control, a software send window, and RPC-assisted recovery. In production inference, ByteExpress reduces mean and P99 model parameter fetch latency by 35.7% and 43.7%, respectively, and total CPU usage by 10.69% compared with kernel TCP. In training, ByteExpress reduces P99 model parameter push latency by up to 74.0% compared with TCP, with no PFC pauses observed at runtime.

items.title: Spend Where It Matters: Particle Search with MH Refinement for Budget-Constrained Audio-Visual Alignment
items.summary: Reward-guided inference-time alignment can improve joint audio-visual generation, but optimizing multiple alignment objectives requires many expensive model evaluations, making existing methods costly under limited compute. Particle-based search enables global exploration but incurs estimation error with a finite population, while Metropolis-Hastings (MH) can refine candidates locally but benefits from a strong initialization. We introduce \textbf{S}pend \textbf{W}here \textbf{I}t \textbf{M}atters (\modelname), a two-stage, training-free, reward-agnostic framework that combines particle search with MH refinement under a fixed compute budget. In the first stage, we adaptively allocate particles across denoising checkpoints using online variance estimates, minimizing estimation variance while concentrating compute where it is most useful. This search provides a promising candidate for MH refinement, which uses local noise-and-denoise proposals on completed outputs to further improve reward. By starting from a strong candidate, MH can recover additional reward without requiring a larger particle population or costly global exploration. We show that, at matched compute, combining particle search with MH refinement achieves higher rewards than either approach alone. On \textsc{JavisBench-Mini}, at closely matched compute, \modelname achieves mean relative gains across seven metrics of $30.7\%$ over BoN and $14.1\%$ over EvoSearch with JavisDiT++, and $9.2\%$ over BoN and $17.0\%$ over EvoSearch with LTX-2. Beyond joint audio-visual generation, we also demonstrate the benefits of adaptive particle allocation on SD1.5 image generation, improving AestheticScore by $2.2\%$ and ImageReward by $6.0\%$ over uniform allocation.

items.title: Efficient Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning-Based Neural Architecture Search
items.summary: Audio-visual speech enhancement (AVSE) improves speech intelligibility in noisy environments but often relies on computationally expensive models unsuitable for resource-constrained edge devices. This paper introduces a reinforcement learning-driven neural architecture search (RL-NAS) framework to discover compact, efficient AVSE architectures. The search space preserves temporal alignment between audio and visual streams, while a novel reward function jointly optimises speech enhancement performance, measured by SI-SNR improvement, and model compactness. Using proximal policy optimisation with constraint-aware action masking, the framework evaluates only 35 candidate architectures and identifies a model with 2.9 million parameters, compared with 22 million in the baseline. The proposed architecture achieves a 14.5 dB SI-SNR improvement, only 0.7 dB below the baseline, while reducing model size by approximately nine-fold. Evaluation on commercial mobile CPUs demonstrates a 4.3-fold reduction in real-time factor, supporting practical on-device deployment. Compared with random search, RL-NAS achieves 92% higher search efficiency. Architectural analysis reveals that shallower but wider temporal convolutional blocks and aggressive visual pathway pruning can maintain enhancement performance while substantially reducing computational requirements. These findings demonstrate the potential of reinforcement learning-guided architecture search for developing lightweight, efficient and deployable multimodal speech enhancement systems.

items.title: From Optimal Transport to Optimal Quantization: A Variational Study of the Witsenhausen Counterexample
items.summary: Witsenhausen's counterexample is a canonical problem in decentralized control: a two-stage linear-quadratic-Gaussian team problem in which nonlinear policies strictly outperform every affine one. This paper develops a variational and computational framework for the scalar counterexample based on optimal transport. Building on the transport formulation of Wu and Verdú, we absorb the first controller into a transport map and recast the problem as $J^\star=\inf_Q\{k^2W_2^2(P,Q)+\mathrm{mmse}(Q)\}$, which trades a quadratic Wasserstein transport cost against a minimum mean-square estimation error. The optimal first controller is the monotone rearrangement that pushes the prior $P$ to a minimizer $Q^\star$. We establish the existence and absolute continuity of minimizers, derive an Euler--Lagrange optimality condition, and obtain a semi-closed-form Gaussian benchmark with an explicit second-variation stability threshold. We then show that restricting to finitely supported laws yields an MMSE-regularized optimal quantizer: its optimal values decrease to $J^\star$, its weak limit points are minimizers of the continuous problem, and its stationarity conditions pair centroid levels with power cells, recovering Lloyd--Max quantization as control becomes expensive. This structure leads to an estimation-aware Lloyd algorithm with signalling-based initialization. As $k\to\infty$, the optimal controllers converge to the classical affine pair; as $k\to0$, $J^\star(k)=σ^2k^2+o(k^2)$ and the optimal laws collapse onto $δ_0$, so signalling constellations are a moderate-$k$ phenomenon. Numerical experiments corroborate the theory, and the framework extends to the vector counterexample, where the finite-level program becomes an MMSE-regularized vector quantizer.

items.title: Game Petri Nets: Compositional Modeling and Analysis of Large-Scale Strategic Systems
items.summary: Large-scale strategic systems, such as maintenance workflows, cyber campaigns, and multi-agent AI pipelines, consist of many interactions whose outcomes determine which later interactions become possible, who takes part, and with what resources. We introduce game Petri nets, formalized as outcome-driven compositional game Petri nets (OCGPNs), to model and analyze such systems. Local games are attached to places of a colored Petri net, and a game-to-token interface converts each resolved game into typed tokens that enable, synchronize, or block subsequent games. For general, concurrent nets, we give an operational semantics and a structural theory based on invariants and Farkas certificates, which shows that guards can certify unreachability whereas incentive instruments can only change values. For sequential nets, the net induces a stochastic game on its game places. We prove that global equilibria are exactly collections of equilibria of local games augmented by continuation values, characterize through successor-level pivotality when downstream games change upstream behavior, and compute values place by place via a decomposition into strongly connected components, at a cost additive in local game sizes. A composition calculus based on place fusion glues certificates across subnets and summarizes downstream subnets by their entry values. Two running examples, a maintenance workflow and an intrusion campaign derived from multi-resolution cyber-defense games, illustrate the theory, including the composition of a newly discovered attack scenario with an existing campaign.

items.title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations
items.summary: Autonomous small-body proximity operations require continuous-thrust guidance under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure (SRP), and stochastic disturbances. We combine iterative covariance steering (iCS) with $L_1$ distributionally robust adaptive control ($L_1$-DRAC) to provide risk-aware collision avoidance despite mismatch between the nominal planning model and the true dynamics. Iterative covariance steering plans a nominal feedback policy satisfying distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints, while $L_1$-DRAC compensates for dynamics uncertainty and bounds the residual distributional mismatch through a Wasserstein radius used by the planner. In $\mathbf{1000}$ paired Monte Carlo trials with gravity, SRP, and diffusion mismatch, $L_1$-DRAC adaptive control reduces the keep-out violation rate from $\mathbf{32.7\%}$ to $\mathbf{0.2\%}$ and the physical collision rate from $\mathbf{16.4\%}$ to zero, without actuator saturation.

items.title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation
items.summary: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.

items.title: SENSE: Semantic Neural Speech Synthesis from Brain Dynamics via Spatial Graph Encoding
items.summary: Reconstructing speech from non-invasive brain signals offers a promising pathway for restoring communication in individuals who are cognitively intact but unable to speak. Existing EEG-to-speech approaches formulate this task as acoustic reconstruction, optimizing waveform fidelity while ignoring whether the generated speech preserves high-level semantic content. In this work, we revisit this formulation and argue that EEG signals carry not only acoustic but also semantic information. We identify two key limitations of prior methods: (1) the neglect of spatial relationships between EEG electrodes, and (2) the failure to exploit the semantic structure of the N400 paradigm, where congruent and incongruent trials reflect distinct semantic processing. We propose SENSE(Semantic-EEG Neural Speech SynthEsis), which combines a graph-based EEG encoder over electrode geometry with EEG Semantic Conditioning (ESC), aligning EEG to a pretrained semantic space using only congruent trials. On the N400 dataset, SENSE consistently outperforms prior methods on both acoustic and semantic metrics, and model-internal channel attribution suggests distributed reliance on auditory, sensorimotor, and centro-parietal regions, consistent with known speech-perception neuroscience. In the unseen-subject setting, SENSE trained on only two subjects already surpasses the strongest baseline trained on all eighteen subjects in word error rate, and matches it on acoustic metrics with as few as eight subjects.

items.title: Verifier-Mediated Multi-LLM Coordination for Multi-Robot Path Planning
items.summary: Foundation models are increasingly used for high-level multi-robot task planning, yet independently generated symbolic plans can become jointly infeasible after geometric grounding because of shared spatial and temporal constraints. We study execution-aware coordination of large-language-model (LLM) planners for multi-robot navigation. We compare a centralized architecture, in which one LLM jointly reasons over the robot team, with a decentralized multi-LLM architecture in which each robot independently proposes a task plan. A geometric verifier grounds the candidate plans into robot trajectories, detects predicted inter-robot conflicts, and converts conflict information into structured feedback for targeted replanning. This verifier-mediated architecture separates semantic task reasoning from execution-level feasibility while enabling iterative coordination among LLM planners. Experiments in CARLA and on Crazyflie aerial robots evaluate coordination performance as task complexity increases and characterize the trade-offs between centralized reasoning, decentralized verifier-mediated coordination, and physical executability.

items.title: ROAM: Reinforcement Learning Optimized Adaptive Moving Target Defense for Smart Grid
items.summary: Smart grids rely on distributed phasor measurement units (PMUs) and wide-area communication networks whose data-acquisition pipelines are vulnerable to stealthy false data injection (FDI) attacks that evade conventional bad-data detection (BDD). Moving target defense (MTD) counters this exposure by continuously remapping sensor identities, but existing schemes apply static or pre-scheduled randomization and are each constrained by a single failure mode: seed-based methods are fast yet fragile to key compromise, while machine learning (ML) based prediction methods are resilient yet incur prohibitive latency. Neither adapts its randomization to live threat evidence. This paper presents ROAM, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) driven MTD framework in which a deep Q-network (DQN) agent continuously re-optimizes the sensor-to-ID mapping at the aggregation layer. At each decision step, the agent selects the deception coverage, flags the specific sensors to remap, and sets the split of the remapped sensors between seed-based and ML-prediction-based recovery, without modifying PMU hardware and while preserving IEEE C37.118 compatibility. On held-out BDD-compliant FDI scenarios across the IEEE 14-, 57-, and 118- bus systems, ROAM keeps the percentage of stealthy attacks below 3% while sustaining detection rates above 93%. Against an adaptive soft actor-critic (SAC) attacker that observes the defender's configuration, ROAM keeps stealthy attacks below 2.6% with detection above 92%. Hardware-in-the-loop testing on an OPAL-RT platform confirms real-time feasibility, with sub-18ms average shuffle execution and an average reshuffle blind window of 2.6% of the 3-s decision cycle.

items.title: Discovering Phase Space Structure in Learned Hamiltonian Systems
items.summary: Mechanics-inspired neural dynamical models improve interpretability and physical consistency, but they usually assume a known configuration space, fixed physical parameters, and deterministic prediction from a prescribed initial condition. We introduce Structured Phase Space GAN (SPS-GAN), a conditional generative model that learns structured dynamics from both Cartesian trajectories and video. SPS-GAN combines a port-Hamiltonian backbone with adversarial conditional generation, allowing conservative, dissipative, and forced systems to be represented in a single architecture. To infer latent mechanical structure from raw observations, we use a cyclic-coordinate loss that recovers both the system degrees of freedom and canonical coordinates without access to the true phase space. Experiments on simulated and real-world systems show that SPS-GAN improves trajectory accuracy over supervised dynamics baselines and video consistency over generative baselines, while consistently recovering the correct latent mechanical coordinates across observation modalities and dynamical regimes.

items.title: Lightweight Systems for Spatial Semantic Segmentation of Sound Scenes
items.summary: Spatial semantic segmentation of sound scenes (S5) jointly performs audio source separation and tagging on a multichannel audio mixture. Therefore, an S5 system can be decomposed into an audio tagging model and a separation model. The baseline S5 system in task~4 of the DCASE 2025 challenge uses M2D and ResUNet models for tagging and separation, respectively. These are large in overall size and therefore not appropriate for use in embedded devices. The main aim of this paper is to assess the performance loss in an S5 system when using lightweight tagging and separation models instead. To this end, we first compare the tagging performance of lightweight audio tagging models, namely PANNs and DyMNs, in terms of label prediction accuracy against the baseline M2D model. Secondly, we assess separation performance in terms of the scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio of the baseline ResUNet separator relative to that of a convolutional-based separator using SuDoRMRF. Finally, we combine the tagging and separation models across various configurations and assess the overall performance of the S5 system using the class-aware signal-to-distortion ratio.

items.title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification
items.summary: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.

items.title: Robust and Scalable UAV-UGV Planning for Aerial Monitoring under Energy and Precedence Constraints
items.summary: We consider planning for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) teams in aerial monitoring missions with ordering requirements on the monitoring points to be visited by the UAV. The system consists of multiple UAV-UGV teams, each comprising one UAV and one UGV. UAV energy limitations are modeled through endurance, defined as the maximum flight time on a full battery. The UGVs serve as mobile charging stations and transport the UAVs between consecutive aerial tours. Given a set of monitoring points subject to ordering constraints and the teams' initial and terminal positions, the objective is to minimize mission completion time while satisfying UAV energy limits and the required visit order under bounded travel-time disturbances that may arise during execution. Unlike prior work, the plan jointly determines vehicle routes and their timing, allowing teams to slow down as needed to satisfy the ordering constraints. We develop a polynomial-time algorithm that generates efficient solutions to the underlying NP-hard planning problem. We establish feasibility guarantees, characterize the algorithm's computational complexity, and evaluate its performance via numerical comparisons.

items.title: Mode 0: Architecture, Risk Taxonomy, and Standardization Pathway for RCU-Assisted V2X Safety Communication
items.summary: The 3GPP V2X resource allocation framework offers two entity classes for coordinating vehicle communication --- base-station scheduling and autonomous vehicle selection --- a design space we show to be structurally incomplete for safety-critical coordination. We propose Mode 0, a third entity class centered on the Roadside Computing Unit (RCU): infrastructure integrating elevated sensing, sidelink communication, and local computation, owned by traffic management authorities rather than network operators. We formalize Mode 0's subfamily taxonomy (Mode 0a through 0c), its traffic risk taxonomy and mandatory-escalation boundary, its cross-domain coexistence with Modes 1--4, and its standardization pathway.
